title: Chicago Bears Deemed Potential Trade Landing Spot for 2 Arizona Cardinals Pro Bowlers
full_text:
The Chicago Bears should be one of the most aggressive teams in the NFL ahead of the trade deadline on Nov. 10.
If we've learned anything over these first six games, it's that the Bears look like contenders at 4-2. Caleb Williams is on track to take the step forward we thought he would in 2026 and the defense has been better than expected.
But the defense has also had some injury woes dating back to the offseason, when the team lost starting safety Coby Bryant . More recently, edge rusher Dayo Odeyingbo went on the shelf due to injury, and Chicago also lost Montez Sweat to a suspension .
All three of those issues are a stark reminder of just how quickly things can change at any given position, and that's why the Bears should stop at nothing to continue adding to the roster, and more specifically, to the defensive side of the ball.
In an article naming trade candidates , Sports Illustrated's Matt Verderame mentions Arizona Cardinals safety Budda Baker and edge rusher Josh Sweat, both of whom are former Pro Bowlers.
Verderame then goes on to call the Bears potential fits for both players.
"Baker is not the typical veteran acquisition. He’s an eight-time Pro Bowler and a two-time first-team All-Pro who has been incredibly durable and productive. This year, Baker already has 3.5 sacks and three passes defensed with an interception. Signed through 2027 with a $16 million base salary next year, Baker won’t come cheap. But with his past and present production, he might be the best player on the market," Verderame said. "Potential fits: Bills, Bears."
"For the Cardinals to trade Sweat less than two seasons into his four-year deal, they would likely need significant draft capital. That might be tough for a team to give up, considering he’s getting paid a prorated figure of $9.7 million before $17 million each of the next two years, albeit nonguaranteed. Last year, Sweat notched 12 sacks but is off to a slow start this season with two sacks in six games," Verderame added. "Potential fits: Bears, Lions."
Sweat is the more logical addition between the two.
Montez Sweat has been a disappointment so far this season with just two sacks, and while Odeyingbo has been better than anyone thought he would be with three sacks, his injury issues since last season are a concern and the Bears can't depend on Odeyingbo to continue playing at the level he has when he returns.
Josh Sweat is indeed off to a slow start this season with two sacks, but his history of production gives us confidence he'll rebound in a better situation.
Sweat has posted 7.5 sacks or more in four of the last five years, and he has twice posted double-digit sacks in that span, with 12 last season and 11 in 2022. He would be a massive upgrade for Chicago and is someone general manager Ryan Poles should focus on trying to acquire.
At safety, the Bears aren't in a great spot. Hopefully Bryant will be back at some point, but that may not be until December , at the earliest. Dillon Thieneman and Cam Lewis have played well this season, but a single injury to either one would leave Chicago in a precarious situation at the position, so more depth is needed.
Baker has been one of the better safeties in the league over the course of his career, with his eight Pro Bowls and four All-Pro selections proving that.
The veteran safety is better in the box than back deep, but that's no issue because Thieneman and Lewis can play free safety. Baker is an elite pass-rusher at the position, as evidenced by his four sacks this season, and he is also a very good run defender.
We project Sweat will cost at least a third-round pick, but it would be well worth it for the kind of upgrade he can provide to one of the most important positions on the football field.
Baker probably ends up costing about a fourth-round pick, so the Bears wouldn't exactly have to break the bank to acquire him.
Softening the blow of giving up that kind of draft capital is the fact that both players are under contract beyond this season, so they won't simply be rentals.
Chicago is in good shape with its draft capital, with the team having a pick in each round for the next three years.
With legitimate Super Bowl aspirations, we wouldn't mind seeing the Bears spring for both players, although if they have to choose just one, we're taking Sweat over Baker.
Mike Moraitis is a freelance writer who has covered the NFL for major outlets such as Sports Illustrated and The Sporting News. He has previously written for USA TODAY Sports Media Group and FanSided, and got his start in sports media at Bleacher Report.

title: Should the Bears Start Luke Newman or Jordan McFadden in Place of Jonah Jackson?
full_text:
Many feared the worst when Bears right guard Jonah Jackson went down with a hip injury in the team's Week 6 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
The 29-year-old might not get as much credit as Joe Thuney or Darnell Wright, but he's a Pro Bowl-caliber player (and legitimate road-grader) in his own right. He was immediately listed as doubtful to return, which struck fear in the hearts of the fanbase.
However, the Bears appear to have dodged a bullet with Jackson's injury timeline. ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reports the star right guard is week-to-week with a hip flexor injury.
He'll obviously miss Thursday night's clash against New England, but could have an outside chance to play (thanks to an 11-day break) for the team's Week 8 Monday night matchup with the Seahawks.
Jackson's injury will certainly hurt in the short term. To their credit, the Bears have quality interior depth that will let them survive the loss, though.
Luke Newman took over for Jackson against Atlanta, and he held his own against Atlanta's aggressive defensive front. You could make a strong case that he's not the strongest candidate to take over the job in the meantime, though.
If Jordan McFadden's name rings a bell, you probably remember him starting at left guard in the Divisional Round matchup against the Rams last season. It was a shocking decision at the time, as the Bears moved LG Joe Thuney to left tackle for an injured Ozzy Trapilo.
They felt better about having McFadden, who played two regular-season snaps and spent much of the year on the practice squad, in the lineup over Theo Benedet, who started eight games at left tackle. While Jared Verse's presence surely played a role in the decision, the Rams' interior defensive line was also far from permeable.
McFadden promptly made them look smart for showing confidence in him, too. The Bears might've left with a disappointing 20-17 loss, but their offense looked the part despite the frigid defeat. They put up 417 yards and averaged 5.1 yards per play. The former practice squad guard didn't look out of place, either.
The Bears saw enough from McFadden to reward him with a one-year extension (despite already having quality depth along the line) this offseason. They clearly liked what he put on tape.
Sure, Newman played well against the Falcons. He'd probably do the same against the Patriots' defensive front (although Milton Williams' speed could give him trouble).
However, McFadden already proved he can hold his own in a tougher test, and that's exactly what the Bears will have if Jackson isn't ready by the time they take on Seattle. He should get the first crack at the starting job for however long Jackson is out of action.

Nevertheless, he still Bears Down!

title: Bears NFL Power Rankings For Week 7: Williams, Gordon Propel Chicago Into Top 10
full_text:
My, what a difference two players can make, something we saw in the Chicago Bears' Week 6 win over the Atlanta Falcons.
The Bears welcomed back Caleb Williams and Kyler Gordon on Sunday, and both made massive impacts in their respective returns to the field.
Williams completed 30-of-36 passes for 305 yards and one score, and Gordon was an absolute menace in his own right with three sacks and two forced fumbles while playing just 17 snaps.
Thanks to their performances, the Bears notched a victory and are now moving up in the NFL power rankings of experts for Week 7, going as high as into the top five of one expert's rankings.
Ranking: 5 | Last week: 13
This is the biggest leap up for the Bears in our power rankings round-up.
Orr rightly points out just how massive of a difference it made for the Bears to have Caleb Williams and Kyler Gordon back.
"Caleb Williams's return was spectacular. But so, too, was bringing Kyler Gordon back into this defense as a no-nonsense nickel blitzer that will make Chicago not only the most fun offense to watch in the NFL, but one of the most unpredictable and enjoyable defenses as well," Orr said.
Ranking: 4 | Last week: 10
Davis gets cute here and talks about the impact of "getting a key guy back," but mentions Kyler Gordon only, not Caleb Williams.
"They looked awfully good after getting a key guy back … and we're referring to DB Kyler Gordon, who had three sacks − again, he's a DB − and two forced fumbles in his 2026 debut on Sunday, all in 17 snaps. He's the first player at his position to have such a game in 26 years," Davis said.
We know Davis is trying to be funny and Gordon deserves a ton of credit for what was a historic performance in 17 snaps, but let's not forget the offense looking vastly better upon the return of QB1, who was sensational.
Ranking: 9 | Last week: 13
ESPN's Courtney Cronin was asked to list the biggest issue on the offensive side of the ball right now and she picked penalties, which is certainly a logical choice.
Chicago had 12 penalties on Sunday, including eight in the first half alone, and a lot of them were holding flags.
"One area that can stand to be cleaned up more is offensive penalties, which accounted for seven of the Bears' infractions Sunday. Those offensive penalties helped generate Chicago's most penalty yardage in a game since 2016 (133). The Bears are currently tied for the third-most offensive holding penalties (10). That's an area they'll want to fix so it doesn't derail drives," she said.
Another issue on offense is the absence of Kyle Monangai. Sure, Roschon Johnson played pretty well, but he also had a costly fumble and he just isn't as good as Monangai.
Unfortunately, the second-year back is headed toward sitting out again after he was an estimated non-participant on Monday. A short week will make it difficult for him to get back.
Ranking: 13 | Last week: 15
The Bears are still climbing their way out of the hole they landed in with Prisco after the abysmal Week 5 showing against the Green Bay Packers, with this being the lowest ranking in our round-up.
"Bouncing back from the loss to the Packers by winning on the road at Atlanta is a good look for this team," Prisco said. "Of course it helps to have Caleb Williams back."
In the three games the Bears have had Williams on the field in 2026, they've dropped 30 or more points in two of them. Not that it needed to be said, but this is a very different offense when he's under center.

title: Bengals Get Encouraging Injury News on Key Playmaker Ahead of Ravens Game
full_text:
Every game is important in the NFL. However, the Cincinnati Bengals are preparing for a massive Week 7 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens.
The AFC North is one of the most competitive divisions in the league. A loss for the Bengals would move the team to 0-2 in the division and would also keep them in last place. It's all hands on deck for the Bengals this week, and it felt that way with Zac Taylor's comments to the media on Monday.
As the Bengals deal with a banged-up wide receiver room, Taylor revealed a positive update on rookie wide receiver Colbie Young, who could make an impact for the team on Sunday.
"He's looked as good as he's looked in a long time," Taylor said. "I think last week he had a good week on what he could handle from a rehab perspective. So this week to get him back involved, he looked good running around today. I think it's good to finally get him back and feel like he's closer to 100% health."
The 2026 fourth round pick suffered a knee injury in just his third game of his NFL career. In his short time on the field, Young has two receptions for the Bengals.
If Young is looking as good as Taylor says he is, the rookie wide receiver has a massive chance to stake his claim for the third option in a crowded room.
Andrei Iosivas is still dealing with a thumb injury, meaning Young could get a lot of snaps as the team's third option at wideout this Sunday.
The injury to Iosivas has been brutal for a receiver who is still looking to make his name for the Bengals. But after a strong camp from Young, it feels like Iosivas may soon run out of opportunities to make his name with the franchise.
The Week 7 matchup with the Ravens could be the one that leads to the Bengals finding another reliable offensive weapon.
Quarterback Joe Burrow and this Bengals offense aren't going to hide their strength. The pass game is going to be on full display. Can Young make his presence known?
It feels strange to say so early in his career, but if Young is ready to go, this could be a career-defining game for the young receiver.

title: Film Breakdown Reveals Why the Bengals Struggle to Stop This Type of Run
full_text:
The Bengals defense has improved when comparing this season to last year. They have gone from about 29 points per game to about 22 points per game. That takes them from 30th to about 14th so far this season. However, they have a very clear issue on defense and it’s something that has plagued them for a few years now. They struggle heavily against perimeter runs.
The Bengals run defense has generally been pretty good this season. They’re actually ranked 4th in FTN’s DVOA ranking for run defense. On all runs, the Bengals are allowing 4.5 yards per carry, a 38.5% success rate, 16.4% explosive play rate, and -0.04 EPA per play. However, all of those numbers spike when it comes to perimeter runs. Against perimeter runs, the Bengals are allowing 6.4 yards per carry, a 46.4% success rate, 32.1% explosive play rate, and +0.17 EPA per play.
These perimeter runs have also been a great way to attack the Bengals defense with Dexter Lawrence on the field. With Lawrence on the field, the Bengals run defense is allowing 3.7 yards per carry, a 34.2% success rate, 13.5% explosive play rate, and -0.06 EPA per play. Against perimeter runs those numbers once again sky rocket. The Bengals defense gives up 5.1 yards per carry, 37.5% success rate, 22.2% explosive play rate, and +0.08 EPA per play.
Not only are those numbers abysmal, but teams keep attempting more perimeter runs against the Bengals now that they can recognize this as a weakness.
In Weeks 1 and 2, the Bengals faced a combined eight perimeter runs. They faced six perimeter runs in both Week 3 and Week 4. They faced eight perimeter runs in Week 5. That’s 20 of the 28 perimeter runs in the last three games and there is no reason to think that it’s going to slow down any time soon.
There’s not a simple easy solution for these struggles and there’s also not just one finger to point. There are multiple issues for the Bengals when it comes to their struggles against the perimeter run game.
pic.twitter.com/XfEvCfP2SP
On this play alone, there are a plethora of issues present. The issues start with the play side end (Boye Mafe) who gets pinned by the Y. The next issue is that the nickel (Dax Hill) gets pinned and driven downfield by the F. The next problem comes from the 20 backer (Barrett Carter) who runs himself out of the play by going underneath the block from the center rather than fighting and getting over that block. With all 3 of those support players forced inside and underneath, the force from DJ Ivey is useless. The post safety (Jordan Battle) is the only player left who can make this stop.
Here is a comparison with a surprisingly good perimeter run defense in the Falcons.
pic.twitter.com/faOuFpZqsJ
The play side end fights to get over the block from the Y, the 40 backer flows over that block and takes out both the puller and the fullback, and the strong side safety avoids the block from the wide receiver before making the stop.
pic.twitter.com/lQmh8eyKhu
This time the Bengals are facing a reverse with a false pull. The first issue is that the playside end (Cashius Howell) does not get himself into position to make the play. Carter is in a 60 position over the Y and actually reads this out pretty quickly but he is physically manhandled by Aaron Brewer and pancaked.
Jordan Battle is the near safety on the play but he takes himself out of the play by going inside and underneath of the block from the backside guard. If he could fight over that block and force this further inside, then both Bryan Cook and Hill are in position to make the play. Cook still has an attempt but he is unable to bring down the ball carrier and the play ends up being an easy chunk play for the Dolphins.
Here is a comparison with one of the best perimeter run defenses in the league in the Texans:
pic.twitter.com/FdbCmIrljv
Watch how Will Anderson Jr. makes this play on his own as the playside end. Anderson has incredible processing to recognize this as an end around and he cuts it off by getting penetration.
pic.twitter.com/jiufBBy7Mm
This is just a jet sweep but the Bengals get caught in a nickel B gap blitz. This takes out one of the support players who could help make a stop here but there’s still unsound play from the other defenders. Both the playside end and the nickel could possibly make this play but the backer is unable to get over or defeat the block from the Texans X wide receiver. The corner then gives a very weak tackle which allows the ball carrier to pick up about seven additional yards.
The Bengals defense is going to need to be better against these runs. They need to play team football to do so. Working over the top of blocks won’t give a player stats but it will funnel the ball to his teammates. Right now a majority of the Bengals defenders try to go underneath those blocks to make a superhero play. They aren’t making that play and instead they’re stopping anyone from making that play. Additionally, all of the Bengals defensive ends need to do a better job. Whether that’s as the backside contain player for end arounds or the playside end on crack toss, they need to get themselves in position to make plays more difficult for opponents. Lastly, the nickel needs to be better against F tight end and slot wide receiver blocks. The best defenses in the league have a nickel who is willing to fight blocks. Through five weeks, the same cannot be said about this Bengals defense.
The good news is that these are all mental and technical issues which means they are fixable to some degree. It’s absolutely possible that they come out after the bye as a sound, team defense against these runs. The coaching staff is certainly going to make it a point of emphasis as they have alluded to the fact that they are struggling in this area. It has to improve on Sunday against the Ravens.

title: Bengals Should Buy Low, Trade For New York Giants Running Back to Enhance Offensive Depth
full_text:
The Bengals need to solidify their running back room entering the home stretch of the 2026 season, and a recently embattled young rusher could be the right answer.
Cincinnati may be able to trade for Giants running back Cam Skattebo after he seemingly entered head coach John Harbaugh's doghouse this month.
Skattebo has 81 carries for 291 yards and a score this season, but he played just six snaps on Sunday after being at 34-plus in every game this season.
"You can say, well, I don't like that. I don't like you divvying up the snaps between four backs. And I can tell you, I don't like it either," Harbaugh said about the snap drop for Skattebo on Sunday. "One of those guys needs to step up. Somebody needs to step up and be the back.
"And none of those guys have done that yet. And when one of those guys steps up to be the back, then they'll be the back. That's your answer. And that's as honest as I can be about it. And they know that, too. And believe me, they're all hungry. They want to step up. One of those guys wants to step up. Somebody's going to step up and take that job. We're going to see who it is."
New York has three running backs (Najee Harris cut on Tuesday) vying for snaps on its roster right now and clearly isn't 100% bought in on Skattebo leading the room.
The 2025 fourth-round draft pick might be had for a low-value Day 3 pick in next year's draft, unlike some more expensive RB options out there, and he's flashed some great running before.
Skattebo has just a 55.4 Pro Football Focus grade this season and won't bring anything as a pass blocker (36 pass-blocking grade on 25 snaps this season), but he ran really well last year en route to an 80.5 overall grade.
The 24-year-old should have plenty of tread left on his tires and could spur Chase Brown to more impactful moments down the stretch of his contract season. Skattebo is under contract through the 2028 season and carries just a $1.79 million cap hit for the rest of this season and next.
Cincinnati should take a flier on Skattebo with one of its eight 2027 draft picks (one third-round compensation pick slated for them along with seven other normal picks).
Brown could bounce back and thrive in the final months of the season like he did last year, but it shouldn't cost much to get this insurance just in case that doesn't happen. Cincinnati has a few weeks to mull options before the trade deadline on Nov. 10 at 4 p.m. ET.

title: Bengals Fill 53-Man Roster Entering Ravens Matchup, Add LB to Practice Squad
full_text:
The Bengals made a couple of back-end roster moves on Tuesday. Cincinnati announced practice squad shuffling, with safety Russ Yeast signed to the active roster.
On the practice squad, Cincinnati released safety Isaiah Nwokobia and signed tight end Josh Kattus. The latter had been with the team this summer and went unsigned to start the season.
They also added a linebacker to the practice squad in Emany Johnson, who spent time with Dallas in 2024. He tallied his rookie season on the practice squads of the Cowboys and L.A. Chargers. Johnson played the entire 2025 campaign on the Chargers’ practice squad. He did not suit up for any team in practice or on the playing field to start this season.
Johnson notched a 49.8 defensive Pro Football Focus grade on 86 preseason snaps this year and a 74.5 grade on 149 snaps last year.
It's a minor shakeup for a pretty locked-in roster entering Week 7. Cincinnati should be getting Jalen Davis and Andrei Iosivas back from injured reserve in the coming weeks, while the only injury to monitor is a week-to-week Kyle Dugger (quad).
The pass-catching group has to pick up a little more slack without depth tight end Tanner Hudson for the rest of the season. He's out for months with a torn pec.
"I think we'll call on the whole room in the receiver room. We're getting healthy at the receiver room too, so I think just combining both those rooms and dispersing how those roles will play out is something we're always open to week to week," Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said on Monday. "We feel like we've got a lot of people with a lot of different strengths that can all play at a high level in both those rooms, and just finding ways to game plan for those guys, get them involved, is important for us."
Cincinnati has Tuesday off before returning to practice on Wednesday, Thursday and Friday. They are in a tight AFC North race with a massive road game on deck under the sun in Baltimore this weekend.
That contest kicks off at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday.

title: Blockbuster Trade Idea Gives Bengals Final Piece on Offense
full_text:
Week 6 of the NFL offered more clarity on who could compete for the playoffs this season. After Sunday's conclusion, almost half of the AFC have a record of .500 or worse, including the Indianapolis Colts, who lost to the formerly 0-5 Titans. This led the Colts to fire general manager Chris Ballard and sparked speculation that they could offload veteran talent as they sit at 2-4.
This should prompt the Bengals to strike a deal with the Colts for a difference-maker in Jonathan Taylor to bolster their run game and remain competitive in the AFC North.
Taylor would immediately skyrocket the Bengals running back room to the stratosphere, as the unit has dramatically underwhelmed to start the season.
Taylor has routinely excelled on runs from under center throughout his career. This season he has averaged 4.4 yards per carry when under center compared to 3.4 yards per carry out of shotgun. He would allow Zac Taylor and the offense to continue building their offense from under center.
While his total 3.9 YPC this season may cause some to worry, the situation with the Colts is much different than it would be in Cincinnati . Daniel Jones and the Indianapolis receivers are less than half of what Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins are. Because the passing game poses little threat, opposing defenses have focused heavily on stacking the box to stop Taylor. That focus intensified last week when the Colts lost to the Steelers, who stopped Taylor by stacking the box with eight defenders on 80% of his runs.
With Chase and Higgins at receiver, and given Burrow's ability to dissect defenses, Taylor would arguably have the most open space of his career if he lands with the Bengals.
Taylor has maintained his dominant level of play through six games this season despite his lower numbers and is currently on pace for 1,394 rushing yards and 20 touchdowns. Adding that level of talent to a running back unit that has consistently handicapped the offense in the Burrow era would add another dynamic layer to an already dangerous offense.
Acquiring Taylor would require trading away a premium asset and more, as the closest comparison is likely what the 49ers gave up to acquire Christian McCaffrey from the Panthers in 2022. The 49ers traded a second, third, and fourth-round pick in the 2023 draft, along with a 2024 fifth-round pick, to get McCaffrey.
That is the ceiling on what Taylor's cost likely is. The realistic package for him would likely be somewhere in the middle in the form of a 2027 second-round pick, along with a Day 3 pick. He signed a two-year, $44 million extension before the season; however, the Bengals would only pay his remaining $6.98 million in base salary and incentives this season, since the Colts have already paid his signing bonus.
What could make a hypothetical deal more interesting is what the Bengals can offer alongside draft compensation compared to other teams. The team could make negotiations with Indianapolis more interesting by including underutilized players in the deal, such as Shemar Stewart.
Stewart's played just 17 snaps over the first six weeks of the season. He is a former first-round pick, and those players typically command solid compensation, as the Cardinals got a second- and sixth-round pick for Marvin Harrison Jr.
Including Stewart in a deal for Taylor could shrink the draft assets the Bengals give up.
Acquiring Taylor is a move the front office must consider after they acquired Dexter Lawrence in a blockbuster deal to transform the defense this offseason. Six months later, they have another chance to add a proven superstar to the team. The trade deadline is in three weeks on November 10th at 4 PM EST.

title: Revenge Game? Orlando Brown Jr. Weighs In on Bengals Facing Trey Hendrickson
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals are gearing up for a very important early season game against the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday.
Not only is this game a massive meeting for AFC North supremacy, but it's also the first time the Bengals will face former defensive end Trey Hendrickson.
Hendrickson moved on from the Bengals and joined one of the three teams this fan base would have preferred he not sign with. The former Bengals star may have a pep in his step when he takes the field in Week 7.
On Monday, Ben Baby spoke with Orlando Brown Jr. about the matchup with his former teammate. The Bengals are definitely expecting more spark from their former teammate.
"Just the way things ended here, from a personal and player perspective, I get it. I've been in that position before as well," Brown said when asked if Hendrickson would have extra motivation on Sunday. "I imagine he will have a little something extra to play for."
Brown also went on to say that he expects Hendrickson's best on Sunday because every time he has went up against the former Bengals star, he has gotten his best.
Hendrickson has missed two games this season with the Ravens, but returned on Sunday in the team's 13-10 loss to the Cleveland Browns in Week 6.
The Ravens pass rusher earned his second sack of the season against the Browns. Hendrickson has been dealing with issues with his finger after having a surgery, but it seems like there's no chance in this world he will miss the opportunity to go after Joe Burrow this week.
"He's a good player," Bengals head coach Zac Taylor said. "They got a lot of good players on their defense and we got to put together a great plan and be able to execute it to give ourselves the best chance to win."
Bragging rights will be on the line Sunday, but there's more than that at stake. With the bye week, the Bengals fell to last place in the AFC North at 3-2, while the other teams are 4-2. A win on Sunday will put the Bengals back in a good spot in the division race. A loss means the Bengals will move to 0-2 in the division, putting them a lot further behind than they would like.
The talk leading up to this game will be about Hendrickson, and rightfully so. All four of his Pro Bowl selections and his First-Team All-Pro honors came with the Bengals. But even he knows this game is more than earning bragging rights over his former home. This game has major postseason ties to it. The Bengals will need to bring their A game.

title: Zac Taylor Sets Injury Table Following 2026 Bye Week, First Ravens Matchup Next
full_text:
The Bengals returned to practice Monday afternoon after the 2026 bye week. Zac Taylor spoke with the media following that session and gave the latest health update on his team.
Beyond the injured reserve list, Cincinnati looks pretty healthy as it enters a break-less stretch of the 2026-27 regular season. Just about every player on the 53-man roster reportedly got some type of work in on Monday. Cashius Howell (sick) was the only notable absence.
"I think he's progressing along, and so we'll kind of see where he's at," Taylor said about Kyle Dugger (quad), who entered the bye week-to-week. He also confirmed Howell missed today's session due to sickness.
Cincinnati is entering its most important game week of the season against Baltimore. The AFC North standing margins are razor-thin right now, with every team holding at least three wins and two losses.
The Bengals already lost a frustrating game against Pittsburgh; starting 0-2 in the division would be a tough hole to climb out of.
"It's exciting. I think our guys are really get fired up for this game. Not that they don't get fired up for every game, but every point in Baltimore in a divisional game is a fun one to get out for, and our guys will be up for it," Taylor said.
Cincinnati will have to replace Tanner Hudson as a key member of its pass-catching depth. It may be showtime for 2026 seventh-round pick Jack Endries (one offensive snap this season) or just added burden on the other parts of the TE room.
"He's Mr. Dependable, whether he's on the practice squad, whether he's on the roster; he's going to show up," Taylor said about Hudson this season. "He's been who we thought he was. Tanner shows up and makes plays, never complains. Erick (All) goes down for a play; he's in. Mike (Gesicki) goes down for a play; he's in. He knows them all; he can play them all. I just need the defense to decide who he is, so we know if we're going to get base or nickel when he's in there."
Cincinnati has Tuesday off before three straight practice days this week.

title: Latest AFC North Projections Favor Bengals Ahead of Ravens Showdown
full_text:
The Bengals have emerged as the projected AFC North favorites entering Week 7 after the Browns pulled off a massive upset win over the Ravens on Sunday. The Bengals are the favorite to win the division at 40.7%, while the Ravens' chances dropped to 39.2% according to ESPN analytics.
The Steelers have a 15% chance to win the division and the Browns have a 5.1% chance, despite being 4-2 on the season.
The Bengals now face a crucial three-game stretch, with a chance to win in Baltimore this week. Should they beat the Ravens, they then face the Titans before traveling to Madrid to play the Falcons in Week 9.
Given the current state of all those teams and the Bengals having had time to get healthy over their bye week, they could realistically go 3-0 this stretch. The Browns and Steelers play each other in Week 8, while the Ravens go on to play the Bills in Buffalo and welcome the Jaguars to Baltimore in Week 9.
If the Bengals handle business against the Ravens, they could enter Week 10 with a 6-2 record. That would set up a game that could ulitimately decide the winner of the division against the Steelers on Sunday Night Football.
Pittsburgh could enter that game with a 6-2 record as well, with a game against the Saints next week, with the clash with the Browns after.
The toughest opponent in the division for the Bengals remains the Ravens even after they fell to the Browns. Baltimore has been without Lamar Jackson for the last two weeks, and all signs point to his return this week when Joe Burrow and company travel to Baltimore.
Regardless of the Browns' and Steelers' current records, the Ravens have the most potential to threaten the Bengals. Jackson has only lost to the Bengals three times in his career, with 11 total victories. Derrick Henry, meanwhile, has run all over the Bengals during his time with the Ravens, with 320 rushing yards and three touchdowns over four meetings.
If the Bengals are going to compete this season, they have to at least show they can slow down Jackson and Henry. Adding Dexter Lawrence this offseason should help, as he should have as big an impact in this upcoming game as he has at any point this season so far.
Should they successfully defeat Baltimore and stop Henry and Jackson, the momentum they would carry into the next two weeks would be massive.
Sinking the Ravens to a 4-3 record, while defeating them in their own stadium, should set the team up for a great run in November and December. That, in turn, could be the turning point that helps the team regain the AFC North crown and make a deep playoff run.

title: Bengals' Meeting With Ravens Gets Even Bigger After a Chaotic Week 6
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals had Week 6 off, but that didn't stop the rest of the AFC North from creating absolute chaos.
The Pittsburgh Steelers took an overtime victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, while the Cleveland Browns shocked the Baltimore Ravens with a last second field goal. We live in a world where the Browns lead the AFC North at 4-2, with the Ravens and Steelers also at 4-2, and the Bengals still at 3-2, placing them last.
Yes, the Bengals may be last in the division heading into Week 7, but the outcome of the Browns-Ravens game was exactly what Bengals fans should have been rooting for, and one that makes the Week 7 matchup even more important.
The Bengals are getting the chance to come into a physical divisional contest fresh, due to the bye week. They will also have the chance to get ahead of the Ravens in the division with a win.
After stumbling in their first division game this season against the Steelers, this meeting with the Ravens was already massive. Now, the Bengals have a chance to put the Ravens behind them in the standings, just before they take on a Tennessee Titans team that just picked up its first win.
Coming out of the bye week on the right foot would be huge for this team's playoff implications. It also could be the start of a winning streak that will keep the rest of the division on their toes.
Getting a victory in the AFC North is never easy. It's been especially difficult for the Bengals when they've played the Ravens in recent years.
The Bengals are 1-5 in the last three years in the regular season against the Ravens. Want to change the thinking around the league about your team? Then you have to beat the Ravens.
It's not the Bengals who are facing an injury at quarterback when these two teams meet on Sunday. (Knock on wood)
Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson has missed the team's last two games after suffering an ankle sprain in the team's Week 4 win over the Titans.
Obviously, Jackson potentially being out is a huge impact on how this game could shake out. But something tells me the Bengals are going to planning for the former MVP to be on the field this Sunday.
The opportunity is here. Are the Bengals capable of answering the Challenge?

title: What I'm Buying and Selling About the Cleveland Browns After Week 6
full_text:
It’s hard not to feel good about the Cleveland Browns’ 4-2 start to the season, including wins over divisional rivals Pittsburgh Steelers and Baltimore Ravens so far in 2026.
After all, this is the team with the lowest winning percentage in all the NFL (.346) since it grew to 32 teams divided in eight divisions back in 2002, and the longest active drought without a division title league-wide (36 years and counting). Winning just isn’t a common occurrence here.
But even as the Browns face a very accessible schedule with just one remaining out of division foe with a winning mark, not everything has been smooth sailing for the franchise. Here are three things I’m buying and three things I’m selling from the Browns after Week 6 of the 2026 regular season.
The Browns began their regular season getting their teeth kicked in by the Jaguars on Opening Weekend. Since then, this unit has been one of the best in all the NFL. Cleveland is currently ranked second in the league in sacks in their first year without Myles Garrett and zero sacks by his nominal successor Jared Verse, and fourth in total quarterback pressures. Cleveland has also surrendered just one rushing touchdown all year long.
Granted, there are still some issues that need to be resolved, mainly in the secondary, but this unit is going places. Denzel Ward is enjoying one of his finest seasons as a pro, Carson Schwesinger is proving to be the real deal in his second season, and free agent addition Quincy Williams has been playing a very high level of football, too. The D-Line has been the team’s best group, nonetheless. Isaiah McGuire and Maliek Collins have been phenomenal, while Mason Graham has been living up to his billing when healthy. Sam Williams has also flashed on the edge, and Verse is getting the pressures, if not the sacks.
The Browns went all-in on Watson and, so far, there are reasons to be skeptical about his performance so far. His 4.0 percent touchdown percentage is his second worst as a pro, and his numbers across a few other metrics line up exactly to what he’s done before in Cleveland, very distant to what he did before in Houston, including QBR, success rate, yards per attempt, and sack percentage, while his 70.3 on target rate is his personal worst.
So no, Watson isn’t playing better under head coach Todd Monken than what he did under Kevin Stefanski, in any sense. He’s just being backed by a much better defense and has some top notch weapons at his disposal in the ground game, along with a trust-worthy placekicker in Andre Szmyt.
The Browns are winning despite Watson , and that means they can’t change quarterbacks now, but things are likely to get rocky at some point ahead.
Playing on an island on the left side is inherently more difficult than playing guard but make no mistake, Austin Barber has been as good if not better than Spencer Fano for the Browns. Either way, both are outplaying their respective counterparts in veteran left guard Zion Johnson and especially veteran right tackle Tytus Howard, so far.
There’s still a ton of improvement to be made here, and blocking for a quarterback that’s been responsible for a number of sacks is suboptimal, but expect these two to become cornerstones in Cleveland for the long run.
The team as a whole has been struggling mightily in the ground game , no doubt. But Judkins’ woes should come as no surprise when you take a good look at his rookie season.
He’s averaging 3.0 yards-per-rush this year, which is actually worse than his 3.5 yards-per-rush average from a year ago, and hasn’t been able to reach a 4.0 yard-per-carry average since Week 13 of last year, one of only four games all year long he was able to reach or surpass that number. And this year, he’s scored just once despite receiving the lion’s share in snaps on offense (60 percent, compared to 50 percent last year).
Run blocking has been a problem for the Browns, especially in terms of first contact for the backs, but Judkins’ numbers are worse off than last year’s underwhelming stats, neatly disguised by his seven rushing scores as a rookie.
If the rookie offensive linemen have been a hit for the Browns, the rookie wideouts have been even better.
KC Concepcion recovered from a concussion in time to play this past Sunday for the Browns, and he’s still leading the team with 22 catches for 186 yards. Meanwhile, Denzel Boston has 17 catches for 345 yards and a league-leading 20.3 yard per reception average to go along with his three scores.
Yes, the numbers for both could be better by this point, but they truly don’t have much to work with at the quarterback position. Even so, Boston should be seriously considered among the league favorites to take home the Offensive Rookie of the Year Award.
Currently, Cleveland is using play-action at a 18.5 percent rate -- 29th in the NFL -- down from 21.9 percent last year. The team’s EPA per pass attempt is at -0.04, meaning the Browns are faking handoffs at a very low rate, and are not a successful team at passing the ball when they do fake the handoff.
Again, the offensive line has had some protection issues and Watson is not playing good football right now, but a solid ground game would probably earn more respect from the defenses than what’s currently going on. Plus, play-action is known as a good countermeasure to pressure, which would be a good development for a team leading the league in sacks allowed .
Rafael brings more than two decades worth of experience writing all things football.

title: Could Browns’ Carson Schwesinger Enter the Defensive Player of the Year Race?
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns’ reigning Defensive Rookie of the Year , Carson Schwesinger, continues to impress.
In the Browns' Week 6 matchup against division rival Baltimore, Carson Schwesinger was the X factor in the team's win. Despite entering the game listed as questionable with an ankle sprain, Schwesinger recorded 13 tackles. Most importantly, Schwesinger forced running back Derrick Henry to fumble , setting up Cleveland’s game-tying touchdown.
DROY Carson Schwesinger forces the fumble on Derrick Henry! BALvsCLE on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/TY9niNw746
The performance against the Ravens is not a one-off, either. Schwesinger has 56 total tackles through six games.  That averages 9.3 tackles per game, approximately matching Luke Kuechly’s career average. Maintaining that pace over a full 17-game season would put Schwesinger at roughly 159 tackles. Schwesinger has also added quarterback pressure, recording a strip-sack in the Browns’ Week 5 matchup against the Jets.
Carson FLYING in to knock it loose! #CLEvsNYJ on CBS pic.twitter.com/9HFah8X33w
While Schwesinger has been impressive throughout the 2026 season and has largely picked up where he left off in 2025 , his recent two-week stretch of 21 tackles, two forced fumbles, and a sack may strengthen his case for another individual honor.
Schwesinger already emerged in 2025 as one of the league's best defenders , but his recent production, despite injury, may put him in the Defensive Player of the Year conversation. Schwesinger has been nothing short of elite in the middle of the Browns’ defense over the last few weeks. If Schwesinger can keep playing at this level, even with a bad ankle, the illustrious Defensive Player of the Year award could be within reach.
History isn't exactly on Schwesinger's side, as pass rushers dominate the award.  Luke Kuechly was the last off-ball linebacker to win Defensive Player of the Year, earning the honor in 2013, when he played in all 16 games and recorded two sacks, four interceptions, and 156 combined tackles. Notably, Kuechly won the award in his second NFL season, the same stage of his career that Schwesinger has reached.
Jared Verse on Carson Schwesinger: “He has an old school linebacker mindset … He’s a hooper … He’s the most reliable person I know.” #browns pic.twitter.com/KoXZaGwh8H
Patrick Surtain II is the most recent non-edge defender to win the award, winning it in 2024 with 45 combined tackles, four interceptions, and 11 passes defended. Recent voting trends favor pass rushers like current betting favorite Will Anderson Jr., making it a tougher path for Schwesinger as an off-ball linebacker.
However, if Carson Schwesinger stays healthy and sustains his recent elite play, he could give the Luke Kuechly comparisons even more weight. Like Kuechly, Schwesinger could follow a Defensive Rookie of the Year campaign by claiming the NFL’s top defensive honor in his second season.
Noah Olson is a Northeast Ohio native and lifelong Cleveland sports fan. He graduated from The College of Wooster with a major in Communications and has been sports writing since 2024. As a writer for BIGPLAY On SI, Noah brings a blend of local pride and an insider’s perspective, focusing on thoughtful analysis and storytelling rooted in Cleveland sports culture.

title: Could Audric Estime Be the Answer? Browns Face RB Questions Ahead of Deadline
full_text:
When the Cleveland Browns entered the 2026 NFL regular season, there weren't many concerns about the running back position.
After all, the front office spent all season focused on building up the offensive line, picking a starting quarterback and developing a young wide receiver room. Of all the positions, the running back room seemed to be the last thing on anyone's mind.
However, after the first six weeks of the campaign, it has jumped to the top of the priorities list.
Both starting running back Quinshon Judkins and backup Dylan Sampson ended up injured at the same time. Judkins missed a Week 6 win against the Baltimore Ravens due to an ankle injury, while Sampson was ruled out in Week 1. He unfortunately ended up on the injured list.
At this time, neither has been cleared for Week 7 when the Browns take on the Tennessee Titans on the road in Nashville.
In order to replace some of the lost depth, the Browns' front office went out and signed running back Audric Estime from the Minnesota Vikings' practice squad early last week.
Finding at least one body to pair with Jaleel McLaughlin, who was also thrust into a bigger role with Rahiem Sanders ending up on the injured list, was a big-time need for the Browns.
While Estime was somewhat of an unknown, having only rushed for 234 yards and three scores across his first two seasons in the NFL, he impressed in his debut with the Browns.
On nine carries, Estime recorded 19 yards and one touchdown, picking up two first downs as well. When the ball was in his hands, he had a 55.6% success rate . While his average yards per game was certainly down, his usage, especially in power-needed positions, led to this difference compared to his averages in 2024 and 2025.
But even then, the former Notre Dame standout was still able to find the end zone after just joining the franchise days before his debut.
“I just followed the blocker,” Estime said postgame when asked about what led to him finding six. “And the coaches trusted me. They said when we got down there that I was going to get in the end zone. I had confidence in myself. I didn’t know how it was going to look, but I really had confidence that I was going to get in the paint.”
With more time to get acclimated to the team both on the field and off, and more time for the coaches to get him more intertwined into the system, Estime could carve out a nice role for himself heading into Week 7.
At this point, the Browns are just trying to keep the run game afloat while they await the return of Sampson, Judkins and Sanders, and as long as McLaughlin can affect the game outside the hashes and Estime can get to work in the trenches, the Browns don't need to make a move at the deadline.
Instead, they can lean into the two they have on the roster now, with the hope that by the time Judkins and Sampson are fully good to go, the team is still playing competitive football.
Neither Sampson nor Judkins are supposed to be out for too long of a time period; however, any sort of leg injuries are going to slow running backs down. The Browns will want to play it safe, especially up the gut, so keeping Estime around is going to be important.
And at the end of the day, there is very little downside to letting a 23-year-old get another chance at establishing himself in the league.
“(Estime) shows up (at practice) on Wednesday and, heck, he’s taking meaningful snaps and scores a touchdown (a few days later),” Monken said about him in an article in The Athletic . “So that says a lot about the depth of our team and the expectations of the position, which you should have.
"You should have expectations of any player on your roster playing at a high level."
The Browns and Estime return to the gridiron Sunday, Oct. 25, at 1:00 p.m. EST from Nissan Stadium.
Cade Cracas is a sports media professional with experience in play-by-play, broadcasting and digital storytelling. He is a recent graduate of Ashland University with degrees in digital media production and journalism.

title: One Crucial Schedule Twist the Browns Need to Capitalize On Moving Forward
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are already one of teams making most waves through the first six weeks of the regular season thanks to a 4-2 record and the fact that they have already beaten the 4-2 Steelers and the 4-2 Ravens to claim the top spot in the AFC North, for now.
However, one glance at the remaining schedule for the Browns reveals an interesting quirk that head coach Todd Monken’s team will be looking to parlay into the team’s first postseason run since 2023.
Besides the four remaining AFC North games on Cleveland’s schedule -- a rematch against Pittsburgh, a rematch against Baltimore, and two contests against the 3-2 Bengals -- there is only one team currently holding a winning record among the games yet to be played.
The 3-2-1 New York Giants are the only team currently holding a winning record left on the Browns’ schedule. Besides the Giants, the Las Vegas Raiders at 3-3 are the only other team not holding a losing record. All other opponents left currently carry losing records: Titans, Saints, Texans, Falcons and Colts.
While the Browns would need at least two more wins to cover their win total odds of 5.5 from before the season started, winning all five games left against teams with losing records would ensure a winning season for the first time since 2023, and even then, playoffs might not be guaranteed. That’s why the way the Browns’ remaining schedule is lining up is so important for this team.
Life is hard within the league’s most competitive division. It’s not just the fact that back in 2023, it became the only division in league history with all four teams sporting winning records. It has to do with how hard it is to exert dominance over the other clubs.
Since 2002, the league’s probability at sweeping a divisional opponent sits at 42 percent, but in the AFC North, that number is roughly 34 percent. Likewise, the NFL has a league-wide probability of 3.8 percent of sweeping all three divisional opponents in any given year, but that number shrinks to 1.04 percent in the AFC North, where it’s happened just five times in its history -- the Steelers have done it three times, while the Bengals and Ravens just once, each. Cleveland has never swept the entire division since its inception.
Furthermore, since 2002, the Browns have only managed to sweep a single divisional rival three times in one season, all three against Cincinnati (2002, 2018 and 2020). Cleveland has never swept the Steelers while playing in the AFC North, and hasn’t done so generally speaking since 1988. The Browns have yet to sweep the Ravens in any instance.
With the Browns already handing losses to Pittsburgh and Baltimore, nobody says Cleveland can’t get a sweep over any one of those teams. It just hasn’t happened yet in the AFC North. And even thinking about sweeping Cincy is a complicated proposition, too. Moreover, we haven’t even begun to discuss how and why the team is winning despite Deshaun Watson’s poor performances , and without any sign of life from the ground game .
Yes, Cleveland is off to a phenomenal start to the season , but closing in on a postseason berth won’t be easy. That’s why the Browns need to take advantage of every single opportunity they get, including winning all their remaining matchups against non-winning teams.
Rafael brings more than two decades worth of experience writing all things football.

title: Browns Trade Deadline Big Board: Realistic Targets Ranked by Fit and Cost With Four Weeks Left
full_text:
The Browns are in first place after beating two divisional opponents in three weeks. The roster is filled with exciting young talent, with reinforcements on the way in next year’s draft.
The offense has not been pretty and the defense looks suffocating. In order to keep up the winning ways, Andrew Berry should take a look at these realistic targets at the November 10 trade deadline.
The Cardinals upgraded their running back room in the offseason, and Conner dropped to third on the depth chart. They are not going to win their division or compete for the wild card, so they may want to acquire assets for next year. Conner has been productive in the league, and the amount of carries he would get would be spread out with the other running backs. He would be obtainable for a very low pick.
Fant was a first-round pick in 2019 and has bounced around the league since. He is a backup in New Orleans and only has nine catches this season, but three of those went for touchdowns. The Browns have Harold Fannin Jr., but no real talent behind him. Deshaun Watson has not developed chemistry with Fannin Jr. this season and the offense needs production from the tight end position.
The pass-catching tight end can provide another outlet for Watson and a stagnant offense. He can be had for a late-round pick if the Saints continue to lose and see their contention chances slip.
Every team is seeking offensive line help at the trade deadline and the Browns could use some depth after a complete rehaul in the offseason. They have not played great in the early portion of the season and Penning can help down the stretch. He has only played in three games this season, but would not cost much capital to obtain.
It is no secret that the Browns’ offense has struggled to run the ball this season. Both running backs who played in Sunday’s game were not with the team at the beginning of the season and the offense could use a reliable back. Pollard is averaging four yards per carry and would immediately upgrade the positional group. He is on an expiring contract and the Titans sit in last place in their division.
Dylan Sampson is set to return at some point, but Quinshon Judkins and Raheim Sanders hit the injured list . Berry has three first fourth-round picks in next year’s draft and Pollard could be had for one of them.
The Chargers are in a tailspin at 0-6 and Mack is 35 years old. He signed a one-year, 18-million-dollar contract last offseason. He has three sacks and could bolster a surging defensive line. Due to his age and contract, the Browns would not have to give up too much to get him as a late-round pick should do it.
The downside would be that the compensation could get too high with other teams outbidding each other. The acquisition would also put the Browns over the salary cap.
The Browns’ roster has arrived early and Berry has some interesting options to upgrade the team right now. However, he has stacked draft picks for a deep draft next season and should not compromise good draft picks for the team this year.

title: Two Browns' Players Who Have Earned More Snaps After Win Over Ravens
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns sitting at 4-2 and leading the AFC North Standings after six weeks has to be one of the feel-good stories over the first half of the season.
However, work is far from finished.
Head coach Todd Monken’s group must still navigate the remaining 11 games, including rematches against the also 4-2 Steelers and Ravens, two games versus the 3-2 Bengals, in addition to improving the team’s current struggles, primarily in the ground game and at the quarterback position.
Here are two players -- on on offense and one on defense -- who should see their snap count incremented over the next few weeks based on what they’ve shown so far, along with the players that could see their minutes reduced, as the Browns will attempt to close out the 2026 regular season as successfully as they have started it.
Listen, I realize this might be an overreaction, but there’s really nothing to lose.
Over the course of the last three weeks, McLaughlin ripped off a 28-yard touchdown run in his only carry versus the Steelers -- second carry all-season long -- and followed that with a nine-carry 41-yard effort on Sunday, with starter Quinshon Judkins out of the lineup .
Even with such a minuscule sample, McLaughin leads the team with a 6.5 yard-per-carry average, success rate (54.5) than Judkins (41.1) or Raheim Sanders (33.3), as defined by Pro Football Reference.
Maybe McLaughlin will earn more carries out of pure desperation, as Sanders also missed last Sunday’s game, while second-year pro Dylan Sampson has yet to log an offensive snap this season, but at least McLaughlin has earned a larger share of the workload based on what he’s shown on limited carries.
So far, McLaughlin has played on 17.65 percent of the team’s offensive snaps, compared to Judkins’ 49.73 percent and Sanders’ 27.01 percent. Newcomer Audric Estime has already seen 5.08 of the offense’s snaps after joining the team last week , wasting no time in scoring his first touchdown for the Browns.
But regardless of when Judkins, Sanders and Sampson are ready to reappear for the team -- “Hopefully we’ll get Samp back this week and we’ll get Q back. We’re hopeful to get two,” stated Monken after the win over the Ravens regarding his backfield -- and how much of a factor they can be coming back from their respective energy, McLaughlin has made a solid argument in favor of, at the very least, a running back by committee approach.
While Sanders’ could see some of his snaps taken away as the team’s primary backup, the Browns need to consider taking away snaps from Judkins in favor of McLaughlin.
“J. Mac ran hard, man. He ran hard. He ran with a passion and a mission,” said Monken about McLaughlin’s performance versus Baltimore.
McLaughlin won’t solve the Browns’ ground game issues by himself, but at least there’s a spark there. It would be a shame to see it go to waste.
Grant Delpit’s first quarter head injury sustained against the Ravens might be the catalyst for a change here. Before Week 6, Delpit had participated in 100 percent of the defensive snaps in four out of the five first games, while logging a 97.2 percent in Week 4 versus the Steelers.
Along with Delpit, Ronnie Hickman has also been on the field almost on every defensive play, including a 100 percent snap count in five matchups and a 95.4 percentage in Week 4 against the Bucs.
This had left McNeil-Warren playing around 32 percent of defensive snaps before he set a personal best of 94.7 against the Ravens in Delpit’s absence. Nonetheless, the rookie out of Toledo has been spectacular over the first six games of his pro career, and is currently graded as the top safety in the NFL by PFF.
Combine that with the fact that Delpit has been playing at a subpar level, and Hickman has had an up-and-down season, there’s no reason to keep McNeil-Warren on the sidelines even if Delpit makes it back fast from his concussion.
Now factor in how much slot cornerback Myles Harden has struggled at times, just like Mekhi Blackmon, and it’s obvious that McNeil-Warren needs more time on the field, even if it’s in big nickel formations along with Delpit and Hickman.
The second-rounder has been a little overshadowed by all the offensive rookies from this year’s draft, but McNeil-Warren’s been more than living up to those hefty expectations.
Rafael brings more than two decades worth of experience writing all things football.

title: Browns Biggest Need Ahead of the NFL Trade Deadline Is Painfully Obvious
full_text:
So far this season, the Cleveland Browns have surprised many people with their game results.
However, there still is one big issue that the Browns need to address with the trade deadline coming up.
The Browns Offensive Line Cannot Hold Up To The Ravens Rush. Deshaun Watson Is Just Trying Not To Get Sacked. This Browns Team Has Looked Ridiculous The Last 5 Quarters. Total Collapse. 😬 pic.twitter.com/yHTaCozrS1
Let's put it plain and simple, the Browns offensive line is not good.
This season, Deshaun Watson is the most sacked quarterback in the NFL after being dropped 24 times through the first six games.
While some have been to the fault of Watson, the offensive line has not given him much help at all.
Clearly, there needs to be improvement made to the unit going forward.
This past week, Watson was only able to throw for 164 yards. Watching the film, he was never able to get comfortable in the pocket. Most plays, Watson was forced to flee and try and make the play himself.
Lots of credit to Watson for having the ability to make those plays, but thats not what the Browns need.
It is incredibly hard for a quarterback to build confidence when he is constantly under attack from four-man pass rushes.
Going forward, the Browns need to either make some changes internally or bring in some help to try and bolster the passing game. Some of the plays up Todd Monken's sleeve cannot be run at the moment because they do not have enough time to develop.
As much as the pass game has been weak, the worst part of the Browns' offense this year has been the run game, without a doubt.
Historically, Cleveland is always super strong on the ground, no matter the state of the team. In the current day, some critics are putting the blame on Quinshon Judkins .
However, if you go back and watch the film, the bigger holes needed for the bigger back in Judkins are not there like they were last season.
Sure, faster running backs like Jaleel McLaughlin are able to get through the initial holes slightly better, but film shows that the run blocking overall needs work.
Cleveland seriously needed to take some time at the trade deadline to look at their current line group.
Maybe, they first try and switch some guys around. All five of the starters are brand new in 2026, so while they are getting used to the new team maybe get them used to a new side of the line.
If not, maybe they turn to a rookie like Parker Brailsford .
If that won't work, turn to free agency. While they don't have an insane amount to work with, the $15 million dollars in cap space should be enough to go out and sign a veteran lineman. While some fans may not like it, Jack Conklin is available.
Lastly, of course you could go for a trade. The main issue there is what you would have to give up and for who. If there's a chance to go out and get a solid starter for years to come, maybe then they should use some draft capitol to make it work.
However, I don't like the idea of giving up draft picks for a temporary fix, especially when Cleveland has been able to hit on draft picks like Austin Barber.

title: Where Deshaun Watson Needs To See Major Improvements Moving Forward
full_text:
While the Cleveland Browns took down the Baltimore Ravens 13-10 in their week six matchup, Deshaun Watson did not look great.
That is, until the fourth quarter.
Here are some areas where Cleveland's starter needs improvement:
Deshaun Watson 164 YDS / 0 TD / 0 INT No QBgami. That stat line has happened 21 times before, most recently by Bo Nix on Oct 17, 2024.
On many occasions, Watson cost the Browns plays and even drives due to his inability to get the ball out quickly.
Whther its entirely Watson's fault or poor play designing, something needs to change.
If Watson is going to keep holding on to the ball and being forced to roll out every play, teams are destined to sniff it out and create big plays defensively.
Not only can the Browns generate a more consistant offense with Watson getting the ball out fast, but they can also build his confidence.
Part of the reason why Deshaun Watson has been so good only in the fourth quarter is because it takes him the entire game to get comfortable with his offensive line and opposing defenses.
Especially as the season progresses, the Browns have to get their guy more comfortable faster.
Similarly to the last point, there have been too many times this season when Watson costs the Browns drives because he takes a sack or dumps the ball off to somebody else who gets tackled for a loss.
If nothing is there and you won't be penalized, just throw the ball away. No gain is better than a loss, ten times out of ten.
While turnovers thankfully have not been a big issue, this method limits those turnovers as well.
It all comes down to taking care of the football and extending drives.
This play deserves a little more love 3rd & 4 after Carson Schwesinger's forced fumble. Need a Touchdown badly. Deshaun Watson with a perfectly placed ball over Nnamdi Madubuike to KC Concepcion for 15 Yards... TD a few plays later #DawgPound pic.twitter.com/GDyXNulYRR
The glaring issue with Watson's play this season has been the fact that he is only hot for a small portion of the game.
As we get further into the season and even potentially into the playoffs, Watson needs to perform at a higher level throughout the entire game.
For example, in the first half against the Ravens, Watson went three for nine, with 32 total yards.
In each of the Browns' wins so far this season, head coach Todd Monken did one thing that helped Watson out tremendously. He kept it simple.
Until late in the game, Watson doesn't need to be taking shots down the field.
While it would be nice, Watson can execute the offense just fine with shorter passes. Ultimately, that's going to allow receivers to make plays, drives to consume more time, and confidence to be found.
Its great to win games, and Watson does deserve lots of credit for the Browns' success.
There are just a couple of factors that, if worked on, could take Cleveland to the next level going forward.

title: Deshaun Watson Says the Browns Have Yet to Play Their Best Football
full_text:
Deshaun Watson has made the late game dramatic moment very familiar in Cleveland this season. Following the Browns' 13-10 comeback win over the Ravens, Watson said the confidence the team has in those scenarios is a product of the work they do all week.
"This is what we practice for ," Watson said. "We practice it all off season. We practice it every week."
Cleveland were still struggling with consistency on the day offensively as Watson admitted. 16 of 26 passes completed for 164 yards, no TDs, no INTs and 29 yards on the ground. When they needed a play late though, Watson found Jerry Jeudy on a 33 yard completion which put them in a great position to win.
Deshaun said he'd been given the advice by Jeudy as to the route. Having spotted the late shift in the defense he went to the in-cut and found Jeudy down the field.
“He did a good job getting his depth and I put it on time,” Watson said. “He caught it, got the extra yards and put us in a position to win.”
Watson says he takes over in those moments, reminding the lads that their opportunity is going to come.
"I take charge and look at every single one of those guys in the eyes and let them know that, hey, opportunity is going to come. Let's finish it. Let's go win."
The QB also gave credit to the Baltimore defense for making the game so tough. Watson said they were constantly mixing up their coverages and pressure schemes which forced Cleveland to make adjustments and get the ball out quicker.
Even with the offense still working through those adjustments Watson feels there's still room for improvement. The Browns improved to 4-2 and moved into first place in the AFC North. Watson noted that you can certainly learn from a close win prior to the next two divisional games.
"We haven't even played our best football," said Watson.
For now the division leading Browns are finding ways to finish games. Watson pointed out that the more you see players encouraging each other through the missed opportunities and the tough stretches, the more belief you start to get. The challenge for Cleveland will be to find a way to bring that 'we'll finish' mentality into the game earlier on.

title: Browns May Have Beaten Ravens, But Deshaun Watson's Struggles Put Team in Difficult Spot
full_text:
The late great John Madden used to say that “winning is the greatest deodorant”, but the AFC North leading Cleveland Browns might be considered an exception.
Even standing at 4-2 and owning the first two tie-breakers over the Ravens courtesy of their Week 6 victory at Huntington Field on Sunday, 13-10 , Deshaun Watson has been stinking it up at the quarterback position.
Against Baltimore, Cleveland had all of 11 passing yards at the halfway mark, at which point Watson had completed just 3 out of 9 pass attempts, and had been sacked three times. At halftime, Baltimore was leading 10-0, and over the course of the following two quarters did everything in their power to end up with the “L”, but that doesn’t erase just how awful Watson was playing up to that point.
In the third quarter, Watson went 5 for 5 for 46 yards before finding a little rhythm late with an 8 for 12 fourth quarter for 94 yards, bringing his final stat line of 16 for 26 for 164 underwhelming but at the same time deceiving yards against the Ravens, while also getting sacked two more times over the final half. His QBR for the game was a miserable 22.8.
The Browns have been winning despite a subpar performance by Watson all season long. Yes, he’s been able to engineer four game winning drives so far , but the fact remains that Cleveland’s offense has barely resembled a professional outfit throughout most of the team’s six games to date.
And while there are several issues on offense that don’t depend on Watson -- like the team’s still struggling ground game -- the quarterback is literally putting the Browns behind the 8-ball. Before today’s game against the Ravens, Watson had been sacked a league-leading 19 times, most of them his responsibility.
Out of those 19 sacks, eight had come on first down, and 13 of them with 10 or more yards to go, including three on third and 10+ to go. Among today’s five sacks, one came on first and 10, another on second and 10, and the other three on third down, including a third and 14 to go.
Another interesting split is that before today’s game, he was completing just 47.2 percent of his throws on third down. Facing Baltimore, he managed to convert three times out of 16 pass attempts on third downs for the game.
Watson entered today’s matchup ranked 26 out of 33 qualified passers in Total QBR, while the Browns are currently third in the league with 31 punts so far, including all five first half drives against the Ravens today.
A win is a win, there’s no denying that, and any Cleveland Brown will appreciate it. But the current trend of winning despite Watson is unsustainable.
To make matters worse, there is no Plan-B ready to go for the Browns.
Cleveland went all in with Watson when the team decided back in preseason that they were sticking with the 31 year-old veteran as the starter after not playing an official game in almost two years. After all that has transpired since second-year passer Shedeur Sanders led the team to three victories over the second half of last season, including the firing of Kevin Stefanski as head coach and the hiring of Todd Monken to replace him, and a quarterback battle between Sanders and Watson that nobody expected -- while leaving fellow second-year passer Dillon Gabriel on the sideline -- only to hand Watson the starting gig, the only way to sit Watson now is to do it in a definitive manner.
The Browns have been overselling Watson so hard throughout the last few months, that Cleveland can’t bench him unless it’s for good, and that won’t happen while the victories, no matter how narrow, keep coming.
On one hand, Watson has at least shown enough resiliency to bring those four wins home. On the other, the Browns don’t seem to have a plan anymore for Sanders -- nor Gabriel, for that matter.
So it’s become Watson or bust for the Browns, and with the team installed in first place of the AFC North, some would say you don’t need to fix something that isn’t broken. However, the team’s offense, especially at the quarterback position, is evidently broken -- just not broken enough for Cleveland to be losing the games that would inch them closer to one of the top quarterback prospects for next year’s draft .
In that sense, winning despite Watson playing so poorly has become Cleveland’s most recent quarterback curse, because if we’re being honest, how long do you expect to continue to win with this caliber of play at the trigger. And if you do continue to win a few more games, are you really entertaining the idea of extending one of the worst contracts in league history, with what Watson has been showing so far?
Rafael brings more than two decades worth of experience writing all things football.

title: Updated Cowboys Depth Chart For Week 7 vs Eagles Gives Rookie Well-Deserved Promotion
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys' 2026-27 season is teetering on the edge of being a complete disaster after suffering two embarrassing losses in a row. Unfortunately for Dallas, both losses were in primetime, so the entire NFL world was watching.
Dallas will be looking to bounce back in Week 7 on the road against the division rival Philadelphia Eagles , with yet another primetime clash. The NFC East showdown will go down on Monday Night Football.
As the team prepares to ramp up its preparations for the upcoming weekend, the Cowboys dropped their unofficial depth chart . There were very few changes, but they were noticeable, including a slight promotion for a fan-favorite rookie. Now, sorry, we aren't talking about Caleb Downs this time.
Let's take a look at the latest Cowboys depth chart as the team prepares for its third primetime game in three weeks, which will hopefully be a return to the win column.
The biggest takeaway on the defensive side of the ball comes at linebacker. While the injury to Dee Winters plays a role in the movement on the depth chart, rookie Jaishawn Barham moves into the starting slot after a hot start to the season.
In DeMarvion Overshown's absence, Barham was handed green-dot duties as a rookie , which says a lot about the coaching staff's confidence in him. Let's hope the movement on the depth chart gives Barham some additional confidence as he continues to develop.
Overshown, meanwhile, is expected to return on Monday Night Football and occupies the other starting linebacker position, so it will be interesting to see who handles green dot duties moving forward.
Another interesting note is that rookie edge rusher Malachi Lawrence, who earned the start last week over Donovan Ezeiruaku, is still listed as the backup. We'll have to see if that continues as the week rolls on, or whether Lawrence will ultimately leapfrog Ezeiruaku on the depth chart.
Dallas returns to the practice field on Wednesday afternoon, so we'll have to see how it all turns out.

title: Cowboys Cut Ties with 2024 Draft Pick, Sign QB to Practice Squad Among 3 Roster Moves
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys did some roster shuffling on Tuesday, with the team making three moves in total.
Along with signing Kyle Trask to the practice squad , Dallas promoted safety Juanyeh Thomas to the active roster and waived cornerback Caelen Carson.
The signing of Trask gives the Cowboys a new quarterback on the practice squad after the last one, Joe Milton, was poached by the Philadelphia Eagles last week.
Carson was a fifth-round pick of the Cowboys in 2024 and never panned out over his two-plus seasons with the team. Carson had played just 17 snaps on defense this season, all of which came in Week 3. He was inactive in Weeks 1 and 2, and he only played on special teams in Weeks 5 and 6.
Carson was involved in a competition for a starting cornerback spot in the offseason, but he ultimately lost out to Cobie Durant and failed to secure the top backup job over Shavon Revel.
Carson's opportunity at any semblance of a role went out the window after the Cowboys traded for Joey Porter Jr. late last month.
The Cowboys' willingness to part ways with Carson could be a sign that they expect Durant back this week. The veteran hasn't played since Week 2 due to a hamstring injury.
Thomas was signed to the practice squad late last month and he has since gotten into three games for Dallas, playing 12 snaps on defense and another 65 on special teams.
Thomas, who appeared in 36 games with the Cowboys over the last three seasons, has four tackles in his three contests in 2026.
Dallas has been ravaged by injuries at safety this season, with both P.J. Locke and Jalen Thompson, two of the team's free agency acquisitions during the offseason, landing on IR.
Thompson is will be eligible to return in Week 8 after being placed on IR in Week 4, and Locke is eligible to be removed from the list this week, although it remains unclear if that will happen.
Trask was a second-round pick of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2021 and has played in seven games since then but has never made a regular-season start during his disappointing career.
Trask fills in behind the two quarterbacks Dallas has on the active roster in Dak Prescott and Sam Howell, the latter of whom beat out Milton for the QB2 job during the offseason.
