title: Is DeMarvion Overshown Playing vs. Eagles? Cowboys LB Says He's Back After Missing 5 Games
full_text:
It's no secret that the Dallas Cowboys have had arguably the worst defense in the NFL this season amid a 2-4 start.
However, a multitude of injuries haven't exactly made things easier on the defense under first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker.
The Cowboys have been without some key starters for multiple weeks and are now dealing with the looming absence of linebacker Dee Winters, who suffered an Achilles strain in the 23-13 loss to the Green Bay Packers in Week 6.
Fortunately, the Cowboys are set to welcome back a starting linebacker to help make up for the loss of Winters as Dallas looks to fight for playoff positioning in a weak NFC East.
Cowboys linebacker DeMarvion Overshown told Patrik Walker of DallasCowboys.com that he will make his return for Week 7's road matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday Night Football.
Overshown originally suffered a hamstring injury in Week 1's loss to the New York Giants and has been sidelined for the past five games.
Following Winters' injury, Overshown is making a timely return and could be tasked with wearing the green dot on defense moving forward.
It's unrealistic to think that Overshown's return will magically fix the Dallas defense but perhaps he can provide some sort of spark that helps the unit make even the slightest bit of progress.
Given what he's had to go through in the past, Overshown took the hamstring rehab "very serious" and is continuing to stay thankful for the opportunity to play football regardless of what challenges get thrown his way.
“I’ve definitely taken this rehab, this recovery, very serious," Overshown said, per Jon Machota of The Athletic. "I’ve been trying to get back on the field since the week after I got out, so getting this opportunity to go this week. I’m thankful that I’m still able to get to do what I love.”
Cowboys fans will be holding their breath once Overshown returns to action against Philadelphia. He's had an unfortunate injury history, and the recent hamstring issue has been the least among these complications.
Overshown has undergone major surgery on both knees due to two separate season-ending injuries that took place a year apart in 2023 and 2024.
When healthy, he's been a solid linebacker, but the injury label will continue to follow him until proven otherwise.

title: Week 7 NFL Power Rankings: Cowboys Continue Free Fall
full_text:
While no loss is easy to swallow, the past two for the Dallas Cowboys have been incredible difficult.
We all knew Dallas would have issues on defense. Even with a rebuilt roster and a new defensive coordinator in Christian Parker , no one realistically expected an elite unit. Instead, all they asked for was a competent group that could occasionally make a stop. What was unexpected was the offensive ineptitude we have seen the past two weeks.
After six games, the Cowboys are now 2-4 and have one of the worst defenses in the league. They also have an offense that scored 29 points combined in their prime time games in Week 5 and Week 6. Their sudden offensive struggles have them flying down many boards in our Week 7 NFL power rankings roundup.
Ranking: 21 | Last week: 23
Connor Orr has the Cowboys moving up two spots, but that has to do with other teams falling. He's still not sold on Dallas and believes Brian Schottenheimer could be in danger of losing his job if he doesn't do well with the next three games, which are all winnable.
"The Jerry Jones referendum on hiring Brian Schottenheimer as head coach has been delayed long enough. Lose multiple times against the Eagles, Cardinals and Colts over the next three weeks and we might be talking about must-see Jones press conferences on a weekly basis from here on out," Orr wrote.
Ranking: 20 | Last week: 15
ESPN had Dallas on the edge of playoff contention last week, even after losing to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Now, they're all the way down to No. 20. One major concern for them, according to Todd Archer, is the sudden lack of a ground game.
"The Cowboys' running game is off to its worst start -- 456 yards in six games -- since 1989, the year before Emmitt Smith showed up. Six different running backs have more total rushing yards than the Cowboys. Javonte Williams has seven rushing touchdowns, but the inconsistency and lack of attempts are killing the offense," Archer wrote.
Ranking: 22 | Last week: 17
Brent Sobleski also took aim at the offense, saying they were bad enough when it was just the defense that was inept. Now, the Cowboys can't do anything right on either side of the ball.
"It was bad enough when the Dallas Cowboys' defense wasn't working. Now, the same can be said about the squad's previously potent offense," Sobleski wrote.
Ranking: 22 | Last week: 20
Josh Kendall and Chad Graff work together on The Athletic's rankings, and have the Cowboys sliding two spots to No. 22. They do have one silver lining, although it's fantasy related. That said, they're not wrong about CeeDee Lamb, who is having a phenomonal season.
"The only people associated with the Cowboys who are happy at the moment are Lamb’s fantasy managers. He’s ninth in scoring (21.9 ppg) and third in the league in receiving yards (577). He was targeted 18 times Sunday night and finished with nine catches for 70 yards," Kendall and Graff wrote.
Ranking: 26 | Last week: 24
Nate Davis, like many others, is shocked by the way the Dallas offense performed. He even called them out for the "GOTI" claims that Dak Prescott made famous this offseason.
"GOTI, aka, Greatest Offense There Is? It's nice to have goals. Not always wise to publicly reveal them," Davis wrote.

title: Ex-Cowboys QB Questions Effort on Offense in Latest Indictment of Brian Schottenheimer
full_text:
While the putrid showing from the Dallas Cowboys' defense hasn't been much of a surprise given the issues the unit has had in recent years, the struggles on offense have been.
Over their last two games, the Cowboys have scored 29 points combined, and they have scored 20 points or less in three of six contests this season. No surprise, Dallas has lost each game.
Even when the Cowboys have put a lot of points on the board, the offense has had to work very hard to get them and consistency remains an issue.
Former Cowboys quarterback Ben DiNucci weighed in on the situation after the Week 6 loss to the Green Bay Packers and, based on what he's seeing on tape, he thinks there are a few causes for the offensive woes, with effort being one of them.
"You can’t turn on the Cowboys tape from last night and tell me guys on that offense are giving 100%," DiNucci said . "Lazy, no attention to details, no creativity with play calls."
The part about a lack of creativity with the play-calling has been a common complaint from Cowboys fans and analysts alike. There is no doubt head coach Brian Schottenheimer's play-calling is preventing this unit from hitting its ceiling.
But we also believe the Cowboys have enough talent to overcome that, or at least to put up better showings than we've seen the last few weeks.
As DiNucci went on to note, a lack of effort is a culture issue , which is yet another indictment on Schottenheimer.
Another major issue for the offense has been the Cowboys' inability to account for the blitz. Part of that is, again, because of Schottenheimer's play-calling, but DiNucci also believes there's a communication problem.
"If I had to guess communication issues - when guys aren’t on the same page that’s normally what it is," he said of the blitz pickup . "Pass pro all 5 linemen and RB/TE HAVE to be on same page."
Dak Prescott has traditionally been good against the blitz, but that has not been the case this season overall.
Yahoo Sports' Matt Harmon noted that Prescott is averaging a woeful 4.83 adjusted yards per attempt this season, which is Prescott's lowest mark of his career, and he has a success percentage of 41.7.
To compare, Prescott has totaled 10 adjusted yards per attempt or more in each of the last five seasons, with a career-high 12.44 in 2021. The next lowest mark in Prescott's career against the blitz came back in 2020, when he totaled 5.36 in five games.
The Cowboys' offensive line has seen a precipitous fall in pass-rush win rate as compared to last season.
Dallas ranks 29th (43%) in that area in 2026 after ranking ninth (40%) in 2025, according to ESPN.
What's very clear is execution and play-calling are sorely lacking on offense for the Cowboys, and Dallas can't hope to dig out of this hole it's in if the effort isn't there, also.

title: Cowboys and Dolphins Considered Possible Trade Partners Amid Dallas' Defensive Woes
full_text:
If there is one certainty with the Dallas Cowboys this season, it's that their defense stinks.
Through six games, the Cowboys sport one of the worst units in the NFL. Dallas ranks 23rd against the pass, 32nd against the run, and the team is giving up the eighth-most points per game.
Dallas has problems at every level of the defense, but one of the most glaring issues is the pass-rush , which has mustered up just eight sacks, three of which came in Week 6.
And, of those eight sacks, only 2.5 of them have come from the team's edge rushers, so it goes without saying the Cowboys should be looking to add there before the trade deadline.
In an article identifying 15 players who could get moved before the trade deadline on Nov. 10, Sports Illustrated's Matt Verderame listed Miami Dolphins defensive lineman Zach Sieler among them.
Verderame also mentioned the Cowboys as a potential fit for the veteran lineman.
"Sieler is an interesting trade chip. On one hand, he’s already 31 and he’s signed through 2029 with base salaries of $12.6 million, $15.4 million and $16.2 million, respectively. In short, he’s not cheap to acquire," Verderame wrote.
"Conversely, none of that money is guaranteed, and he could be traded for and then released for no dead cap charge if things don’t work out. For Miami, it makes sense to move on, but what’s the right price point? Since 2023, Sieler has 27.5 sacks."
"Potential fits: Lions, Cowboys," Verderame added.
Sieler has proven to be an effective pass-rusher during his career. He has 27.5 sacks dating back to 2023, and in that span he has tallied 10 sacks twice.
He has two sacks this season, which would be tied for the most on the team, and he had 5.5 in 2025.
The problem, however, is the 6-foot-6, 300-pound veteran is an interior lineman. Granted, he has lined up as an edge rusher, but that's in a 4-3 defense and the Cowboys run a 3-4 , which means they need an outside linebacker, something Sieler is not.
Now, if the Cowboys were to completely strike out at the deadline on traditional outside linebackers and it's between someone like Sieler and nobody, Dallas might spring for a trade for him, but Miami would have to eat a ton of money for the Cowboys to consider it.
Sieler would amount to an upgrade over Otito Ogbonnia when it comes to pass-rush ability, and he has historically been a strong run defender, although he has struggled mightily in that area this season, as evidenced by his Pro Football Focus grade of 31.6.
An interior trio of Sieler, Kenny Clark and Quinnen Williams would be quite formidable and no doubt one of the best in the NFL, and that trio might be able to offer the much-needed boost in the pass-rush the Cowboys need.
All that said, we find it very hard to believe Sieler will ever end up in Dallas, barring a catastrophic injury to Williams or Clark.

title: Cowboys Week 6 Stock Report: Joey Porter Jr. Leads 3 Rising, Caleb Downs Among 6 Falling
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys enter Week 7 of the 2026 campaign in a rut after yet another loss to the Green Bay Packers on Sunday that pushes Dallas to a 2-4 record.
If there's one positive we can point to for the Cowboys amid their putrid season, it's the NFC East, which has been a total disaster .
The Giants are the only team in the division with a winning record, and to show you how awful the NFC East has been, it became the first division in NFL history to see each team fail to win a single game in back-to-back weeks, per ESPN's Adam Schefter .
But it's even hard to get excited about that. Even if the Cowboys find a way to win the division, this team isn't going to do anything in the playoffs, so it would just be delaying the inevitable, which is another disappointing finish to a season.
But let's justt focus on the now for now. Here's the biggest risers and fallers in our Week 6 stock report.
It unfortunately came in a loss, but Williams had his best game of the season in Week 6.
Williams recorded his second sack and had five pressures in total, the second-most on the team, and he had a pair of run stops and tackles for loss.
When it was all said and done, Williams' 86.2 defensive grade,  according to Pro Football Focus , was the highest on the team.
This is what the Cowboys thought they were getting when they traded for Williams, and then signed him to an extension . Now, Williams has to stack good games.
Prescott has seen better days than the one he had against the Packers on Sunday.
Prescott completed 34-of-54 passes for 258 yards and one score to two interceptions, although one of those picks was the result of CeeDee Lamb simply falling down in the middle of this route.
Even still, Prescott was not sharp and he didn't appear to pick up the blitz all that well. We will say, however, that head coach Brian Schottenheimer's play-calling is not helping at all.
One of the biggest changes on Sunday was Spann-Ford getting the start over Jake Ferguson. However, Ferguson still ended up out-snapping Spann-Ford, 42-36.
That said, Spann-Ford still played the highest percentage of snaps he has seen this season, and he recorded better offensive numbers than Ferguson with four catches for 35 yards.
Ferguson took a back seat to Spann-Ford in terms of getting the start, and rightly so because he has been bad this season, both in the passing game and as a blocker. But, as we said, he was still on the field for a higher percentage of plays than his fellow tight end.
Ferguson didn't do much with his snaps, with the veteran tight end recording just two catches for 13 yards on three targets. Ferguson is fortunate the Cowboys don't have another viable tight end on the roster or else his playing time might dwindle.
With a post-June 1 out in Ferguson's contract in 2027, he could be on the chopping block after this season if he doesn't get his act together.
Porter played a season-high 36 snaps and, according to PFF, he was targeted four times but did not allow a reception. Porter had three tackles, including one for loss, and two passes defensed.
While he hasn't had a full workload yet, Porter is already making a big impact. One thing to watch is his ankle, which Schottenheimer said limited Porter to 36 snaps on Sunday. With how awful this defense has been, the Cowboys need more.
Downs moved back into the slot for the majority of his snaps on Sunday after playing more safety in recent weeks because of injuries.
His return did not pan out well, as the Packers picked on him all game long, and had success doing so. Downs allowed seven receptions on all seven targets thrown his way for 76 yards.
We definitely aren't panicking about the first-round pick, but his struggles are certainly worth noting.
After starting over the first five games, Ezeiruaku took a back seat to Malachi Lawrence, with the rookie starting over him . Ezeiruaku also played a season-low 54.7% of snaps.
The good news for Ezeiruaku is, Lawrence didn't do anything with his increased role other than recording a pass break-up. Even still, Ezeiruaku didn't earn his way out of the dog house after posting just one tackle.
The second-year edge rusher hasn't had a sack or QB hit since Week 1 in what has been a disastrous sophomore campaign so far.
We don't need to rehash what Schottenheimer and defensive coordinator Christian Parker are doing wrong because it's the same stuff every week. We're over both and if the Cowboys decided to fire them, we wouldn't bat an eye.
Sadly, there is no change like that coming after Stephen Jones once again expressed confidence in both. Where that confidence comes from is anyone's guess, but what we do know is we won't hold our breath for Parker or Schottenheimer to lose their jobs.

title: Cowboys Get Unexpected Lifeline From Historically Bad NFC East
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys are bad this season , but their division is even worse .
Once seen as a prominent division in the NFL, the NFC East is suddenly in the midst of a terrible stretch of futility. All four teams have gone at least two weeks now without a win, something that hasn’t happened since the 1970 merger .
The NFC East is the first division since the 1970 merger to go winless in back-to-back weeks with every team playing. pic.twitter.com/G2ZBiRoblG
As bad as that sounds, it’s even worse when you realize two of these teams played one another in Week 5, and still no one won. Instead, the Washington Commanders and New York Giants played to a shocking tie.
With every team struggling, the Cowboys have been given an unexpected lifeline and a shot to salvage their season. With the stage set, let’s check out the current standings and how each team looks entering Week 7.
We need to give Dan Quinn some credit because his Commanders defeated the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks in Week 3. That remains their only win, but they did fight back from a 23-3 deficit against the San Francisco 49ers on Monday night to make it a 23-17 ending.
Still, they have just one win and are 0-2-1 in the division. Right now, Quinn has one of the hottest seats in the NFL.
At 2-4, the Cowboys should feel hopeless. That’s not the case, however, since they’re tied for second place with the Eagles. They’re on the wrong side of the tiebreaker but that could change if they find a way to defeat the Eagles , who are without Jalen Hurts, on Monday Night Football.
Dallas did show some signs of life against the Packers on defense, which is encouraging. Dee Winters had an interception, Quinnen Williams and Kenny Clark each had a sack, and Joey Porter Jr. was lights out. If they can build on that and get the offense back on track, they could make a run.
Philadelphia has lost four in a row and will likely be without Jalen Hurts for the remainder of the season due to blood clots in his lungs. It’s a scary situation for Hurts and his health is the top priority. That said, the season is going in the wrong direction and the Cowboys have a chance to kick them while they’re down this week.
John Harbaugh and the Giants shocked Dallas in Week 1, but since that win, they’ve only defeated the Arizona Cardinals and Tennessee Titans. They lost to the Los Angeles Rams and New Orleans Saints while tying the Commanders.
Losing quarterback Jaxson Dart has been devastating for the Giants, and they’re in line for a tough game in Week 7 against the suddenly surging Houston Texans. They’re in first place now, but that might not be the case for long.

title: Dallas Cowboys 3 Biggest Concerns Entering Week 7 Showdown Against Eagles
full_text:
Another week brought us another embarrasing loss for the Dallas Cowboys.
In Week 6, it was the Green Bay Packers who defeated the Cowboys, handing them a 23-13 loss on Sunday Night Football . That score is misleading since a late touchdown from the Cowboys made it seem closer than it actually was.
In reality, the Cowboys were outplayed from the opening drive and enter a Week 7 showdown with the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday Night Football with several concerns to address. Here we look at three of the more pressing issues that need attention.
Last year, Javonte Williams ran for 1,201 yards and averaged 4.8 yards per attempt. Through six games in 2026, he has just 317 yards while averaging 3.7 yards per carry and is still looking for his first 100-yard outing of the season.
Dallas was supposed to have an explosive offense with a running game capable of carrying the load. As they prepare for Monday Night Football in Week 7, that rushing attack has been non-existent making this one of the primary concerns against the Eagles. If they can get Williams going, everything will become easier on offense. If not, Dak Prescott might be asked to throw it 50-plus times again, which isn't typically a recipe for success.
Dak Prescott has feasted historically when blitzed. He's been phenomonal at identifying where the rush is coming from and finding the open player. Over the past two weeks, that hasn't been the case.
Prescott has put together his two worst performances of the season as the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Green Bay Packers made life difficult on him with their pressure. In Week 5, Tampa Bay blitzed on 43% of of the plays and as Jon Ledyard writes, that led to a major drop in Expected Points Per Play .
"On non-blitzed dropbacks, Prescott had a +0.09 EPA/play, a number that fell to -0.31 EPA/play on blitzed dropbacks. That means the Cowboys were losing about a third of a point on every Bowles blitz," Ledyard wrote.
Green Bay blitzed 35.71% of the time and Prescott again struggled as he finished with two interceptions and just one touchdown in each game. Following those two games, Cowboys insider Bryan Broaddus expressed concern about Prescott's current struggles with the blitz.
What's going on with Dak Prescott against the blitz? @BryanBroaddus : "The quarterback hasn't been very good (against the blitz). He got fooled tonight. This is the second week in a row (he's struggled against it)." pic.twitter.com/SpNFzmJy5N
In Week 7, the Cowboys will face a Philly team that doesn't blitz often under Vic Fangio . That said, he's an experienced defensive coordinator who will switch things up if needed. Expect Fangio to use more blitzes than typical as he tests whether Dak has fixed the issue. If he hasn't, it could be disastrous for this offense.
At this point, there's no phase of the defense that Dallas should have faith in. They're struggling in coverage, struggling against the run, and absolutely abysmal on third downs. On Sunday, the Packers were 11-of-18 and are now surrendering a first down 54.67 percent of the time on third downs.
Those conversions are one of many reasons the Cowboys have given up at least 20 points in 13 consecutive games. That's the longest active streak in the NFL and the longest in franchise history.
Dallas still has a chance in the NFC East since the division is a mess as a whole, but they have to start winning to take advantage. That begins with the defense figuring out how to play at a higher level.

title: Brian Schottenheimer Explains Why Dallas Cowboys' Offense Lacks Creativity
full_text:
Six weeks into the 2026-27 NFL season, the Dallas Cowboys still have not figured things out . In fact, it has gotten worse.
We knew that there would be growing pains for the Cowboys after an offseason full of rebuilding the roster and revamping the defense , while bringing in a new coaching staff, but then everything went completely off the rails.
Injuries started to pile up, and there was no cohesiveness, so we were back to watching a completely disjointed defense trying to figure out a game plan. Unfortunately, the defense isn't the only problem. Dallas' offense has also regressed, and head coach Brian Schottenheimer seems completely over his head .
The Cowboys' offense has become predictable and stagnant. The team can't figure out how to get anything going against the blitz because it is one-note. Schottenheimer was recently asked why the Cowboys' offense has fallen off over the past few weeks , and he turned the blame back to the defense.
DAL's motion/motion at the snap rates the last two seasons. Why the change? https://t.co/wNCJLWEkL6 pic.twitter.com/ad3rawYAbW
Dallas' motion rate has completely fallen off, which is part of why George Pickens' stat line has taken a dip, but Schottenheimer explained that's because the offense is always playing from behind.
Once again, it's a lack of accountability , which is an increasing issue when evaluating Schottenheimer as a head coach.
"You're trying to go fast. You're trying to keep the defense on their heels . You're trying to extend the game for as long as you can and get as many ops as possible, because you don't know what's going to happen," Schottenheimer said, via Joseph Hoyt of the Dallas Morning News . "So that's the No. 1 thing. When you shift in motion, obviously the play clock and the game clock go down, and so that limits your ops.
"That's a big reason why, when you see teams go no-huddle, usually receivers don't change sides. Usually you're moving one guy, maybe the back, and one guy, and you're trying to do that to stay ahead of the clock."
Schottenheimer does have a point. When you're playing from behind, it dictates how you have to play in order to stay in the mix. Playing catch-up is not where anyone wants to be, and unfortunately, Dallas' defense is doing the team no favors.
Ultimately, the entire team needs to step up, because no one has been getting the job done. And if the coaching staff doesn't figure things out quickly, there could be some major changes at the end of the month ahead of the NFL trade deadline. For Schottenheimer, whose seat is getting increasingly hotter, that could be some bad news.

title: Insider Reveals Troubling Root Cause of Bo Nix's Struggles
full_text:
Bo Nix hasn't looked right since the 2026 season began.
The Denver Broncos' third-year quarterback has looked hesitant , as if he's either unsure of what he's seeing or afraid of getting hit. Turns out, fear has played a big role in Nix's funk, and much of it stems from his ankle injury.
Based on what NFL insider James Palmer posted on X this week , that fear is twofold. Palmer has deep connections to the Broncos front office, and his long X post offered quite a few gleanings into what the team believes is going on with Nix.
Let's examine what Palmer had to say, starting with the root cause of Nix's slump: the fear factor.
Nix seems to be afraid of getting hit and turning the ball over. It's easy to see that he's still carrying some anxiety over his ankle, but instead of that play-to-win mindset that helped him win 24 games in his first two seasons as a starter, he now seems to be focusing too much on playing not to lose.
"My understanding is there is a difference with Nix in 2026, where Nix is focused on not losing the game more than winning the game. Don't turn the ball over," Palmer wrote. "Don't be the reason why we lose the game. That's kind of manifested in his mind to the point that the conservative approach has become an issue on the field."
Despite having a Pro Bowl wide receiver — Courtland Sutton — who Nix has targeted 287 times since 2024, a two-time Pro Bowl tight end — Evan Engram — and a dynamic new weapon the Broncos paid dearly to acquire — Jaylen Waddle — the young quarterback leads the NFL in passes behind the line of scrimmage. That's great for PPR fantasy owners who drafted running back RJ Harvey, but it's bad news for the Broncos' offense.
Nix won't push the ball vertically, nor will he target the middle of the field. As Warren Sharp noted on X , 63% of Nix's passes have been outside the numbers, the most in the NFL, but his 6.0 yards per attempt on those throws rank 32nd in the NFL.
Fear is a powerul motivator. But you miss 100% of the shots you don't take. Pardon the cliche.
All opponents have to do is keep the two-high shell to dissuade Nix from throwing deep, swarm the boundary, and they can bottle up the Broncos' offense. Clearly, he's hesitant to throw inside, and that's allowing opponents to easily predict what he'll do.
Middle-of-the-field avoidance has been a flaw in Nix's game since he entered the league, but he's taken it to a whole new level this season. It's a big reason why Sutton is on pace for a career-low year and why Waddle has just 228 receiving yards thus far.
Palmer reports that Nix's ankle is "fine," and while the Broncos understand that recovering from a serious injury can take time, they want to see him take a big hit so he can get back to his feet and realize that he's okay. That could also help Nix be more assertive with his legs.
"The Broncos want Nix to run it more and they're seeing a player that is a bit gun-shy right now," Palmer wrote. "If you look at the runs that Denver has dialed up, a lot of them he's looking for the sidelines and he's looking for a way to get down as soon as possible. He's not looking for the extra yards or the needed yards in key situations. It's been frustrating."
Nix has definitely looked far more reluctant to use his legs this season. But his mobility has always been a big part of his game and the threat he presents to defenses, and his newfound timidity has removed that from the equation this season.
When it comes to off-schedule throws, Nix has never been on a Patrick Mahomes level, but it's always been one of his strong suits — until this season. This season, when Nix breaks the pocket, he's looked anxious and unpoised, leading to fewer rushing yards and fewer big off-schedule completions.
Nix looks uncomfortable, even when the Broncos' offensive line gives him clean pockets. He's bailing on pockets way early, which not only sabatoges the routes in the play-call, but it puts him on the move where, as we just discussed, he's not playing with poise and seeing the field.
It sounds like the Broncos are frustrated with Nix's reluctance to use his legs. And per Palmer, that fear his injury created has much to do with his sketchy pocket presence.
"This plays a part in the drifting or escaping out of clean pockets, I'm told. This has always been an issue with him his whole career, but this year it's more exaggerated and impacting a passing game where WRs are open," Palmer wrote. "Nix oftentimes is on the move before even the first read gets to the top of their route. The play designs have some longer development downfield, so this is a bad combination right now."
Nix isn't giving his receivers the time they need to run the route and get open. He's bailing on clean pockets, and while he's called it "hero-ball," it basically cuts the field in half and reduces the Broncos' offense to a slapdash backyard football exercise.
Sean Payton and the Broncos' coaches are working to coax Nix out of this shell. Following the Broncos' Week 5 win over the Chargers, Payton said at the podium that he wants Nix to " let 'er rip ."
Nix took that to mean "trust what you see." But we didn't see a change in his performance on Thursday night.
Against the Seattle Seahawks four days later, we saw Nix uncork two downfield passes, neither of which were complete, although one of them drew a defensive pass interference penalty that set the Broncos up on the 1-yard line. From there, though, the Seahawks just kept deploying the two-high shell over the top, and dared Nix to throw underneath; when he did, they'd swarm and tackle.
The Broncos went 3-of-14 on third down against Seattle because of this and an inability to get the run game going. It has all dovetailed into a world of suck for the Broncos' offense.
If Nix can get back to trusting his eyes and O-line, everything becomes possible. Per Palmer, Nix is too spooked out there.
"Nix is seeing ghosts at times," Palmer wrote.
Payton made it clear on Monday that the Broncos aren't considering making a change at quarterback. Nix is 18-3 in his last 21 starts. No team benches a quarterback with a .700 winning percentage.
But Palmer reports that the Broncos are "concerned." That being said, based on Nix's 30-game sample size as an NFL starter, the Broncos believe they have plenty to draw on to help get him back on the horse.
That brutal six-game schedule has played a much bigger role in Nix's failure to launch this year than most people realize. Now that the Broncos are through it — navigating that gauntlet with a 4-2 record — I think we're going to start seeing Nix loosen up a little bit.
This is a guy who's always at his best when the chips are down and the pressure is the highest. All it might take is one big game to shake the cobwebs off and get Nix back to playing like his pre-injury self.
The schedule opens up now, starting with this week's road trip to take on the Arizona Cardinals. There's a lot of season left to be played, and Nix has proven to be one of the NFL's best finishers.
He may not have started on the right foot, but if past outcomes are the best predictor of future outcomes, I fully expect Nix to finish strong.

title: Broncos Trade Deadline Big Board: Best Targets Ranked by Fit and Cost
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is on November 10, and given Sean Payton’s aggressiveness, the 4-2 Denver Broncos could be buyers this year.
The Broncos weathered the initial six-game storm largely because of their defense, with Bo Nix and company barely scraping by, so if they do buy, it’ll likely be on offense to find a piece or two to help jump-start the unit.
While there are some intriguing defenders who could be available out there, it makes less sense for the Broncos to go buying on that side of the ball, unless they suffer injuries between now and the deadline, so knock on wood that they don’t.
The Broncos could use help at running back, tight end, left guard, center, and right tackle, as the players at these positions have underperformed, and they'd be the easiest to upgrade. Looking around the NFL, not many trade rumors are circulating yet, but there are some.
Any of these players could make sense, depending on the compensation it would take for Denver to acquire them. Today, we're unveiling our Broncos trade deadline big board, ranked from most to least likely.
Note: At this time, all players listed below are on teams with no more than two wins through six weeks.
The Titans are having a terrible season, and their offense is falling apart, with Cam Ward not looking like a legitimate starting quarterback. There have been rumors that Pollard is available, even going back to before last year's trade deadline.
He's mostly been linked with the Seattle Seahawks, but with the Broncos' running-game issues, they could look his way given J.K. Dobbins's struggles. It's unlikely Pollard would cost in a trade, maybe an early third-round pick in 2027 or 2028, with Denver getting him and a pick a round or two later back in return.
With the Colts firing GM Chris Ballard , many believe a fire sale is coming, but they made it clear they still have high expectations. However, if the Colts lose two of their next three games, that could change.
Nelson is playing on an expiring deal, and the Colts don’t have a first-round pick in 2027. Rumors suggest Indy may be willing to move Nelson to add to its Day 2 war chest in 2027. I could see Payton convincing Broncos GM George Paton to pull the trigger on Nelson amid Ben Powers’s struggles, though he hasn’t been the weakest link on the offensive line.
Taylor is a great running back, but his down-to-down consistency has struggled this year, with a success rate barely better than Dobbins’s. But Taylor does have a higher explosive run rate.
Teams aren’t selling out to stop Taylor, as he is facing only a slightly higher rate of stacked boxes than Denver, with both below the league average. The Colts will likely ask a lot for him , and the cost could be the sticking point.
There's also the fit issue. Taylor is better when the quarterback is under center, and Nix is one of the worst quarterbacks in that department, so it's not something the Broncos do much. If Denver wanted to pay for reputation, then giving up an early-round pick for Taylor is possible.
Still, his current level of play and the running-game analytics suggest a third- or fourth-round pick instead of a first- or second-rounder.
Luke Wattenberg has been a mess, and the Broncos are stuck with him through the 2027 season due to the extension he signed last year, unless they can trade him. Payton is familiar with McCoy, who can also play left guard if Denver wanted to look his way to improve over Powers.
McCoy is better at center, though, and his contract wouldn't be an obstacle in a trade. He should cost only a third- or fourth-round pick if the Saints want to move on from him. The Saints may need to suffer one or two more losses before they'd be willing to sell off some players.
The Texans' offense hasn’t been the issue amid their struggles; their defense has. Moreau has had a good year, and the Texans will likely look to offload either Brevin Jordan or Moreau, but the former's injury history and play should stay Denver's hand.
The Broncos should target Moreau, who has legit Y-tight end upside and could raise the floor, but would two Day 3 picks spread over the next two years be enough?
The Cowboys are underachieving, but they like Spann-Ford for his Y-tight end ability as a blocker and receiver, though he is limited as a pass-catcher. The Cowboys just signed him to a three-year extension, and he's a coach's favorite, but Jerry Jones likes to send messages to coaches when the team is underperforming, and that could lead to Spann-Ford being moved.
There haven’t been any rumors, but an earlier Day 3 pick could probably get it done if the Cowboys had interest in moving him.
This would be a dream get for the Broncos, as Parkinson is one of the better true Y-tight ends in the NFL. He is one of the best blocking tight ends and is more than enough of a receiving threat to be a game-changer for defenses.
However, Sean McVay loves Parkinson, and the Rams love their 13 personnel, which works because of him. Parkinson is still young and could be worth a slight overpay to get the Rams to make the trade, but they’re more likely to be buyers than sellers at this time in what could be Matthew Stafford's last ride.
Still, like multiple other players, a few more losses could change things in L.A.
Unlike Taylor, Williams does his best work in shotgun rather than the center, though he is more than capable at both. He isn’t afraid to open up to the media about topics his team would rather keep behind closed doors, and that's something Payton would take issue with.
Williams is a key player in the Rams' running game, and they're unlikely to move on from him unless they are offered a great deal, but as with Parkinson, two more losses could lead to a massive shift in the Rams' goals for this season.
The Bucs are another underperforming team likely to clean house, as questions arise about whether Todd Bowles will even finish the season as head coach. The Bucs could look to sell some players and kick-start a slight rebuild, so maybe Denver could convince them to move on from their starting right tackle.
Heck, the Broncos could even give them one back in McGlinchey, along with picks to get Goedeke. Probably not, though, given McGlinchey's low quality of play and his contract.
Teams don’t like to sell off offensive linemen who are playing well, even if the Bucs decide to be sellers. It's hard to build a quality offensive line in this league.
This is the dream . The Cardinals are wasting McBride’s prime, and they're still multiple years away from being a threat. It would undoubtedly take a first-round pick just to open the conversation, because he is one of the best tight ends in the NFL.
The Cardinals could be willing to trade away McBride at the right price, though. A couple more losses would likely have to happen first, and the Broncos could help with that by defeating them this week.
While McBride isn’t overly realistic, rumors over the past couple of years suggest Denver has been interested in him ahead of the trade deadline. Never say never.

title: Broncos' IR Watch: Who's Eligible to Return and What They Bring
full_text:
Help could be on the way to the 4-2 Denver Broncos.
Those first six games were brutal, but the Broncos weathered the storm. As the schedule begins to ease up, a handful of Broncos are eligible to return from injured reserve.
Keep in mind that just because they're eligible to return doesn't mean they're healthy enough , nor that the Broncos are ready to activate them.
Let's take a look at the three Broncos eligible to return from IR, starting with the one most fans have been pining for since Week 2.
Coleman suffered an ankle injury in Week 2, though he finished the game and was a big reason the Broncos were able to defeat the Jacksonville Jaguars. The Broncos placed him on IR a few days after that game, and he's missed the four mandatory games to be eligible for return.
Activating Coleman is a no-brainer, but the exact timing of when the Broncos do so could be tied to what happens with Tyler Badie. Badie suffered a thumb injury last week against the Seattle Seahawks, and if his recovery is longer than a couple of weeks, he could end up on IR.
The Broncos started the season with four running backs on the 53-man roster, but they only ever dress three, plus fullback Adam Prentice. Coleman's return would put them back at four, but since the rookie hit IR, other demands may have affected the roster math, which is why we may not see news of Coleman's return until later in the week.
The fourth-round rookie out of Washington plays with tremendous vision and burst, which are two elements the Broncos' ground attack is sorely missing right now. Suffice it to say, this offense could really use him, given that J.K. Dobbins is averaging a career-low 3.3 yards per carry this season.
Crum suffered a knee injury in the preseason, and he's eligible to return, if he's healthy enough. We don't know that he is healthy, though, and it's not a subject Sean Payton tends to open up about.
One big question worth asking here is whether the Broncos need Crum. My answer would be no, unless there were an injury to Mike McGlinchey, at which point, Alex Palzcewski would step in at right tackle, and the Broncos could use Crum.
He's a super smart, athletic freak, but I wouldn't expect to see Crum back any time soon.
After an impressive showing at the Broncos' rookie minicamp, we haven't seen hide nor hair of Lohner. He went under the knife right before OTAs began for a "routine" clean-up procedure that wasn't supposed to impact his training camp availability.
Alas, it did. The Broncos put him on IR designated to return. Given that Denver has already rostered one tight end it hasn't needed yet — rookie Dallen Bentley, who is yet to dress for a single game — I doubt the Broncos are urgently looking to get Lohner activated.
Then again, Payton seems to love Lohner, so that could change the thinking here. But I doubt it.
Gargiuolo suffered a torn ACL in the preseason of 2025. Alas, given that we didn't see him this past summer at training camp, I can only assume his recovery has been slow-going, or he experienced a setback.
The Broncos have some quality interior offensive line depth, so there is zero urgency to push Gargiulo back onto the field. And since we haven't seen the former seventh-round pick for 14 months, odds are he's on ice until 2027.
Bryant went down with an ankle injury in Week 4 , and with two games in the rearview since then, he has two more to go before he's eligible to return. Week 9's road game against the Carolina Panthers will be the soonest he can return, health-willing.
It was a shame to see Bryant get hurt because he was building up some nice momentum, and clearly has a connection with Bo Nix. The injury bug is no respector of persons, though.
Just when Bryant starts rolling, he gets hurt. That's been the theme through his first two NFL seasons; let's hope it's not a permanent one.

title: Broncos Stock Report: 4 Risers, 4 Fallers Entering Week 7
full_text:
The Denver Broncos weathered the storm of their first six-game stretch, getting out to a 4-2 start, which is about as good as anyone could have expected.
The Broncos' overtime win over the Seattle Seahawks afforded them a three-day "mini-bye," a needed breather to rest up before preparing for the Arizona Cardinals in Week 7. The last few weeks have seen several players rise in relief of injured players, especially on defense.
Coming out of this mini-bye, let's break down the Broncos' biggest risers and fallers.
Barron has helped keep the Broncos' passing defense afloat while Patrick Surtain II has missed the past two-plus games. While he's given up completions, Barron has been physical and sticky in coverage, competing hard at the catch point.
Throw in his reliability as a tackler this season — which is huge, given that Denver co-leads the NFL in missed tackles — and it's safe to say the Broncos have a real player on their hands. All that summertime "bust" talk should be thrown completely out the window.
This former first-rounder has been playing up to his draft pedigree.
Like Barron, Abrams-Draine has been relied upon to help cover for the absence of Riley Moss. Although Moss dressed and even played 20 snaps last week, Abrams-Draine saw the lion's share of the snaps, tasked with covering Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Cooper Kupp.
Abrams-Draine's fourth-quarter interception against Seattle was huge, and it illustrated the confidence this kid is playing with as a cover corner. I'd like to see his tackling improve drastically, but he's never been the most physical defensive back.
The NFL's biggest talking point over the past four days has been Nix's slump and whether the Broncos should bench him. However, at 4-2, head coach Sean Payton made it clear on Monday that Nix's job as the starter is still secure.
That doesn't mean the Broncos are blind to Nix's struggles, though. The buzz out of Broncos HQ is that Nix is still quite bothered and affected by his ankle, which he fractured in the playoffs last season.
The Broncos say the ankle is healed, so it sounds like Nix is still struggling with the mental recovery. But now that the worst of the initial schedule is behind them, the third-year quarterback could be poised to get back on the horse, and give fans more than a glimpse of the dynamic player he was before his January injury.
Robinson is on a roll, and the Broncos are going to need him to stay on it. He co-led the team last week against Seattle with six QB pressures, notching his second sack of the season.
With Jonathon Cooper returning and Jonah Elliss dealing with what could be a severe leg injury , Robinson's role should be unchanged moving forward. Robinson has been one of the Broncos' best surprise players of 2026.
Dobbins looks indecisive and lacks burst. The Broncos have fed him over the past several weeks, but it hasn't led to much production.
Dobbins did score his first and second touchdowns of the season over the past two weeks, but he's otherwise been ineffective overall as a between-the-tackles runner. He seems to believe that the schedule had a lot to do with his lack of success early on, and if that's true, we should see him take some measurable steps forward.
Sutton is in line for a career-worst season. Granted, much of that has to do with Nix's slump and the Broncos' disjointed passing offense, but Sutton isn't blameless.
The veteran wideout isn't fighting for the ball at the catch point as we're used to seeing, and he's struggling to create separation as a route-runner, leading some to wonder whether Father Time has caught up to the ninth-year pro. Sutton needs to step it up.
Although he's still on the practice squad, Rapp came in handy last week against the Seahawks with Talanoa Hufanga sidelined with an injury. Rapp played 65 of the 85 total defensive snaps last week, and he was very good for the Broncos, helping to limit JSN and Kupp.
Rapp totaled six tackles and seemed perfectly comfortable and natural playing next to Jones. The Broncos have found their No. 3 safety, it would seem, but when Hufanga comes back, they're going to have to promote Rapp to the 53-man roster eventually, which will mean parting ways with JL Skinner or Tycen Anderson, in all likelihood.
I get it. Wide receiver is a quarterback-dependent position, but Waddle's impact could already be much greater than it's been.
He's dropped to many passes and I don't like the body language I'm starting to see from him. Right now, the Broncos need to fall in line and close ranks around the beleaguered Nix, and for guys like Waddle, when his number is called, he has to answer the bell.
Look for Payton to start opening up this offense moving forward. That should benefit Waddle.

title: Broncos Have Several 2027 Restricted Free Agents—Only One Is a No-Brainer
full_text:
The Denver Broncos sit at 4-2 , with several players set to be unrestricted free agents in 2027. We've updated the outlook for each of those players six games into the season, and now it's time to examine the Broncos' 2027 restricted free agents.
Restricted free agents are eligible for a first-, second-, or original-round tender, which represents the draft-pick compensation the Broncos would receive if an outside team signed the player to an offer sheet. If it's an original-round tender and the player was undrafted, the team that loses the RFA doesn't get a draft pick as compensation.
The Broncos have five players set to become restricted free agents in 2027. We'll look at what the future likely holds for each after six games of the 2026 season, along with an early prediction.
Tillman has excelled as a depth and rotational player on the Denver defense. He has 28 pressures and nine sacks in his career, with four pressures in five games this season.
This will be an easy decision for the Broncos. Tillman needs to get a second-round tender so the Broncos can keep him for another year. The estimated $6.261 million salary is worth it.
Verdict : Second-round tender.
Jackson hasn't seen a lot of playing time the past couple of seasons. The Broncos mainly kept him for depth purposes, but other players have surpassed him on the depth chart.
Jackson won't be tendered, but there's a small chance that the Broncos will re-sign him to a one-year deal. However, that depends on how much the Broncos like players such as Sai'vion Jones and Tyler Onyedim.
Verdict : No tender, might not re-sign.
Key excels at special teams ( first-team All-Pro last year ), and he's shown he can do some good things on defense. He played a significant number of defensive snaps against the Seattle Seahawks because Talanoa Hufanga was out with an ankle injury, though Taylor Rapp received more.
There's a chance the Broncos will give the second-round tender to Key, even if they re-sign Brandon Jones. Another option is a two-year deal, like what the Broncos gave to offensive guard Alex Palczewski this past offseason.
Verdict : Second-round tender or re-sign to a short-term deal.
Badie has stuck around on the depth chart because of what he brings to special teams. He's shown he can be a productive back when called into action, but he's not somebody you want to rely on as a top option.
Badie isn't worth tendering. However, the Broncos like what he brings to special teams, so they could re-sign him to a one-year deal at the veteran minimum to compete for a roster spot.
Verdict : No tender, likely to re-sign.
Crum was the swing tackle and sixth offensive lineman last season after Matt Peart's season was cut short because of injury, and Palczewski stepped in at left guard for multiple games.
Crum did some good things last year, but he struggled in the preseason and is currently on injured reserve. He's unlikely to be tendered, but the Broncos might be willing to give him a one-year deal to let him compete for a roster spot.
Verdict : No tender, likely to re-sign.

title: What it Would Take the Broncos to Trade For RB Jonathan Taylor
full_text:
After losing to the winless Tennessee Titans, the Indianapolis Colts fired their 10-year GM, Chris Ballard , on Monday morning.
The Colts are only two games behind the AFC South-leading Jacksonville Jaguars, but Indy is a mess right now.
If you're the Denver Broncos, it begs the question: Could Colts Pro Bowl running back Jonathan Taylor be available?
The NFL trade deadline is on November 10 , so the Colts have plenty of time to take some calls and look for the best possible offer for Taylor, if they're of a mind to blow it up. He's only 27, and he's coming off back-to-back Pro Bowl campaigns with 1,400-plus rushing yards.
Meanwhile, the Broncos' ground game is still looking for lift-off. The Broncos not only re-signed J.K. Dobbins this past offseason, but the $8 million per year they gave him represented a 4x raise.
Dobbins hasn't been four times better, and he's been far less effective than he was in his 10 games last season. While he's angling for a career-low yards-per-carry average (3.3 YPC), it's important to factor in the caliber of defenses he and the Broncos faced through the first six weeks. The Broncos will be looking for his numbers to climb now that their initial six-week gauntlet is behind them.
That being said, Dobbins has to be better, but so does the Broncos' offensive line — a unit that has also underachieved thus far. It's hard to point to any individual or collective on the Broncos' offense that hasn't failed to meet expectations this season.
That's why Taylor suddenly looks very appealing. However, the financial factors could inhibit a possible trade.
The Colts just signed Taylor to a two-year, $44 million deal in August, and he's on the books this season for a $16.1 million salary-cap hit. In 2027, that number climbs to $21 million and $22.98 million in 2028.
The Broncos have several of their own free agents to worry about after 2026, so any potential trade would have to be balanced against those demands. There's also the reality of wide receiver Jaylen Waddle's cap number ballooning from $4.8 million this season to $27 million in 2027.
Then there's Bo Nix. All the scrutinty around his second contract has gone from a matter-of-course eventuality to a holding pattern amid his slump to start this season, but he's eligible for an extension next spring.
If Nix turns the ship around this season, and the Broncos not only make the playoffs but strike deep again, his financial future will come back into focus. The going rate for a franchise quarterback starts around $40 million per year, and only goes up.
While that's a lot to budget for a quarterback, if conditions led to the Broncos signing Nix to a sizable extension, the bulk of the salary-cap ramifications wouldn't set in until 2029, assuming the team also exercises his fifth-year option.
The Broncos have ways to trim the salary-cap down; saying goodbye to left guard Ben Powers and right tackle Mike McGlinchey after this season would free up enough money to offset the absortion of Taylor's contract, for example, but the team would need viable options ready to start in 2027.
Kage Casey at left guard and Alex Palczewski at right tackle could be those options.
The Colts would likely start the Taylor conversation with an asking price of a second-round pick, plus late-round compensation. A desperate team might pay that, but given the high mileage on Taylor's tires (1,652 career carries) since entering the league in 2020, the Broncos could potentially negotiate it down to a third-round pick, plus maybe a 2028 conditional Day 3 pick.
However, that might be wishful thinking since Taylor is still well under 30. His new contract will expire just as he's about to hit 30, so any team that took him on could feel confident in the next two-plus years of production.
As always, the compensation would also be influenced by supply and demand. If the Colts have a big market for Taylor, it'll only drive the price up, but if the calls are few and far between, that's where the Broncos could potentially slide in with a third-round offer, plus a conditional late-rounder.
People will point to the Christian McCaffrey trade as a potential precedent in 2022. The San Francisco 49ers gave up a king's ransom to the Carolina Panthers for McCaffrey, relinquishing a second-, third-, fourth-, and fifth-round pick.
At the time, McCaffrey was a year younger than Taylor is now, and he was already a two-time Pro Bowler and All-Pro. Factor in his draft pedigree as a former top-10 pick, and the 49ers' needs, and the Panthers were able to come away with a big return in the trade.
Taylor has way more mileage than McCaffrey had and is older, so I have serious doubts that the Colts could command a similar haul that Carolina did. But it make take as much as a second-rounder to pry Taylor off Indy's hands.
Would Taylor be worth such an investment? That's what the Broncos would have to decide. Given their current circumstance, my answer is yes.
Given how often the Broncos run out of the shotgun, they'd need to tweak their run game a bit to give Taylor the runway he needs to get up to speed. But that wouldn't be the worst thing — getting Nix under center more and building the run game and play-action passing attack around it.
Taylor would be an immediate impact player, though. A three-time Pro Bowler and a one-time first-team All-Pro, he led the NFL in rushing in 2021 and has paced the league in rushing touchdowns twice.
On a struggling team, Taylor has rushed for 492 yards and seven touchdowns already, but he's only averaging 4.0 yards per carry. He's on pace to finish with 1,394 yards and 17 touchdowns.
Do you know the last time the Broncos had a 1,000-yard rusher? Phillip Lindsay in 2019. That was a long time ago. But it sure would be nice for Nix to have rushing reliability behind him in the Broncos' backfield.
Unfortunately, Dobbins and RJ Harvey haven't provided that consistency this season. But the Broncos believe the worst is behind them and that offensive improvements are right around the corner .
Given the Broncos' investment in Dobbins and the imminent return of rookie fourth-rounder Jonah Coleman, I have my doubts about them making a move for Taylor. The financial components and trade compensation would also play a role, and after giving up a first- and third-round draft pick to acquire Waddle, which has yet to pay dividends, the Broncos might be a bit gunshy.
Sean Payton loves Dobbins, but if the Broncos made a move, they could get out of his contract painlessly after this season. Meanwhile, Harvey already has a key role in the offense as a 'joker' weapon in the passing game and as a change-of-pace back.
The Broncos also believe in Coleman, but he's been on injured reserve since Week 2. They might want a longer look at Coleman before making any kind of push for Taylor.
One thing I can say for sure is that Taylor would be an immediate upgrade over Dobbins. We have a few weeks until the NFL trade deadline, so we'll be keeping our ear to the floor for any possible buzz.

title: Broncos HC Sean Payton Details OLB Jonathon Cooper's Return to Play
full_text:
It was reported following the Denver Broncos' Week 6 win over the Seahawks that starting outside linebacker Jonathon Cooper was being removed from the commissioner's exempt list and could return to play for Sunday's road matchup at Arizona.
On Monday, as the team turned its attention to the Cardinals, head coach Sean Payton praised Cooper for taking the requisite steps with the NFL to see the field in 2026 following his domestic violence-related arrests over the summer.
“He initiated the steps right away himself," Payton told the media via conference call. "I won’t go into detail all the things that he felt were important. I think the league was on the same page, the club. A lot of it becomes a league issue at that point. To his credit, he didn’t back away at all from what he felt like was necessary.”
Cooper had been on the exempt list since Aug. 30, days before Denver's regular-season opener while awaiting a trial, which directly impacts when he can play football again. ESPN's Jeff Legwold reported on Oct. 16 that "he was in Douglas County (Colo.) court last week for a motions hearing and has a March 2-4 trial scheduled in his case, with a pretrial hearing set for Feb. 19."
Legwold also noted that "his time on the exempt list -- the first six weeks of the regular season -- would count toward any league-mandated suspension in the future. If suspended, however, he would have to return the weekly game checks he has received because suspensions from the personal conduct policy are without pay."
Cooper — whose conditions to return this season included meeting with a therapist — attended weight-lifting sessions, participated in meetings, and was generally active inside the Broncos facility during his stint on the exempt list, Payton revealed in August.
“We wait on the league," he said on Aug. 31. "In the meantime, the difference now is he’s in the facility, he’s lifting, he’s in the meetings. He can’t practice, and then we just wait for this process to play out.”
The Broncos were granted a one-week roster exemption for Cooper's impending return to the active roster, from which the club must make a corresponding move, as it's at the 53-man limit. That move is likely to come in short order.
Even on a limited snap count — it'll be his first meaningful action since January, after all — Cooper should slide back into his old starting job opposite Nik Bonitto, especially with OLB Jonah Elliss nursing a leg injury from last Thursday's victory in Seattle.
Cooper, who's amassed 31.5 sacks across his six-year career, also gets a plus matchup against pocket-passing Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett. Brisett has been sacked 12 times in six games — and was taken down five times in Arizona's Week 5 loss to Detroit.

title: Bench Bo Nix? Broncos HC Sean Payton Gives Definitive Answer
full_text:
Bo Nix has been put through the wringer since the Denver Broncos' 17-14 overtime win over the Seattle Seahawks on Thursday Night Football .
Throwing for just 107 yards against Seattle — on the heels of back-to-back lackluster performances against the San Francisco 49ers and Los Angeles Chargers — Nix has been under fire in the media and on social media. There have been open calls to bench him — both from the local and national perspective — and no small number of Broncos fans have joined in.
After enjoying the fruits of a three-day mini-bye, Broncos head coach Sean Payton held court via Zoom on Monday morning, and his answer to whether he's considering benching a quarterback who's won 18 of his last 21 starts was as definitive as it gets.
“To answer your question, no," Payton said.
Payton said Nix's performance, far below the standard he set in his first two years, is a "byproduct" of all the little things the Broncos aren't executing on offense. The veteran coach believes that as the Broncos fix these things, Nix will improve as a "byproduct" of that process.
"He’s going to become the byproduct of all the finer things that get improved," Payton said of Nix. "The improved play from our offensive line, the more efficient we are relative to balance, running the football. That’s our jobs as coaches here. We talked after the game about we’re excited to get that win, and yet at the same time find that improvement we need in all areas. So, it starts with all of us.”
Payton says that he hasn't paid attention to the tsunami of Nix criticism in the press of late, but we know the veteran coach gets on X and keeps an eye on social media. He's been a strong defender of Nix publicly, including on social media, so it's hard to believe Payton hasn't seen at least some of the recent shade, but he said that his focus has been elsewhere.
“I try to focus on the next day here," Payton said of the Nix criticism. "We’re trying to focus on getting ready to play Arizona. That’s kind of where our attention is.”
On one hand, it's easy to see that Nix hasn't gotten a lot of help from his supporting cast. On the other, a franchise quarterback is supposed to be the tide that raises all ships, making everyone around him better.
We certainly saw that from Nix in his first two seasons. After going four years without eclipsing the 1,000-yard receiving mark, wide receiver Courtland Sutton crossed that milestone in his first year with Nix, and repeated it last season with the added accolade of a Pro Bowl selection.
The Broncos' offensive line has been widely viewed as one of, if not the, best units in football — at least, going into this season. Nix had a big impact on that perception, too. Only one quarterback has been sacked fewer times than Nix since he entered the league in 2024.
Beyond the individual level, Nix obviously raised the Broncos' ship as a whole. This team went from missing the playoffs for eight straight years to earning a wildcard berth his rookie year.
Nix's Broncos followed that up in 2025 with a 14-win season, an AFC West crown, and the No. 1 playoff seed in the conference. Nix had the Broncos on the doorstep of the Super Bowl — hosting the AFC championship game — when he suffered a broken ankle.
So in every way possible, Nix has already proven to be the tide that raises all the ships around him. That's what has made his Year 3 performance so troubling.
All we can do is speculate on why Nix hasn't looked like himself, and beyond the obvious changes at offensive coordinator and play-caller with Davis Webb, the only explanation that makes any sense is that he's still dealing with the effects of his ankle injury. But both Nix and the Broncos have maintained that he's 100% recovered from the ankle injury, even if the eye test would beg to differ.
Even if Nix's ankle is fully healed, is his psyche? We've wondered about that, but one of the intangible traits that attracted the Broncos to Nix in the 2024 draft was his mental toughness and resilience. Fans can only hope that Nix's mental mettle can help him get through what appears to be a serious obstacle.
“This is a tough league. We hit every aspect, and I think that’s one of the things that attracted us to Bo in the beginning is we had seen his ability to climb through adversity," Payton said. "It’s not just Bo that feels that. Right now, offensively, I feel that, our players feel that and we’ll improve.”
Payton remains adamant that Nix and the Broncos' offense will improve. Payton has taken ownership of the offense in his public remarks and by reclaiming the play-calling duties.
Payton didn't say "we'll try to improve." He said "We'll improve."
Fortunately, the Broncos are through the brutal gauntlet of their first six games, coming out as well as anyone could have hoped at 4-2. The schedule eases up a bit now, with a trip to take on the Arizona Cardinals (who just beat the Los Angeles Rams, by the way).
But that Cardinals road game will be followed by a rematch with the Kansas City Chiefs at Mile High. Then it's a road game against a better-than-expected Carolina Panthers team, followed by the Broncos' Week 10 bye.
I suspect things will be looking much better offensively by Week 11. Payton has changed Webb's verbiage back to his terminology , which certainly hasn't helped Nix from a mental bandwidth perspective, but those kinks are being worked out on the hoof.
Payton is a coach who loves to get the last word. When Jacksonville's Liam Coen beat the Broncos in Denver last year, then talked some smack at the podium, Payton circled Week 2's rematch this season, telling Coen at the NFL owners meetings that he's coming for him . Denver won that game.
After Mike Macdonald's incendiary comments about Payton were caught on a hot mic a few weeks back, you can believe the Broncos' head coach double-circled Week 6. Payton won that game, too.
Payton can't miss all the hate being fired at his quarterback. It's about continuing to win games, sure, but you can trust Payton to double his efforts to get Nix and this offense rolling.
And when that day comes, Payton will stand at the podium and smirk, relishing the ridiculousness of being asked whether he'd consider benching a quarterback with a .700 career winning percentage. Yeah, you can believe Payton looks forward to that day, and it might not be too far off.

title: Broncos' 2027 Free-Agent Progress Report: Who Stays & Who Goes
full_text:
We're six games into the 2026 season , and while there are 11 games left to play, we can notice some trends regarding the long-term future of some of the players on the Denver Broncos' roster.
Multiple Broncos will be either unrestricted or restricted free agents after this season, which means the team will have decisions to make.
Today, we're going to look at the Broncos set to become unrestricted free agents in 2027 and examine what the future may hold for them. We'll determine how these players are trending, whether it's a priority to re-sign them, possibly re-sign them, or allow them to depart.
In future installments, we'll look at the players set to become restricted free agents and players whom the Broncos may have decisions to make about their contracts.
Jones has been a solid contributor as the starting free safety and he's come at a reasonable salary. He's not a top safety, so it's not likely the Broncos will have to break the bank to keep him.
It's not out of the question for Jones to be re-signed but it may not happen before the end of the season. Whether he returns in 2027 will most likely come down to his asking price.
Verdict : Possible re-signing.
McMillian has been invaluable as the slot corner and a player who can be utilized in blitzes. He has thrived in Vance Joseph's scheme.
Because slot corners don't command a lot of money, the Broncos could get McMillian re-signed at a reasonable price. The Broncos should try to get a deal done before the end of the season.
Verdict : Priority re-signing.
Moss has continued to play well, with five pass breakups in five games. That puts him on pace to have 17 for the year, not far from the 19 pass breakups he had last season.
While his play warrants Moss sticking around, will the Broncos be able to afford his price point? There's also the presence of Jahdae Barron, who has shown promise since Moss and Pat Surtain II went down with injuries. One can't rule out Moss staying, but there are factors that may mean he moves on after 2026.
Verdict : Likely to depart.
Mims missed a couple of games because of injury. Since his return, he's seen snaps on offense and special teams. However, he hasn't had many explosive plays .
While Mims is a talented player, it's not a given he'll be re-signed at this point. The Broncos might be content to look elsewhere rather than commit money over multiple years.
Verdict : Likely to depart.
Uwazurike has started five games, but has just two pressures. He's shown he can be a good rotational player, but his play hasn't quite been what you expect from a starter.
Sai'Vion Jones and Tyler Onyedim are likely to be in the mix next season for more snaps, and if the Broncos are happy with how they are developing, they will likely let Uwazurike move on.
Verdict : Likely to depart.
Powers enters the final year of the four-year deal that he signed back in 2023. He has a void year for cap purposes, added after he restructured his contract in 2024.
Powers isn't playing as well as he was last season before he got injured. It's not hard to see the Broncos not move on from Powers, especially if they believe Kage Casey and Alex Palczewski can compete for a starting job.
Engram signed a two-year deal in 2025, and the Broncos added a void year for cap purposes. He's had his moments, but it's clear his best years are behind him.
The Broncos will almost certainly allow Engram to leave and look to either free agency or the draft to get another receiving tight end.
The former 2023 sixth-round pick has mostly contributed on special teams, though he has a handful of defensive snaps. It's special teams where Skinner has done his best work.
This is a case of a player the Broncos won't re-sign during the season, but there's a good chance they will get a deal done with him just before free agency or during that period after he's tested the market.
Verdict : Possible re-signing.
The former 2023 seventh-round pick has started six games. Forsyth has been solid but appears to be better suited as a depth player than as a starter for multiple games.
Still, you always want quality depth on the offensive line, so it would make sense to keep Forsyth around. As with Skinner, Forsyth won't get re-signed during the season, but the Broncos might do so closer to free agency or after letting him test the market.
Verdict : Possible re-signing.
Stidham has shown throughout his career that backup quarterback is his ceiling. He is somebody that is respected in the Broncos locker room, though, which means you can't rule out him sticking around.
Much of this will come down to his asking price. Stidham is getting $6.5 million this season and will likely seek a bump above that in a new deal. Also, the Broncos might opt to keep another player (who will get to in a minute) and draft a quarterback to compete for the backup job.
Verdict : Possible re-signing.
The rest of the pending unrestricted free agents are LS Mitchell Fraboni, WR Lil'Jordan Humphrey, TE Nate Adkins, C Michael Deiter, FB Adam Prentice, OT Matt Peart, IDL Matt Henningsen, QB Sam Ehlinger and S Tycen Anderson.
Among these players, Fraboni, Humphrey, Adkins, Prentice and Ehlinger could all be brought back on one-year deals, with the idea that they would compete for roster spots, and in a couple of cases, get added to the practice squad if they don't make the 53-man roster.
Peart is another possibility, but the Broncos might let him walk if they are fine with the other offensive tackles they have to serve as a a swing tackle.
Deiter and Hennigsen, who were both placed on season-ending injured reserve, will likely be allowed to depart. The same may happen with Anderson, as he hasn't stood out thus far.
