title: Broncos' Mini-Bye Player Grades: MVP, Standouts & Underachievers
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are 4-2 after their first six games, which nearly no one expected given the toughness of their initial schedule.
It hasn't always been pretty. The Broncos' offense has struggled, outside of a few moments, and the defense has been mostly great. Still, they got out to a 4-2 start , tying four other teams for the third-best record in the AFC.
Both of the Broncos' losses came at the hands of the only two remaining undefeated teams entering Week 6: the Kansas City Chiefs and the San Francisco 49ers.
With that first six-week gauntlet now in the rearview, we're taking a look at how the individual Broncos have graded out. After every game , I grade each player on a snap-by-snap basis, but this "mini-bye" was a great opportunity to look back at the season so far.
To qualify for a grade, a player needed at least 175 snaps. Only 10 Broncos on offense and 15 on defense qualified.
These grades will cover the Broncos' MVP on both sides of the ball, the highest-graded players, the quarterback, the second- to fourth-highest-graded player on each side of the ball, and the three lowest-graded players on each side of the ball. So, let’s get into it.
This season, Meinerz has allowed six total pressures, tied for the seventh-fewest among 41 guards with at least 300 offensive snaps, and his pass-blocking efficiency is the same. Meanwhile, he has been the NFL's best guard in run blocking across multiple metrics.
Allen has been a monster at the start of the season, and while he has some down moments as a run defender, he still looks improved from where he was a year ago. He leads the Broncos with 26 pressures and leads all NFL interior defensive linemen.
Including edge rushers, Allen ties for the sixth-most pressures in the NFL. With defensive stops, he is tied for the fifth-most among all defensive linemen and edge rushers and is tied for third among interior defensive linemen.
This season has been rough for Nix, with his average depth of target dropping from 7.51 in 2025 to 5.56 in 2026 and his air yards per completion dropping from 4.74 to 3.6. He has taken a massive step back in his play , grown too comfortable in the dink-and-dunk game, and isn’t pushing the ball.
Nix's percentage of throws of 10 or more air yards has also dropped significantly. Denver is 4-2 and through the toughest part of its schedule, but this team needs Nix to be better.
Garett Bolles | LT | Grade: 72.8
Bolles has allowed three pressures on the season, which is the fewest of the Broncos' starting five offensive linemen, and three fewer than Meinerz. Among 45 tackles with at least 300 snaps, Bolles is tied for the fewest pressures allowed and has the highest pass-blocking efficiency.
Nik Bonitto | OLB | Grade: 71.6
Bonitto has the second-most pressures on the team, but his impact was limited over the first four weeks. He totaled just a single sack over that span, 12 of his 20 pressures, and had serious issues as a run defender.
Bonitto has surged over the last two weeks, though, with eight pressures, three sacks, a forced fumble, and improved run-defense play.
Talanoa Hufanga | S | Grade: 64.7
Hufanga has had a good season, but not as good as last year. His run-defending issues and unreliable tackling have contributed to the Broncos' inconsistencies against the run.
Still, Hufanga has done well in coverage and is moving around a bit more to create confusion for opposing quarterbacks. He also has two interceptions, including a pick-six, which helped swing Week 3's victory over the Los Angeles Rams.
Malcolm Roach | DL | Grade: 63.9
Roach has the third-most pressures on the team, the fourth-most stops, and leads in batted passes, but his seven missed tackles are the fifth-most. He's had some huge moments in the passing game and has improved as a run defender each week after a terrible season opener.
Jaylen Waddle | WR | Grade: 59.7
The second game of the season highlighted Waddle's upside, but he has struggled since then. He has four drops through six games, and he needs to clean that up.
However, Waddle's routes have been clean, and his 3.5 yards of average separation is the 15th-highest among 74 receivers.
Ben Powers | LG | Grade: 55.6
Powers has been hit or miss and has allowed the second-most pressures on the Broncos, with 13. His run blocking has helped his grade some, but this still isn’t ideal for a six-game sample size.
Powers is the fourth of 10 offensive players who qualified for a grade over the first six games, with him being 0.3 points higher than tight end Evan Engram and 2.2 points higher than wide receiver Courtland Sutton, before getting to Nix and those in the negative group.
Adam Trautman | TE | Grade: 43.1
Trautman has been rough this year, and his issues as a receiver and blocker have been a detriment to the offense. Nate Adkins has outplayed Trautman, falling short of the snap count for the overall grade, but in the three games Adkins qualified for a grade, he was in the 70s. Trautman's season high was 55.2, and he finished four of the six games under 50.
Eyioma Uwazurike | DL | Grade: 44.7
The Broncos gambled on Uwazurike as a key piece, but he has been mostly a liability on the field. He has easily been the Broncos' worst defender this season, and is having maybe two good or great plays a game, which isn’t ideal for someone averaging 37 snaps per game.
Maybe it's time to get Tyler Onyedim involved on defense. The rookie has been a healthy scratch all season, despite being the Broncos' first pick in the 2026 draft.
Luke Wattenberg | C | Grade: 48.5
Wattenberg has been bad, allowing the third-most pressure on the team and the second-most among 25 centers with at least 300 snaps. His pass-blocking efficiency is tied for second-lowest.
Wattenberg's run blocking has been an even bigger detriment to the offense, and he ranks in the bottom three in almost every run-blocking metric for centers.
Jonah Elliss | OLB | Grade: 51.1
Elliss is a technical player, but he isn’t overly explosive, which hurts in the modern NFL where explosive plays and explosive potential matter so much. He's had some awful moments, but overall he was solid, though he showed he isn’t a starting-caliber player but rather a solid depth piece.
Elliss's injury against Seattle looked severe , but at least the Broncos are getting Jonathon Cooper back . In other positive developments, Que Robinson vastly outperformed Elliss in five of the six games so far.
Mike McGlinchey | RT | Grade: 52.9
McGlinchey has allowed the most pressure on the team with 14, which is tied for the 15th-most among 45 tackles with at least 300 snaps. He has always been a bit inconsistent as a pass protector, with his run blocking as a strength, but he's been even more inconsistent in that area this season.
Ja’Quan McMillian | CB | Grade: 53.1
McMillian has made some big plays in big moments, both in his career and this season, but he hasn’t been the most consistent player. His lack of size has been a detriment in the slot, as opponents have looked to take advantage of it both in the passing game with bigger slots and in the run game.
McMillian's missed tackles stem from his lack of size, and opponents have generated multiple explosive plays targeting him. That said, he's been solid, and a 53.1 grade is slightly above average; he just finds himself in the negatives because most of Denver's defenders have been good or great.

title: Kerby Joseph Posts Intense Workout: Will Safety Play in 2026?
full_text:
Detroit Lions safety Kerby Joseph excited supporters when he posted on social media a workout at the teams Allen Park Performance Center.
In the early morning hours, Joseph shared an intense workout that highlighted his speed, ability to cut and to change directions.
It has been over a calendar year since the All-Pro safety played, fueling speculation his career could be in jeopardy.
He has been seen at the practice facility in a jovial mood, but still remains on the Physically Unable to Perform List.
Head coach Dan Campbell, speaking to local reporters prior to practice on Tuesday offered an encouraging update, when asked about the former third-round pick.
“He's doing well. I'll leave it at that. He really is. He's doing a good job. I'm not going to give you a timetable, but I've been pleased with where he's at," Campbell said. "He's in a good head space right now, which is great because that's hard. You're coming off this, you're wanting to go and you're working at it, and at some point it's time for football. We all know that and recognize it, but we'll take it one day at a time.”
When asked directly if he expects Joseph to play this year, Campbell replied, "I do."
Additional NFL Insider Analysis: Detroit Lions Biggest Need Ahead of Trade Deadline Is Painfully Obvious
Kerby Joseph posts workout @DetroitPodcast pic.twitter.com/a1AkhGeJGS
It has also been a year since the Lions were able to string together consecutive victories. The former NFL tight end expressed it was not ideal to be on a roller coaster and there were at times frustrations.
“Yeah. I mean, that's tough. You don't want to do this roller coaster. It can get frustrating. And inevitably, if we really want to be the team we need to be, that we need to be, we want to be, you've got to win back-to-back games. And you’ve got to do it more than once a year," said Campbell. "Every winning team I've been a part of, you start stacking wins and even after a loss, you'll stack a couple more.
"So, we've got to find that again, see if we can get these back-to-back wins. We're capable. We’ve just got to play 60 minutes of football, and we've got to play better than we did at Arizona. That's the truth, versus these guys. We're going to have to play a lot better and we can and we should.”

title: Lions Biggest Need Ahead of NFL Trade Deadline Is Painfully Obvious
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is growing closer, and as a result the Detroit Lions should be looking for ways to upgrade their roster.
Sitting at 3-2, the Lions are in position to make another push for a division title and playoff appearance after missing the postseason last year. However, their roster doesn't appear to be complete enough to make that push quite yet.
For general manager Brad Holmes, adding a player or two at the deadline would come with obvious benefits. In particular, Holmes should look to add talent in the secondary for the remainder of the season in an attempt to fortify the team's biggest area of weakness.
Detroit currently ranks last in the league in passing yards allowed per game, and have the fourth-worst passer rating against at 106.3. This has been the case despite the defense also ranking first in the league in sacks with 20.
For years, pass-rush was considered a major weakness for Detroit. However, through five games it has been one of their biggest strengths on defense. Now, the Lions need to find another option or two to help solidify their coverage attack.
Earlier in the year, the Lions were linked to Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. after he missed the start of the season amidst a contract dispute. However, they were outbid and ultimately missed the opportunity as Porter was dealt to the Dallas Cowboys.
There are several intriguing options who are expected to be available based on the start of the season across the league. In particular, the Indianapolis Colts, Los Angeles Chargers and Philadelphia Eagles are all off to slow starts and could theoretically be sellers come the Nov. 10 deadline.
Each of these teams has some intriguing options, including Los Angeles' Tarheeb Still, Cam Hart and Donte Jackson. Philadelphia has Riq Woolen, while the Colts could be open to a potential deal involving Sauce Gardner amidst their change in leadership after Chris Ballard was ousted as general manager.
The Lions need to add some depth to the cornerback room at the very least. D.J. Reed has not been the player that Detroit hoped he would be when they signed him to a three-year deal last offseason, as he has struggled against opposing team's top options.
Veteran Rock Ya-Sin entered the season as the second starter after the release of Terrion Arnold, but has lost his starting spot in favor of Roger McCreary. Ennis Rakestraw has also received some opportunities, but this area is Detroit's biggest detracting factor in their pursuit of the postseason.
Because of that, the Lions need to be active at the deadline and acquire an experienced option who fits their style and can give them consistency on the outside. Detroit could also look to add safety depth if Kerby Joseph isn't nearing a return by the time the deadline rolls around.
However, Detroit's safety room will get a big boost potentially as soon as this week with Brian Branch returning from an Achilles injury. If the Lions feel that one move is what they need, their efforts should be focused on adding a cornerback.

title: Detroit Lions Bring Back Rookie DL, Cut DL Chris Smith
full_text:
The Detroit Lions announced a pair of practice squad roster moves early in the week ahead of their first divisional contest of the 2026 NFL regular season.
After visiting for a workout earlier this week, defensive lineman Aidan Keanaaina was brought back to the practice squad. In a corresponding move, defensive tackle Chris Smith was cut.
Keanaaina played collegiately at Notre Dame and for the California Golden Bears. In his last two years,  he secured101 tackles, 2.5 sacks and five tackles for loss.
He went undrafted and landed in Motown for his first NFL training camp. Unfortunately, he suffered an undisclosed injury and was waived in the middle of August with an injury settlement.
Lions team reporter Tim Twentyman expressed excitement about observing the 6'3, 320-pound defensive lineman during training camp, prior to his injury and subsequent release.
"One player I'm looking forward to watching a little closer once the pads come on Monday is rookie defensive lineman Aidan Keanaaina out of California," Twentyman wrote. "He's had some nice interior rushes early in camp and has worked his way into some second-team reps. Detroit's looking for depth and playmakers along the interior, especially at nose tackle. He had 101 tackles his last two years at Cal in that role. That's a lot of tackle production from the position."
Additional Lions NFL Insider Analysis: Mike Valenti Shares Bold Opinion After Brad Holmes Does Not Land CB Joey Porter Jr.
Smith has been a player that has bounced around from the active roster and the practice squad since he joined the team in 2023 as an undrafted rookie free agent. He did not make the 53-man roster this year coming out of training camp, but signed to the practice squad quickly after getting cut.
The 26-year-old had a solid preseason performance against the Bengals, drawing praise from head coach Dan Campbell.
The former NFL tight end expressed Smith does a lot of the little things correctly and is a disciplined player.
“He doesn’t make the same mistake twice," said Campbell. "He’s the guy you love to coach because he’s up here all offseason, works his tail off, is always trying to hone his game. He plays disciplined football.”

title: Lions Announce Week 7 Uniforms: How They Have Fared
full_text:
The Detroit Lions return to action this week against the Green Bay Packers, and will be wearing their all-black uniforms for the divisional tilt.
It'll be the first time Dan Campbell's squad dons the alternate uniforms this season and the seventh time overall.
Billed as the “Motor City Muscle” jersey combo, the uniform made its debut in 2024, and features a black jersey, black pants, and a blue helmet with the black Lions logo.
Detroit won its first ever game in the jersey in Week 4 of the 2024 season, defeating the Seattle Seahawks, 42-29, at Ford Field. The Lions weren't as lucky in their second go-round with the unis, however, losing to Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills in a Week 15 contest, 48-42. It marked the Lions’ second and final loss of the ‘24 regular season.
Campbell & Co. proceeded to finish the aforementioned campaign with a 2-1 record in the all-black jerseys. Meanwhile, in 2025, Detroit also recorded a 2-1 mark in the retro uniforms. The lone loss for the Lions in the all-blacks last season came against the Minnesota Vikings on Christmas Day.
In Detroit's upcoming Week 7 matchup with Green Bay, it will face a Packers team which has won three straight games. Jordan Love & Co. beat Dak Prescott and the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday night for their most recent win, improving to 4-2 on the season.
The Packers are playing like one of the best teams in football right now, and arguably will be even stronger a week from now due to the return of running back Josh Jacobs.
Jacobs, who has missed the season's first six games while serving time on the commissioner exempt list, will suit up for the first time in 2026 next Sunday against the Lions.
Having Jacobs back should provide a major boost to Green Bay's run game, which has basically been nonexistent through the season's first six weeks. For example, the Packers’ top back in Week 6 was Pierre Strong Jr., who accumulated just 28 yards on 11 carries.
The Lions will square off with Jacobs and Green Bay in their all-black uniforms Sunday at 4:25 p.m. (EST) at Ford Field.

title: Mike Valenti Shares Bold Feelings About Lions Not Landing Joey Porter Jr.
full_text:
The Detroit Lions were not able to land one of the top available cornerbacks and frustrations are mounting, as Kelvin Sheppard's pass defense is the worst in the National Football League.
Among the critics of general manager Brad Holmes not being able to land a player that would significantly upgrade the defense is 97.1 The Ticket sports talk radio host Mike Valenti.
He expressed his views earlier this week after witnessing Porter Jr. perform well in coverage against Packers wideout Christian Watson.
"Man, you really f'd up not getting Joey Porter Jr. Watching last night really encapsulates it," said Valenti. "And again, I think the dimwitted take would be, 'Well, Dallas isn't winning.' Their defense didn't cost them that game last night. Joey Porter Jr. locked up on Christian Watson, who's been a top five receiver this year. That's a big player. That's a 6'3, tall, rangy, big-bodied receiver. Porter was tasked with playing Watson most of the night with no help.
"Watson had his quietest game of the year. Multiple PBU's. Yes, there was one penalty, but Joey Porter Jr., they were helping everyone else, not him."
Additional Lions NFL Insider Analysis: Packers Enter Week 7 With Josh Jacobs, Without Micah Parsons
Against the Cowboys, Watson secured only three receptions for 64 yards, below his season average entering the Week 5 contest.
"You put that guy on this Lions defense, allowing D.J. Reed to have help. Man, what a difference it would make. You really f'd up," Valenti said. "That was the guy. That's the best corner that's going to get dealt. That's the guy. And you saw it living color last night. You did not lose that game because Joey Porter Jr. got dusted. They didn't. And again, a corner can only do so much. The pieces have to work together. The two games he's played for the Cowboys, I think he had poopy pants last week. He had to leave the game sick. He's been excellent. You f'd up."
It has been a completely smooth transition for the former Steelers defender. An illness forced him to miss a game already for the NFC East squad.
"I really just couldn't hold anything down," he said, via the Cowboys team website . "You know, I just kept throwing up. I try to fight through. I tried to take a nap before the game, just to shake it off, but I just couldn't hold in deep down. So, that's when they made the call to send me home."
Despite his best efforts to attempt to play, he was unable to suit up against the Buccaneers.
"On my way to the game, I was throwing up outside of my Uber," Porter explained. "It was brutal. I'm not gonna lie. You go into the week thinking you're gonna get more of a workload, and you're ready to go, and then that's ultimately what doesn't happen. It was very frustrating . I was prepared to play all week. My mindset was on playing, the mindset was to get the dub, and obviously I didn't get to do that, and we didn't get the dub. I was pretty pissed."

title: Lions 2026 Playoff Standings Update: Divisional Showdowns Loom Large
full_text:
The Detroit Lions are exiting their bye week and entering into what could be a season-defining set of games.
Through the first six weeks of the NFL season, the NFC North is looking like one of the toughest divisions in football yet again. It's one of only two divisions in football where every team has a winning record, with the other being the AFC North.
Because of the heightened levels of competition, every week is an urgent one for all four teams including the Lions. This is especially true for Detroit in its upcoming two games , as they will play their first two divisional games of the season.
Both games will be at home, which will be a big boost for a team that has had lots of success in its two games in front of their home crowd. This could be a big advantage as these two games against the Packers (Week 7) and Vikings (Week 8) could be season-defining for a team looking to win its third division crown in four years.
Green Bay has won two games in a row after a tough start, and are getting running back Josh Jacobs back at running back after being taken off the Commissioner's Exempt List. Additionally, quarterback Jordan Love appears to be rounding into form and his connection with wide receiver Christian Watson has been dangerous for opposing defenses.
After that, the Lions will take on the undefeated Minnesota Vikings, who would enter that matchup 6-0 if they defeat the Indianapolis Colts this upcoming week. Through five games the Vikings' defense, led by wunderkind coordinator Brian Flores, has allowed just 64 total points.
Because of how competitive the division is, the Lions must at least take one of the two in theory to remain in the mix for the division title. With the NFC East and West divisions off to slow starts, the North could send multiple teams to the playoffs and as a result a Wild Card spot would still be within reach even if Detroit falls to 3-4.
However, the Lions under Dan Campbell have always held a home playoff game in high regard, and the only way to earn one would be to win their division. As a result, these games will hold the utmost value moving forward.
Currently, the Lions hold the seventh and final playoff spot in the NFC through six weeks. Seattle is right behind them at 3-3, as they haven't had their bye week. Beyond them, the Atlanta Falcons, New Orleans Saints, Philadelphia Eagles, Dallas Cowboys, Arizona Cardinals and Los Angeles Rams are all 2-4.
Detroit will have another big stretch with games against all three of their divisional foes within a four-game stretch to end the year, with all three of those being road contests. By winning these two upcoming matchups, it puts them in an advantageous positions for those late-season tilts.
Here is an updated look at the NFC North and NFC playoff standings after six weeks of the 2026 NFL season.
1.) Minnesota Vikings (5-0). 2.) Green Bay Packers (4-2). 3.) Chicago Bears (4-2). 4.) Detroit Lions (3-2).

title: Lions Trade Deadline Big Board: Realistic Targets Ranked by Fit and Cost With Four Weeks Left
full_text:
The Detroit Lions are looking to win a third NFC North title in four years.
After missing the playoffs last season, Dan Campbell's team has started 3-2 in 2026. Coming off their bye week, they have big divisional matchups against the Green Bay Packers and Minnesota Vikings in their next two weeks.
The Lions have had some success, but their defense remains a detracting factor as far as their long-term viability. They will have an opportunity to add talent in this area ahead of the trade deadline, which is set for Nov. 10, and doing so in the defensive backfield appears to be the best path forward.
For general manager Brad Holmes , there are multiple intriguing options that could be available after the first six weeks of the season.
Here is a list of candidates that could be intriguing trade targets at the Lions' biggest area of need with less than a month remaining until the trade deadline.
1.) Philadelphia Eagles CB Riq Woolen
Woolen signed a one-year deal with the Eagles this offseason after a strong start to his career in Seattle. However, with the Eagles now sitting at 2-4 and quarterback Jalen Hurts on injured reserve, things are trending down and as a result they could wind up being sellers.
While he doesn't have the flashiest numbers in his six games to start the year, Woolen is a veteran who won the Super Bowl last year in Seattle. He's also a rental, so the price to acquire him shouldn't be astronomical.
2.) Kansas City Chiefs CB Kristian Fulton
Fulton is a player who has been linked to the Lions for several weeks. In the final year of his current deal with the Chiefs, he's part of a logjam at cornerback in Kansas City that features veteran L'Jarius Sneed and first-round pick Mansoor Delane.
Because of their depth, the Chiefs could view Fulton as expendable despite their undefeated start to the season. He would instantly slot in as Detroit's second-best option behind D.J. Reed, giving the Lions another solid veteran option.
3.) Tampa Bay Buccaneers CB Zyon McCollum
Tampa Bay has had a difficult start to the season, now sitting at 1-5 after an overtime loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers. As a result, they could look to deal some of their expensive options that have some value such as McCollum.
It wouldn't be a cheap add for the Lions, as McCollum is under contract through the end of the 2028 season as part of a three-year, $48 million contract extension. The Lions still want to get deals done with Sam LaPorta and Brian Branch, so adding another big contract to the books through trade may create some challenges.
4.) Los Angeles Chargers CB Donte Jackson
Jackson has missed the last two games due to a hamstring injury. However, he's a veteran journeyman who has experience in different schemes, and if healthy would be a worthwhile addition for the Lions.
The Chargers have sputtered out of the gate to an 0-6 start, and so the Lions could also inquire about defensive backs Tarheeb Still and Cam Hart. Jackson, a veteran who is in the final year of his contract, is the most likely of the group to be available.
5.) Philadelphia Eagles CB Kelee Ringo
Ringo would be a buy-low option for Detroit in the event that other top targets go off the board. He has played almost exclusively on special teams this year, and hasn't had much in terms of proven defensive production throughout his career in Philadelphia.
This is a player that was billed as one of the top corners in the 2023 draft at one time, and perhaps the Lions could get some value out of making a deal and giving him an opportunity. He'd be another rental option, and might be best as a supplemental addition.
1.) Arizona Cardinals S Budda Baker
The Lions just got an up-close look at Baker last week in their win over the Arizona Cardinals. In that game, Baker started the game with a big play as he timed up a blitz perfectly to sack Jared Goff.
Baker's credentials are among the best of any player expected to be available. He's an eight-time Pro Bowl selection and a two-time First Team All-Pro, and would bring some serious versatility to Detroit's secondary.
He's under contract through next season, which would give the Lions some stability moving forward or an opportunity to create some cap space if they don't see a benefit of keeping him into next year.
2.) Atlanta Falcons S Jessie Bates
Bates is in the final year of his contract with the Falcons. Atlanta is still in the mix in the NFC South, even at 2-4, but could look to be sellers at the deadline in an effort to add some draft capital. He doesn't have an interception this year, but has notched 27 total across his career.
With the uncertainty surrounding Kerby Joseph, Bates is a proven takeaway generator who could give the defense a spark.
3.) Tennessee Titans S Amani Hooker
Hooker signed an extension prior to last season, and is under contract through the 2028 season. The Titans are sputtering at 1-5, and he could wind up being one of their most valuable trade pieces as they look to rebuild in Robert Saleh's first year as head coach.
He's another option the Lions could look to to fill Joseph's void, or at the very least supplement their depth at safety.

title: Packers-Lions Matchups: Just One Advantage, But It’s Huge
full_text:
The Green Bay Packers have won three games in a row. As fictional manager Lou Brown from Major League II once said, that’s called a winning streak.
Can the Packers extend their streak to four? They will face a big challenge in Detroit against the Lions at 3:25 p.m. Sunday. It will be the first of five consecutive games against teams that would qualify for the playoffs if the season were to end today.
The Packers swept the Lions last season, including a 31-24 in Detroit on Thanksgiving. The teams are different now. Some key players are back. Others are on the shelf due to injuries. The Lions are coming off their bye week, while the Packers played Dallas on Sunday night.
While the Lions have the rest advantage, who has the advantage on the field? We go through that in our weekly matchups.
The talking point last week was that the Packers were playing well on defense but that they had not faced a real quarterback.
Now they have, and the Packers beat up Dak Prescott on Sunday night. This week? They’ll face another high-powered offense with a quarterback who has been mostly flawless this season.
Jared Goff does not get the league-wide respect that he deserves, but he’s been nothing short of excellent since coming to Detroit.
This year has been no different. He has completed 67 percent of his passes. His passer rating is 111.3. He’s thrown 12 touchdown passes and has yet to be picked off.
Perhaps Detroit’s offense was summed up best by Green Bay defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon.
“They’ve scored 30 any time they’ve touched the grass,” Gannon said on Tuesday .
Four out of five games but, with a second-ranked 32.8 points per game, close enough. Detroit’s offense is dangerous. They’re loaded with weapons. Receivers Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams and tight end Sam LaPorta can all hurt the defense in different ways.
Last week, the Packers handled their matchup against George Pickens and CeeDee Lamb well. This group is deeper, and more dangerous.
The key to slowing down the Lions is pressuring Goff. The Packers beat him up last year at Lambeau Field and held the Lions to 13 points.
Can the Packers get enough pressure? Will Gannon have another masterclass up his sleeve?
As good as Green Bay’s defense has played early in the season, this matchup is closer than you would think at first glance.
Jonathan Gannon was asked what makes Jahmyr Gibbs, Jahmyr Gibbs. He sighed, before saying, “Woah.”
Gibbs is the fastest player on the field every week that he steps on it. He’s a dominant force in a Detroit ground game that remains its identity even with the loss of some of the personnel that made it such a powerful unit in 2024.
Green Bay’s run defense has truly only struggled once this season. The problem? That came against the Falcons, who employ a back with a similar running style to that of Gibbs. There’s an argument to be made that Gibbs is a better running back than Bijan Robinson, but it’s those two at the top of the league with everyone else fighting for a seat at the table.
Either way, Gibbs makes this group go.
The Packers did a good job against him last year. Gibbs was held to 19 yards on nine carries at Lambeau Field. He added 10 catches for 31 yards. If the Packers can hold him to 50 yards on 19 touches, they’d be thrilled.
In the rematch at Ford Field, Gibbs was more productive, but not up to his usual standard. He touched the ball 20 times for 86 yards. The Packers held him in check, but will be missing both linebackers from those games. Quay Walker is playing in Las Vegas while Edgerrin Cooper is rehabbing a torn Achilles.
Regardless, Gibbs’ excellence and the Packers’ recent history against a back of his caliber gives the nod to Detroit.
The Lions can make things difficult with their pass rush. Their front boasts two really good players in defensive tackle Alim McNeil and defensive end Aidan Hutchinson. D.J. Wonnum is sixth in the lead with five sacks. Hutchinson has four and McNeill has 3.5.
Added together, the Lions lead the league in sacks – even while playing one less game than most teams.
So, why does their defense stink?
Once the ball goes in the air, the Lions have had significant problems. Their defensive backfield was in flux before the season even began. Their once elite safety tandem of Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph have missed the entirety of the season with injuries. Following last year’s torn ACL,, Branch is likely to return this week, which should give them a boost.
The cornerback spot has been an issue. D.J. Reed has not worked out as a free agent signing, and they’ve been struggling to find someone to give them consistency. Keith Abney is the only cornerback with an interception.
That’s good news for the Packers as they come in rolling. Jordan Love’s stats won’t show how well he played on Sunday against the Cowboys, but he was three drops away from throwing four touchdown passes.
Matthew Golden has back-to-back 100-yard receiving games, the first for the Packers since Davante Adams, and is turning into a star. Will the Packers be able to protect Love long enough to exploit a leaky pass defense? That’s the million-dollar question.
With the advantages Green Bay has, especially at quarterback, where Love has thrived almost regardless of the situation, the nod here goes to the visiting team.
Green Bay’s run game stinks. If there was any doubt about that, Sunday’s results against the Cowboys, who were 32nd in the league against the run, should have answered any remaining questions.
As has been the case all season, the Packers were terrible on the ground. Their leading rusher was Pierre Strong. He had 28 yards on 11 carries. Their starting running back was MarShawn Lloyd. He had negative yards rushing at halftime and finished with 10 yards on eight carries.
Their most efficient runner was Savion Williams, and those runs were on plays in which Jordan Love threw the ball behind the line of scrimmage.
They could be getting a boost this week. Josh Jacobs is off the commissioner’s exempt list, and looks to be on track to play this Sunday. How much can he play? He can help, but how much?  Those are questions we don’t know the answers to yet.
Until we know, it’s impossible to give the Packers the edge, against any opponent, let alone one that has been a decent 13th in rushing yards allowed per game and 12th in yards per carry.
From a special teams perspective, the Lions have some stability at kicker and punter. Jake Bates has been perfect on field goals this season and Jack Fox is averaging 47.2 yards per punt.
There is a slight transition in their return game with Tom Kennedy taking over for Kalif Raymond, who joined Ben Johnson in Chicago.
Green Bay’s special teams entered the Dallas game struggling. Trey Smack missed three kicks against Chicago and Skyy Moore is missing from their return game due to a high-ankle sprain that landed him on injured reserve.
Coleman Owen was elevated from the practice squad last week to return punts in Moore’s place while J. Michael Sturdivant and Bo Melton returned kickoffs. Neither did much to stand out, but they protected the football. Matt LaFleur noted that he thought Owen did a nice job returning punts other than calling for a fair catch inside the 10. He will likely be elevated again this week.
Smack shook off some struggles against Chicago with a 5-for-5 night against the Cowboys. This game is in a dome, which should remove the degree of difficulty for kickers to some degree. Having said that, two of the worst games of Mason Crosby’s career came at Ford Field.
Detroit’s excellence at kicker and punter and its strong coverage units give them the nod.

title: Coordinators Detail Huge Challenge Packers Will Face at Lions
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers have gotten their season back on track. They will take a three-game winning streak into Sunday’s game at the Detroit Lions.
It will be one of their biggest tests of the season.
The Lions, who were the back-to-back NFC North champions in 2023 and 2024, are 3-2. They are 2-0 in home games this season and 20-7 at Ford Field dating to the start of the 2023 campaign. They are coming off their bye week, giving them a tremendous scheduling advantage . Home teams coming out of a bye are 53-34 since the start of the 2021 season.
And then, there’s the talent. The Lions have as much top-end talent as any team in the league. Especially on offense.
Here’s a closer look through the words of Green Bay’s three coordinators.
A week after Jonathan Gannon’s defense shut down the high-powered Cowboys on Sunday night, his unit will face an even bigger challenge against the Lions. Like Dallas, the Cowboys have a great quarterback (Jared Goff), great receivers (Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams), an impact tight end (Sam LaPorta) and a strong offensive line.
Unlike the Cowboys, the Lions have a cream-of-the-crop running back in Jahmyr Gibbs.
“Woo,” Gannon said when asked about Gibbs.
“He’s faster than everybody,” Gannon said. Plus, he can cut – especially at Ford Field – and he’s got “really good contact balance” and he “breaks a lot of tackles.”
Gibbs trails only the Chiefs’ Kenneth Walker with 149.4 scrimmage yards per game. He has three games of more than 160 total yards and he’s scored in every game.
As usual, Goff ranks among the league leaders in passer rating. He’s second at 111.3 on the strength of 12 touchdowns, zero interceptions and 67.0 percent accuracy.
Even while playing one fewer game than most players, St. Brown is seventh with 37 receptions and tied for third with five touchdowns. Williams has elite speed, making him a game-breaking threat.
Detroit’s offensive coordinator is Drew Petzing, who was Arizona’s coordinator under Gannon the previous three seasons.
“There's no tendencies,” Gannon said. “He's creative as all get out. He uses his playmakers in a way to showcase their talents. The quarterback does an excellent job of getting them in the right place to put you as a defense at a disadvantage. When you want to be aggressive, he burns you. When you want to be safe, he burns you.”
A calling card of Gannon’s defense has been its swarming play style. The Lions will match their intensity.
“They play hard,” Gannon continued. “They are tough, they play hard, they’re physical. That comes from the head coach and then the coordinator and then the position coaches. Hank Fraley, their O-line coach/run-game coordinator, this O-line is souped up now. They’ve got good players, they collectively play well together, they communicate, they never bust, their protection scheme is on point. And then they can run it to win and they can throw it to win.”
When Gannon said the Lions have scored 30 points “every time they’ve touched the grass,” he is only slightly wrong. They scored at least 31 points in four games (and 26 in the other).
They enter Week 7 ranked fourth in total offense and second in scoring, even though they are a woeful 22nd on third down.
On the other hand, Detroit’s defense is horrendous. It ranks 30th in points allowed per game, just 0.1 points per game better than the Cardinals and Saints. They are last in total defense and passing defense, and 30th or worse in third down, fourth down, red zone and goal-to-go.
However, they do rush the passer with D.J. Wonnum (five sacks) and superstar Aidan Hutchinson (four). Detroit’s front will challenge Green Bay’s biggest weakness, which has been its offensive line.
Plus, star Lions safety Brian Branch is expected to make his season debut following last year’s torn Achilles.
Embattled Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard remains on the job. He will have had the bye week to find some answers.
“The one thing about these guys is we’ve got to be ready for everything,” offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich said. “They bring a lot of different fronts. They bring a lot of different pressures. I think their D-line is really good. Obviously, Hutchinson and [defensive tackle Alim] McNeill are excellent players, Wonnum’s got a lot of sacks, so they’re playing really well up front. Their linebackers are athletic and aggressive.
“So that’s one thing, their front’s salty so we’ve got to make sure we do a nice job of handling those guys because it’s going to be a tall task for sure.”
Detroit’s is going to make life difficult for a Packers return game that lost its excellent returner, Skyy Moore, to an ankle injury.
Punter Jack Fox ranks ninth with a 43.3-yard net average this season and led the league in 2024.
“He’s very, very talented,” Achord said. “I think he’s got one of the bigger legs in the league, high, high hang times, and that allows the coverage units to get down there. Anytime you’re putting the ball 4.8s, 4.7s up there plus, it allows the gunners outside to factor.”
Plus, their interior players are tough. Added together, the Lions are 11th in punt coverage and seventh in kickoff coverage. They are one of six teams in the top 11 in both categories.
“They’re playing physical, they’re strong,” Achord said. “They do a really good job condensing it and squeezing to the ball. Our guys have to do a good job standing up to their size and physical presence out there.
“So, it’s going to be a great challenge. They are one of the top teams in coverage, in both phases, so I think it’s a really good challenge for our guys, and it’s something we’ll look forward to this week, being able to stand up to those guys.”

title: Consensus NFL Power Rankings for Week 7: Packers’ Astounding Rise Continues
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – After a blowout loss to the Falcons and uninspiring victory over the Buccaneers, the Green Bay Packers fell all the way to 24th in the Packers On SI Consensus NFL Power Rankings.
What a difference two weeks make.
First, what are our Consensus Power Rankings? We take eight sets of national power rankings and turn them into one more-powerful-than-a-locomotive power ranking.
After beating the Bears, the Packers rose to 14th . Now, after a convincing win over the Cowboys on Sunday night, they’ve moved up to 12th.
Here’s a closer look, with more extensive analysis and the full rankings available at the links.
Conor Orr could hardly be more bullish on the Packers as he moved them up eight spots from No. 12.
“With Micah Parsons en route at some point and the defense having posted back-to-back weeks of all-out swarming, the mood has shifted demonstrably in Green Bay,” Orr said. “The Jordan Love MVP conversation will soon round into shape. “
The Packers are up two spots in Mike Florio’s rankings. As he wrote, “They’re getting Josh Jacobs back at a perfect time.”
The Packers are up three spots in ESPN’s rankings , which are selected by its team beat writers.
This week’s theme is the ineffective running game, which is the worst in the league by a wide margin. As noted by Rob Demovsky, “MarShawn Lloyd, who missed most of the past two seasons because of injuries, is finally healthy but has averaged just 1.27 yards after contact -- 42nd among 43 qualified running backs. Kaleb Johnson has Green Bay's longest run of the season at 31 yards, but he has fumbled twice and barely played the past two weeks.”
Pete Prisco inched the Packers up two spots in his rankings.
“We knew the offense will get it going with the explosive passing game,” he wrote, “but it's the improved defense that has turned their season around. That unit will be tested on the road this week against the Lions.”
The Packers moved up one spot by Chad Graff and Josh Kendall in their rankings.
This week’s theme is fantasy football. They chose receiver Matthew Golden, noting: “Golden has been over 20 points in three of the last four games, and since Week 3, he is seventh in the league in receiving yards (348), just 2 shy of teammate Christian Watson. All three of Golden’s career 100-yard games have come in the last month.”
The Packers zoomed up eight spots from No. 22 in Ralph Vacchiano’s rankings.
He noted how coach Matt LaFleur was perhaps on the hot seat after a 1-2 start. Now, they’ve won three in a row.
“Jordan Love and the offense has clicked in that span, and the defense has been excellent, too,” he wrote. “So, why are they ranked this low? Because they barely beat the Bucs, they beat the Bears without Caleb Williams and then beat the reeling Cowboys. They can’t do anything about the schedule, but let’s see how it goes at Detroit, vs. Carolina, at New England and vs. Minnesota in the month leading into their bye week before I put my cheesehead on.”
The Packers moved up four spots in Frank Schwab’s rankings. He mentioned the Packers as one of the teams that are “impossible” to rank or figure out based on their performances during the first four games compared to their last two.
“Then the last two weeks, the Packers blew out the Bears and Cowboys, and are suddenly 4-2 and on a roll,” he said. “Had you just watched the last two games and nothing else, you'd think the Packers might be a top-five team at worst. But the first four weeks did happen too. The Packers still struggle mightily to run the ball and to protect Love, though the QB was masterful against pressure on Sunday night. Green Bay, like many other teams this season, is hard to figure out.”
The Packers gained one spot in Nick Shook’s rankings. The Packers’ defensive success against Chicago wasn’t a fluke, Shook said.
“Green Bay shut down Dallas’ explosive offense, making life miserable for Dak Prescott and Co., while Jordan Love and the offense did enough early to cruise to a victory. There are still kinks to work out offensively (which could be solved quickly if Josh Jacobs can get off to a fast start upon returning), but it’s time to start taking this team seriously.”
The Lions will host the Packers at noon Sunday at Ford Field. They are our 13th ranked team, or just one spot behind Green Bay, with individual rankings ranging from No. 9 at The Athletic to No. 18 at Pro Football Talk.
Sports Illustrated’s Conor Orr has them at No. 11.
“The Packers and Vikings are next on Detroit’s post-bye schedule. We’ll find out immediately if the defense was fixed, has the potential to be fixed, or if Jared Goff is going to continue needing to score 30-plus a week to keep the Lions in the conversation.”
Fox’s Ralph Vacchiano was surprised the Lions didn’t change defensive coordinators during their bye. They are giving up 404.4 yards per game, almost 20 yards worse than any other team. Opponents have eclipsed 440 yards and 30 points in three games.
“It’s a shame, really, because the Lions offense can run up the score on any team in the league, but the defense is going to kill them,” Vacchiano wrote. “Teams rarely last in the NFL when their only hope is to win 41-38 while praying they get the ball last.”
Sportsbook odds aren’t part of our rankings, but they do provide another useful perspective on how teams are viewed. In Packers-related odds at FanDuel Sportsbook :
The Packers, who were +2000 to win the Super Bowl before Week 1, plunged to +6000 after losing to the Falcons and stayed there after beating Tampa Bay and Chicago. Now, they’re +3000, though that still ranks only 15th.
Among NFC North teams, the Bears are +1400 and the Lions and Vikings +2000.
Green Bay opened the season ranked seventh in the NFC playoff odds at -112, fell to as low as 12th at +250 after the win at Tampa Bay, but are back to -118. They rank seventh in the NFC and last among the NFC North teams (Minnesota is -500, Chicago is -230 and Detroit is -188).
Quarterback Jordan Love opened at +2200 to win NFL MVP. He bottomed out at +10000 but is right back in the thick of the race, with his +3300 ranking ninth. Buffalo’s Josh Allen (+175) and San Francisco’s Brock Purdy (+250) are the clear front-runners.
In the NFC North odds at DraftKings, the Packers are still considered the long shots. Minnesota is +105, followed by Detroit and Chicago at +350 and Green Bay at +530.

title: No. 8 Is Coming Back; Eight Reasons Why Josh Jacobs Must Save Run Game
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs will get a “full week of practice” this week and could play at the Detroit Lions on Sunday, coach Matt LaFleur said on Monday.
Goodness knows, they need him.
Jacobs spent the first six games of the season on the exempt list following an off-the-field incident with a female over Memorial Day Weekend. He was removed from the exempt list on Monday but isn’t necessarily in the clear.
While Jacobs hasn’t practiced since the end of training camp, he’s been working out with the training staff and participating in team meetings, so he shouldn’t need a ramp-up like a player coming off a significant injury.
“Well, that’s to be determined,” LaFleur said of Jacobs’ readiness. “We feel like he’s in a pretty good spot. He’s been training, but he’s missed the exposure to football.”
The Packers don’t just need Jacobs. They desperately need him. Just look at the numbers.
Green Bay’s rushing attack is the worst in the NFL by a considerable margin. Here are eight statistics that show the complete ineptitude.
One: The Packers are 32nd in the NFL with 59.8 rushing yards per game and 2.87 yards per carry. They are last in both categories by considerable margins: 16.2 yards per game behind Dallas and 0.14 yards per carry behind the Raiders.
The Chargers in 2000 averaged a record-low 66.4 rushing yards per game.
Two: The Packers’ best rushing day this season was their 86 yards against Tampa Bay in Week 4. There have been 45 individual games of more than 86 rushing yards this season.
The Packers’ best rushing day in terms of efficiency was their 3.5 yards per carry against the Jets in Week 2. That best day would rank 30th in the NFL over the course of the season.
Three: On first-down running plays, the Packers are averaging a worst-in-the-league 2.25 yards per carry. The Raiders are 31st with a 2.81-yard average. A total of 26 teams are averaging at least one more yard per carry. Against Dallas, the Packers’ first-down average plunged to 1.47 yards per carry.
Four: Yards before contact can be an offensive line stat, but it obviously can be swayed by a player’s ability to get through a hole or make someone miss. According to Stathead, the Packers have a league-low 239 yards before contact. Their 1.9-yard average is 31st.
With Jacobs, the Packers were 26th with 2.2 yards before contact per carry in 2025 and 17th with 2.4 yards before contact per carry in 2024.
Five: Yards after contact is almost totally a running back stat, though speed through a hole and getting to the second level with the offensive line matters. The Packers are last with 120 yards after contact and 31st with 1.0 yards after contract per carry, according to Stathead.
With Jacobs, the Packers were 13th with 1.9 yards after contact per carry in 2025 and third with 2.4 yards after contact per carry in 2024.
Six: Green Bay’s rushing success this season is 34.3 percent, which ranks 30th. A “successful” play gains at least 40 percent of the required yards on first down (a 4-yard run on first-and-10 would be a success), 60 percent of the required yards on second down and 100 percent of the required yards on third and fourth down. Jacobs had individual success rates of 52.2 percent in 2024 and 49.1 percent in 2025.
Seven: A “stuff” is a run that gains 0 yards or worse. The Packers are 31st in stuff percentage, with a drive-killing 29.0 percent of their runs failing to gain yardage. With Jacobs, the Packers ranked second in stuff percentage in 2024 (17.6) and 12th in 2025 (19.3).
Eight: MarShawn Lloyd leads the Packers with 122 rushing yards. That’s a 17-game pace of 346 yards. That projected total would rank 16th in the league through Week 6.
Lloyd is averaging 2.54 yards per carry. It would require him to carry the ball 394 times to reach 1,000 yards. That would be the seventh-most rushing attempts in NFL history.
So, Jacobs could be a season-changing addition. The Packers have won three games in a row with no running game whatsoever.
“Well, I think he’s an elite-level back,” LaFleur said. “He’s certainly not going to hurt it. I think he can provide a spark.”
Is it the backs? Is it the blocking? LaFleur deflected the blame when asked about the running game on Monday, instead choosing to credit the Cowboys, who had the worst run defense in the NFL entering Week 6 but were coming off their mini-bye.
“I think there were some moments where it was good and then there were some moments where it wasn’t as good,” he said. “And then there were some moments where, quite frankly, the concepts had no chance based on different front structures they were presenting to us.
“They did a good job. I think any time that you go into a game and the opposition has a little longer to prepare for that, I think there’s some unscouted looks that can come up. Certainly, they caught us in a couple of those looks, where we didn’t have good plays for what they were showing.”
The Packers will play at the Lions on Sunday. They rank 20th in rushing yards allowed per attempt and 15th in rushing yards allowed per game. Then, they’ll host the Panthers, who are last in the league in yards allowed per attempt. Back-to-back games against the Patriots and Vikings, who boast top-10 run defenses, will follow.
Jacobs, even if it’s turning runs blocked for 1 yard into gains of 3 yards, could be a season-changing addition, perhaps as soon as Sunday.
“Yeah, absolutely,” LaFleur said when asked if Jacobs can hit the ground running. “I think that’s possible but we’ve got to go through the week and see where he’s at.”

title: New Packers Defensive Tackle Will Have Micah Parsons’ Seal of Approval
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – There might be nobody happier about the Green Bay Packers’ decision to sign Mazi Smith to the practice squad on Monday than his former-turned-current teammate, Micah Parsons.
As reported by ESPN.com’s Rob Demovsky , the Packers signed Smith to the practice squad following a Monday workout.
“Let’s go!” Parsons screamed when the Cowboys drafted Smith in the first round in 2023.
Parsons with the Packers has been the hype man for Lukas Van Ness, among others. He was the same way with Smith during their time together. More on that in a moment.
“NO MORE QB SNEAKS AJ!” @MicahhParsons11 told Cowboys DC Dan Quinn to pick Michigan's Mazi Smith earlier today and IT HAPPENED 😂 pic.twitter.com/nGm62CAnDK
Smith was a bust for the Cowboys and represents a Hail Mary of sorts for the Packers on a talented player who could fill a need. The Packers have been hammered by injuries at defensive tackle, with Warren Brinson, Javon Hargrave and Jonathan Ford on injured reserve. They beat the Cowboys with only four defensive tackles on the active roster. Plus, they have only one player on the practice squad, undrafted rookie David Blay Jr.
So, maybe the Packers will catch lightning in a bottle with Smith, who was the 26th pick of the 2023 draft.
"It's like Christmas," then-Cowboys coach Mike McCarthy said after Smith was selected. “When you look at all the work that goes into it, going back to his 30 visit, and just what a great fit he is for us … I just want him to be himself. He is a great fit for us.”
During the predraft process, Smith gained a big supporter in Parsons. He even texted his defensive coordinator at the time, Dan Quinn, hoping the Cowboys would draft Smith.
“It’s not what I think he can be, it’s what Mazi has to be,” Parsons said at the start of training camp in 2024 . “When you get to this business, there is no more of a choice or a can, it’s either you will or you won’t. They usually try to find someone else to do it if you can’t. It’s what Mazi has to be. He has to be dominant. He has to be a force. He has to be that guy for us.
“That’s why they drafted him in the first round. You’re not getting drafted in the first round not to be a productive talent, not to be on the sidelines. We drafted him to be in the game and that’s how much confidence you have (to have). I don’t expect Mazi to do anything. It’s what Mazi has to do at this point.
“That’s why I’m in his corner, I’m rooting for him and hoping to get him better every day. Pushing his conditioning, pushing his limits, because we need Mazi to be strong. We need Mazi to be that great force. He can be a dominant player, it’s just a will and mindset. That’s why we’re all here.”
Responded Smith : “I don’t really set goals. Everybody want to be an All-Pro, everybody wants to be a top five. I want to be the best me I can be and I know what that can get me. It’s got to this point so, I ain’t worried about accolades or that type.”
Smith played in 17 games with three starts as a rookie and started all 17 games in 2024, when he set career highs with 41 tackles and four tackles for losses.
“You can see it in his face that he loves ball, he loves everything about it,” Cowboys executive vice president and director of player personnel Stephen Jones said. “All the coaches that met with him agree that he'd be a great fit in this organization, and for him to fall down there to us and for us to have the opportunity to pick him, I feel like Mike. I feel like it's Christmas."
Last year, the Cowboys traded him to the Jets in the midseason blockbuster for Quinnen Williams, so he played in a total of eight games between the teams. He failed to make the Jets’ roster in training camp this year and signed to the Dolphins’ practice squad. He played in one game with Miami and was released last week.
Added together, Smith is in his fourth season. He’s played in 43 games with 20 starts. He has 57 tackles, including two sacks and seven for losses.
“I'm excited to get pointed in the right direction," he said after he was drafted, a quote that perhaps fits today. “To climb this big ole' mountain, they'll tell me where to start. I'm excited to get into the heavy duty [part] of things. I'm ready to put this work in and feel what my first offensive lineman feels like in the NFL.”
The native of Grand Rapids, Mich., was a consensus first-team all-Big Ten selection at Michigan in 2022, when he was the Wolverines’ defensive player of the year with 48 tackles in 14 games.
He was the No. 1 player on Bruce Feldman’s prestigious Freaks List before the 2022 season. He measured 6-foot-3 and 323 pounds at the 2023 Scouting Combine. He skipped most of the testing but put up 34 reps on the 225-pound bench press.
“A dog. A big dog, you know what I’m saying, he said after he was drafted. “A big fella; a big, physical guy. I’ve never been afraid of contact. I’ve never been afraid to ball. A guy that’s going to get in somebody’s face. A guy that isn’t going to make it easy.”
He used that size in college to be a premier run-stopping tackle.
“Man, I’m like 325 pounds. I’ve got real power in my hands. I’ve been strong my whole life. I came out of the womb looking like I did pushups. I was doing pushups in there, so I’ve just been strong my whole life. I’ve figured out how to use it on the field, figured out the right techniques, figured out the right stance to get into and just started striking blocks and making sure they went backwards.”
Parsons hoped that would improve Dallas’ run defense. It did not, but maybe that from-the-womb strength will be an asset with Parsons in Green Bay.
“You got to give him attention,” Parsons said after the 2023 draft . “He’s going to push guys back. He’s powerful. He’s strong. He’s going to get under people’s pads. And he’s great in the run and we’re going to develop him in the pass.”

title: Three Overreactions After Packers Beat Cowboys: Collapse Like House of Cards?
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – A win is a win. The Green Bay Packers earned a big one against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday night. It was a surprisingly easy victory considering the number of self-inflicted wounds that prevented the Packers from winning by30.
Here are this week’s Overreactions
If ever there were a chance for Green Bay’s slumbering running game to at least crack open its eyes, yawn, stretch and shift positions, it was this game.
On offense, the Packers entered the game ranked last in the NFL with 60.4 rushing yards per game – almost 20 yards worse than any other team – and next-to-last with 3.05 yards per carry. On defense, the Cowboys entered the game ranked last with 168.4 rushing yards allowed per game and 29th with 5.10 yards allowed per carry.
Instead, the Cowboys looked like the Tom Landra-era Doomsday Defense and the Packers looked, well, exactly like they have all season.
The Packers ran the ball 26 times for 57 yards. Even with Jordan Love’s 13-yard run putting some cologne on a swine, they averaged 2.2 yards per carry. The 20 handoffs to running backs generated 36 yards, or 1.8 yards per carry.
The offensive line didn’t provide many openings. When there was a crack of daylight, the backs acted as if they were blindfolded in a cave trying to find a lost black sock.
The Packers’ run game almost impossibly went from worst to more worst – the intentional butchering of the English language a perfect fit for the butchering of the building block of offensive football. Green Bay is down to 59.8 rushing yards per game (Dallas is next with 76.0) and 2.87 yards per carry (Las Vegas is next with 3.03).
The 2000 Chargers set the dubious NFL record with 66.4 rushing yards per game. Over the past 70 seasons, only the 1994 Patriots’ 2.79 average was worse.
The Packers have 359 rushing yards in six games. Thirteen individuals have more rushing yards.
“Certainly, there’s some stuff that we can clean up where we’re maybe not winning a block or whatever it is, or we miss a cut,” coach Matt LaFleur said. “But we got to keep hammering it because it is critical in today’s football to be able to run the football at a decent level.”
A “decent level.” What a damning statement. Not a top-10 level. Not a winning level. The Packers, who are so far down the rankings that they have to reach up to touch bottom, would settle for decent.
A decent running game would open a world of possibilities. Against Chicago last week, Love in the play-action game was 12-of-14 passing for 245 yards and one touchdown. Against Dallas, those play-action fakes elicited giggles, with Love going 1-of-6 for 7 yards and getting pressured four times.
Maybe the vision and power of Josh Jacobs will be the salvation. If nothing else, he’ll fight for a gain of 3 yards rather than running sideways for a loss of 3.
MarShawn Lloyd think he's got 4.30 speed and he's going against some West Coast college's defense. He does not have 4.30 speed and this is not a college defense. pic.twitter.com/hOrNm6DC8Z
“I think that definitely hurts a little bit, especially when we’re trying to sell run action and they’re just sitting there waiting for you to do the passes off of it,” LaFleur said. “You’ve got to get the run game going.”
The Cowboys showed the rest of the league how to beat the Packers. Blow off the play-action game and attack the quarterback. The Packers had better figure it out fast, or the offense will fall like a house off cards.
The big reason why I predicted the Packers would finish 8-9 is that I didn’t think they had a snowball’s chance in a broiler to earn a win or two against the likes of the Bears, Cowboys and Lions without Micah Parsons.
The Packers beat the Bears, but they didn’t have Caleb Williams at quarterback. So, whatever. The game against Dallas would be an infinitely more difficult challenge. Dak Prescott is an elite quarterback. CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens might be the best receiver duo in the NFL. Jake Ferguson is a quality tight end and Javonte Williams is a quality running back.
Without Parsons to protect the secondary, how on earth would the Packers be able to beat teams with real quarterbacks?
That, to me, was the season-defining question. Defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon delivered an emphatic answer on Sunday.
It’s a shame a phantom roughing-the-passer penalty on Lukas Van Ness led to the Packers giving up a meaningless touchdown in the final minute, because they entered the final drive having given up seven points and less than 200 yards. It was a defensive masterpiece for a team that entered the season with suspect cornerback and a suspect pass rush.
Green Bay’s cornerbacks helped limit Lamb and Pickens to a combined 4.9 yards per target. The traditional four-man rush was feeble, but Gannon created enough of a pass rush to make Prescott uneasy. The confusion created by Gannon led to two more interceptions.
“I was really happy just overall with our whole defensive performance, especially against that offense,” LaFleur said. “If you told me going into this game that you’re going to score 23 points, I was like, ‘Ah, we need to score 30-plus.’”
As it turns out, the 17 points in the first half were more than enough.
Through six games, LaFleur’s hiring of Gannon looks genius. The problem with hiring a good coordinator is he eventually becomes a head coach, as was the case with Jeff Hafley. Gannon bombed in his three-year run of coach of the Cardinals, but any team needing a coach at the end of this season should be smart enough to acknowledge that his tenure was torpedoed by the lack of a quarterback.
“I definitely think he’s doing a good job mixing it up,” said safety Xavier McKinney. “Putting guys in different positions, placing guys in different spots on the field, whether that’s deep zone, whether that’s in the half, blitzing, so it’s kind of mixing everything up. It’s hard for the opponents when they’re watching film and trying to figure who’s going to be doing what. So, I think it’s been a good mix of all of us kind of doing different things.”
The Packers are showing signs of being a pretty good team. But this is unsustainable.
The Packers have been penalized a league-high 57 times for a league-high 465 yards. They are first with six roughing-the-passer penalties, tied for second with four unnecessary roughness and tied for third with 10 offensive holding.
The Packers are No. 1 in dropped passes. According to Pro Football Focus, Jordan Love has had 19 passes dropped; no other quarterback has more than 11. All of the other NFC North quarterbacks have had 15 passes dropped.
They cleaned up their act against the Cowboys, but they’re still tied for the second-most fumbles per game.
They seemingly had cleaned up their act in terms of pass protection, but Love faced pressure on 45.5 percent of his dropbacks against Dallas – the fourth-highest of his career, according to Next Gen Stats.
The Packers have the second-highest stuff rate, with 29.0 percent of their running plays gaining 0 yards or worse. Their first-down rushing average is 2.25 yards – more than a half-yard worse than any other team. It was an even more feeble 1.47 yards against Dallas.
Green Bay’s offense is almost fully dependent on Love. It’s up to Love to navigate dirty pockets. It’s up to Love to make the offense work without a running game. It’s up to Love to follow up a perfect pass that was dropped with another perfect pass. It’s up to Love to pick up the slack by the first-down ineptitude.
Love has been tremendous for most of the season. It’s true for almost every team, obviously, that the season will go only as far as the quarterback can take it. It’s especially true for the Packers because of all the surrounding problems that continue to fester.
