title: 3 Colts Who Should Be on Vikings' Trade Radar After Chris Ballard's Firing
full_text:
The NFL trade deadline is coming up on Tuesday, Nov. 10 , and the 5-0 Vikings look like potential buyers who might have a new seller to work with.
On Monday, the Colts fired general manager Chris Ballard . The franchise suffered a humiliating loss to the formerly winless Titans in Week 6. With that change, the Vikings should see whether any of the Colts' assets are available through trade.
The Vikings are undefeated through five games and should do everything they can to stay competitive through the remainder of the season. Not only that, but there are some players on the Colts' roster who could be long-term assets for the Purple and Gold.
The Vikings will get a close look at the Colts' assets this Sunday when they host them for Week 7 action at U.S. Bank Stadium. Minnesota head coach Kevin O'Connell will evaluate talent firsthand and recommend potential targets for general manager Nolan Teasley to pursue.
That said, here are three Colts who should be on the Vikings' trade radar moving forward.
By now, most Vikings fans have seen speculation about the Vikings trading for Colts running back Jonathan Taylor. This trade makes a lot of sense for the Purple and Gold. It is a trade that would make a lot of sense, especially because the 27-year-old rusher could be a long-term answer at the position once Aaron Jones is no longer in Minnesota.
Taylor is a former First-Team All-Pro and three-time Pro Bowl running back who led the league with 1,811 rushing yards in 2021. This season, he is one of the only bright spots on a 2-4 Colts team despite averaging a career-low 4.0 yards per carry and a career-high 10.9 yards per reception.
Having Taylor available would also allow Minnesota to have a three-headed running back attack with Jones and Jordan Mason. The only downside is that he signed a two-year, $44 million extension with the Colts through the 2028 season, but there is a potential out after the current campaign.
If the Vikings can get the financial side of things figured out, this would be a no-brainer trade for them, not only to prepare the running back position for the future but also to give the franchise more offensive firepower this year.
The Vikings lost starting left guard Donovan Jackson for the rest of the season with a torn meniscus and are starting Joe Huber in that spot. Quenton Nelson would be an immediate upgrade, and a trade for him would signal that Minnesota is serious about being a contender this season.
Nelson is a three-time Pro Bowl and former All-Pro first-team offensive lineman. After he fills in for Jackson this season, one of them could move to right guard, and Minnesota could execute a potential out on starter Will Fries's contract.
Fries is set to have a cap hit of around $21 million for the next three seasons, according to Spotrac . Replacing him with Nelson on a new deal makes sense, since he will be an unrestricted free agent after this season.
An 84.3 overall Pro Football Focus grade this season ranks Nelson fourth among all qualifying guards this season. A player of his caliber is rarely available outside of the draft, so the Vikings need to pick up the phone to talk about this possibility.
The Vikings traded J.J. McCarthy to the Giants last month , meaning the team no longer has a young quarterback to potentially develop on the roster unless O'Connell believes Max Brosmer, which would be foolish.
Anthony Richardson Sr. is clearly not part of Indianapolis' future plans since they signed Daniel Jones. Whoever the Colts hire as their new general manager may want input on a young quarterback to develop behind Jones, offering a chance to give the team and Richardson a fresh start.
Meanwhile, the Vikings need to decide whether Kyler Murray is the right man to be their franchise QB past the 2026 NFL season. Brosmer and Carson Wentz likely aren't long-term answers, so why not take a chance on a 24-year-old passer who was the fourth overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft?
The Colts declined Richardson's fifth-year option during the offseason, though, meaning he will be a UFA in March.

title: Breaking Down Vikings' Injury Report Coming Out of Their Bye (Who's Hurt & Who Could Return in Week 7)
full_text:
The Vikings wrapped up their Week 5 matchup against the Saints with a win, but they were also down multiple starters with various injuries. However, last week's conveniently placed bye allowed many of them to get healthy ahead of a Week 7 date with the Colts.
Despite the win, the Vikings were without Jordan Addison, Christian Darrisaw and more against New Orleans. So, who could be back, and who might be out for some time yet?
Here is the latest on the Vikings' injuries coming out of the bye.
Mason was put on short-term IR after injuring his thumb in Week 1. Aaron Jones was left as a one-man wrecking crew and was an absolute workhorse in Mason's absence, notching 97 touches during the four-week recovery. But with Mason now on the mend, it looks like Jones may get a bit of a rest in Week 7.
ESPN 's Kevin Seifert reported on Monday that the Vikings have activated Mason from IR and expect him back at Wednesday's practice ahead of their matchup against Indianapolis, although his potential workload is still unclear.
Addison was close to suiting up against the Saints in Week 5, according to head coach Kevin O'Connell, so he should be a sure thing to play against the Colts this weekend after two weeks of recovery time. Addison had been nursing a hamstring injury and tested it pregame against New Orleans but couldn't get to 100%. He'll be very close to that number now.
Addison has just 11 catches this year and needs some big games moving forward to earn a huge extension this offseason.
The Vikings lost Hockenson on the second play of their opening drive against New Orleans, and the tight end was placed into the concussion protocol after the game. Every injury is different, but he'll likely clear in time to suit up Sunday.
If he can't go, Minnesota will get another strong dose of Bartholomew , who racked up five catches in Hockenson's absence in Week 5.
Darrisaw left the Miami game with a concussion and was put into the protocol. He had initially left the game with a neck injury before returning briefly, then left the contest for good after experiencing concussion symptoms. Darrisaw has had a bit more time to recover than Hockenson, so his status should be good for Week 7, but both will need to be fully cleared before taking the field.
This most recent missed game now assures that Darrisaw will go six straight seasons with at least one spent on the sidelines. As talented as he is, Darrisaw has never made it through a full 17-game season in his career.
Both guard Donovan Jackson and tight end Josh Oliver are confirmed to be out for the year, with Jackson suffering a torn meniscus and Oliver a torn triceps. Joe Huber has filled in for Jackson, while the young duo of Gavin Bartholomew and Ben Yurosek have picked up the slack at tight end.
The Vikings also lost safety Jamal Adams before the season with a torn quadriceps, as well as edge rusher Tyler Batty with a torn ACL.

title: Demond Claiborne Is Officially on the Clock as Vikings Open Jordan Mason's Practice Window
full_text:
As the Vikings emerge from their early bye week , backfield depth behind starting running back Aaron Jones remains a concern. The veteran rusher has taken on more of a bell-cow role since RB2 Jordan Mason (finger) landed on the injured reserve in Week 2, while backups DeeJay Dallas and Demond Claiborne are struggling to produce with limited opportunities.
Dallas didn't sign with the Vikings until September, so his lackluster production is somewhat more excusable. Claiborne, on the other hand, has been with the Purple and Gold since he was drafted 198th overall in April, and fans had high hopes that he could carve out a role in Minnesota's offense after looking like a speed demon at Wake Forest.
Being a Day 3 pick means it'll be easier to walk away from Claiborne if the Vikings want to turn the page, which could happen sooner rather than later after Monday's news. ESPN 's Kevin Seifert reported that Minnesota has designated Mason to return from his finger injury and will be back at practice on Wednesday .
The Vikings have designated RB Jordan Mason (finger/hand) for return from IR and he will practice Wednesday. Lots of optimism he will be ready for Sunday’s game.
Players returning from IR have 21 days to return to the practice field, and it seems like the Vikings are confident Mason doesn't need more time to heal. While that's good news for the backfield's outlook, it's likely anything but that for Claiborne's future in Minnesota.
September and half of October don't provide a huge sample size, but it's large enough to reveal that Claiborne might not be a good fit for the Vikings' offense .
Minnesota has deployed Claiborne for only 18 offensive snaps across four games before the bye week, half of those snaps coming against the Dolphins in Week 4. He had three carries for 12 yards in that outing before watching his opportunities drop to zero against the Saints a week later. He did have a six-yard catch in the 23-13 victory, but it's safe to say it wasn't enough to alter the perception around his spot on the team.
Claiborne heads into Week 7 with just 13 rushing yards on six carries and two catches for eight receiving yards. His 55.2 rushing grade on Pro Football Focus ranks 86th among 105 RBs this season , and Dallas certainly isn't any better (52.5, 96th). This further underscores how badly the Vikings need Mason back.
Before landing on the IR, Mason had the 40th-best rushing grade (65.8), along with 59 rushing yards and a touchdown on 15 carries. He also racked up a 159-758-6 stat line on the ground across 16 games (five starts) with the Vikings last season, showing he can offer the support Minnesota needs to make Jones's life as easy as possible.
That track record will vault Mason back into the No. 2 role in the backfield, leaving Claiborne and Dallas to compete for RB3 honors. It's unlikely the Vikings would keep three RBs on the 53-man roster at that point, and given Dallas's familiarity with general manager Nolan Teasley from their time in Seattle, cutting Claiborne and trying to re-sign him to the practice squad seems like the likeliest scenario.
That said, Mason might not be ready for his full workload, though, potentially making Week 7's clash with the Colts a last chance for Claiborne to prove himself. Indianapolis is allowing the 12th-most rushing yards per game and the sixth-most yards per carry, so there should be plenty of chances for Minnesota's backfield to pick up yards.
At least, for Claiborne's sake, he better hope there is.

title: Vikings Fans Shouldn’t Overreact to J.J. McCarthy’s  Week 6 Performance
full_text:
Hanging out with my kids, eating copious amounts of snacks, and rooting against the Bears and Packers. These were just a few of the ways I expected to spend my Sunday with the Vikings on their bye. What I did not expect was yet another all-out war among the fanbase over a certain former first-round pick.
Turns out, you can't escape J.J. McCarthy.
The former Vikings quarterback had quite the game on Sunday , just a few weeks after Minnesota traded the former 2024 first-round pick to the New York Giants for a 2027 fifth-rounder. Still, calls for head coach Kevin O’Connell and general managerNolan Teasley to eat crow are premature, to say the least.
Let’s break down McCarthy’s performance and what it means for the Vikings, if anything.
The Giants benched starting QB Jameis Winston early in the fourth quarter Sunday against the Saints after his second interception.
The CFP National Championship-winning quarterback had seen a few snaps in designed option packages over the last two weeks, but his fourth-quarter action represented his first real opportunity to quarterback a team since the first half of the Vikings-Packers game in January. With the Giants down 34-10 and one quarter to play, McCarthy put together a quarter-long performance that only further divided anyone who already had any form of opinion of him.
McCarthy threw an interception just four passes in , giving plenty of meme-ammo to those who doubted his abilities as an NFL QB (h/t: Bring Me The News ’ Will Ragatz). But from there, he settled in… sort of.
With the Giants getting blown out, J.J. McCarthy came into the game and threw a pick on his fourth pass. pic.twitter.com/LT3vz9ZiM3
The third-year QB flashed moments of potential and frustration during a rollercoaster performance that was all too familiar for Vikings fans. It should also be noted that he was facing a defense filled with backups playing prevent defense on the majority of snaps.
Still, McCarthy’s final stat line of 11-for-21, one touchdown and one interception is an almost poetic representation of the chaotic divide he represented in the fanbase. He threw for an astonishing 243 yards after entering the game with approximately 11 minutes left in the fourth quarter, giving him the best fourth-quarter passing performance in the NFL this season (h/t: NFL Insider Ian Rapoport).
But anyone who watched the tape knows McCarthy had a ton of help.
#Giants QB J.J. McCarthy threw for 243 yards in the 4th quarter despite coming off the bench. It’s the most passing yards in a 4th quarter by any player this season and the 2nd-most passing yards in a 4th quarter by any QB who didn't start over the last 25 seasons.
His insane yardage output came with help from receivers, who often made difficult catches on throws that weren’t exactly thrown “in the basket.” Layering and placement drew criticism during his time in Minnesota, and it appears a change of scenery didn't suddenly fix that entirely.
Admittedly, a few of his throws showed a level of layering and placement not often seen during his time in Purple and Gold. It was certainly a mixed bag, with McCarthy missing an open Malik Nabers for what could have been a game-tying score to end his day (h/t: Doug Rush).
Malik Nabers was open on the final 4th down play. J.J. McCarthy just didn’t find him. pic.twitter.com/C306TrNcS9
The bottom line is that McCarthy’s inconsistencies continue to show just how unreliable he is for a team looking to make a serious playoff run.
While some would point to McCarthy’s performance as an indication that the Vikings moved on from the young QB too early, the tape does not really reveal anything new about the 23-year-old passer. Is he capable of impressive plays? Yes! Reasonable observers know that was never in question. The issue is (and always was) consistency.
Even Giants coach John Harbaugh downplayed the hype postgame , making it clear that McCarthy was in a unique situation when he entered the game (h/t: PIX11 Sports ).
Did JJ McCarthy play himself into the starting QB role for the New York Giants after nearly pulling off an impressive comeback against the New Orleans Saints? Here's what Head Coach John Harbaugh had to say about that. pic.twitter.com/x84bHuKy50
The Vikings are coming off their bye week with a 5-0 record and the toughest portion of their schedule on the horizon. They simply cannot afford to spend time worrying about what is happening with the Giants’ QB room.
O'Connell and Teasley made a clear decision by trading McCarthy: they were betting on Kyler Murray and the current QB room, for better or worse. So far, it's hard to argue with the results, even if it hasn't always been flashy along the way.
If McCarthy is named the starter going forward and starts stacking impressive performances, it may be time for a talk about the Vikings’ decision to trade him away. But until then, we continue to be stuck in a never-ending cycle of McCarthy-focused debate.

title: Harmon's Longship Week 6: 4 Thoughts on Vikings' Bye Week, Trade Targets & More
full_text:
The undefeated Vikings return to action this week after retreating to friendly shores to recharge and restock as they prepare for their nearly four-month push to pursue the Lombardi Trophy.
While their record suggests an ideal start, the journey to get there wasn't always smooth sailing. From injuries to inconsistencies, the bye week gave the Vikes time to work through plenty of blemishes as they look to be at their best when it matters most.
The Vikings’ bye week was relatively quiet, which could have been worse. The team worked out a few wide receivers early in the week , including former Steeler and Chief JuJu Smith-Schuster (h/t: NFL Insider Tom Pelissero). While no signing seems imminent, the workouts were notable given the ongoing trade rumors around the recently signed Jauan Jennings.
Jennings signed with the Vikings in May but has failed to find his fit in Minnesota’s offense. Despite getting open fairly often on film, the former Niner's stat line of two receptions on five targets has led to visible frustration and has been one of the most disappointing parts of an otherwise successful season for the team (h/t: Bring Me The News ' Will Ragatz).
https://t.co/2MM5mM5y4z pic.twitter.com/bb48Cb9H4U
One area where the bye may prove helpful is in the injury department. The offense in particular was starting to take a significant hit with various injuries to:
That's not to mention the loss of left guard Donovan Jackson for the season .
Needless to say, the early bye may have come at just the right time. There is a real chance the Vikings enter their Week 7 match with the Colts with a clean bill of health and a perfect chance to find a rhythm before their schedule intensity ramps up.
If the Vikings are going to make a real run, they’ll need to get healthy and stay healthy.
Although the Vikings didn’t take the field this past week, they kept a close eye on the rest of the league as the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline approaches . The Vikings look like serious contenders, and adding more talent could be exactly what they need to reach Valhalla.
The Chargers, in particular, are monitor for trade targets as they continue to spiral into a brutal 0-6 start. One potential name to keep an eye on is pass rusher Khalil Mack.
While Mack may no longer be in his prime, he’s certainly proven capable of being an impact player in 2026. The 35-year-old may fit right into defensive coordinator Brian Flores’s unit that already features a 35-year-old Kyle Van Noy and a 37-year-old Harrison Smith.
Running back is another position to keep an eye on, with Titans running back Tony Pollard looking like a possible trade candidate. After all, Tennessee sits at 1-5.
Aaron Jones has been impressive, and Jordan Mason appears to be on his way back, but the Vikings will need all the running back depth they can get if they plan to stick with the offensive game plan they’ve showcased so far this season.
The Vikings remain atop the NFC North, but decisive wins by the Bears and Packers certainly turned up the pressure.
Chicago saw the return of starting quarterback Caleb Williams, who put together an impressive 30/36, 305-yard performance through the air in a 31-23 win over Atlanta. The Packers seem to be finding their stride as they beat the Cowboys 23-13 on Sunday Night Football. Green Bay will soon be getting reinforcements in the form of running back Josh Jacobs and star pass rusher Micah Parsons, who is near the end of his rehab process from a torn ACL and meniscus, making them an even larger threat.
Like the Vikings, the Lions had an early Week 6 bye.
The good news? The rest of the NFC seems wide open.
The NFC may never be this wide open again. Vikings have to make a run.
The heavily hyped Rams appear to be the season's biggest disappointment, sitting at 2-4 after an 18-16 upset loss to the Cardinals. The Seahawks struggled to find any offensive flow against the Broncos, as they lost 17-14 in overtime on Thursday night. The NFC East had another bad weekend, but a Commanders’ upset against the undefeated Niners on Monday Night Football could bring redemption to the division.
As of Monday afternoon, the Vikings are tied with the Seahawks for the second-best NFC Championship odds (+650) on DraftKings Sportsbook.
The Vikings come off their bye week with a home game against a frustrated Colts team that just handed the Titans their first win of the year. The Colts’ defense has given up the eighth-most yards in the league through six games, even after holding the Titans to just 186 total offense on Sunday. On top of that, Indianapolis fired general manager Chris Ballard on Monday morning (h/t: NFL).
Colts announced that General Manager Chris Ballard has been relieved. pic.twitter.com/1kQYz6n4e9
However, the Vikings shouldn't overlook the Colts.
Minnesota is favored at home coming off its bye, which means this matchup has all the makings of a classic “trap game." With playoff seeding starting to be a focus and a challenging November slate on the way, the Vikings cannot afford to slip up against an opponent they should handle decisively.

title: Jordan Addison Leads 3 Vikings Who Desperately Need to Step Up With Bye Week Over
full_text:
The Vikings enjoyed their bye week but now prepare to return to the field to host the Colts at U.S. Bank Stadium in Week 7. The Purple and Gold's schedule gets tougher in the coming weeks, with games against the Lions, Bills, Packers and 49ers.
Through the first five weeks of the season, the Vikings have relied on their defense and the golden leg of kicker Will Reichard to win games, but they will need more help as the challenging stretch looms over the horizon.
A few Vikings need to step up significantly moving forward. While other players have held down their respective roles, three players need to improve for Minnesota to help take pressure off teammates—especially if the Purple and Gold are to remain undefeated.
Jordan Addison has played in four of Minnesota's five games this season. Although he missed Week 5 against the New Orleans Saints, he has not been consistent on the field. He is averaging 5.5 targets and 40.75 yards per game this season.
For reference, in his career, Addison averages 6.16 targets and 41.15 yards per game. He will need to play a bigger role, with fellow wide receiver Jauan Jennings having two catches for nine yards this season and Tai Felton having three catches for 41 yards.
This year, Addison has a Pro Football Focus grade of 63.8 , ranking him 52nd among 71 qualifying wide receivers. PFF also notes that his average depth of target is 14.2 yards, meaning head coach Kevin O'Connell is attempting to use him to stretch the field and take pressure off passes underneath.
Vikings fans know Addison can be a reliable target, especially after he stepped up in Week 3 against the Buccaneers when he caught five passes for 90 yards and a touchdown. Minnesota's offense needs to do everything it can to help quarterback Kyler Murray, and Addison could be a major weapon for him this season.
The Vikings' defense has been amazing this year, but you wouldn't know it from looking at the safety play for Josh Metellus. Minnesota has played the veteran defender on every possible defensive snap, yet he has a PFF grade of 40.2 this season despite always being on the field.
Metellus has allowed 14 receptions this year in pass coverage, leading to a 145.8 passer rating from opposing quarterbacks when they throw the ball his way. With how he is currently playing, he is more of a liability than an asset .
Those struggles wouldn't be so bad if he wasn't such a major part of Minnesota's defense. If Metellus is going to be on the field for every defensive play, he needs to step up and be a solid contributor after the bye week.
For Jordan Mason, the biggest problem this season has been availability. A thumb injury required surgery and forced him onto injured reserve, but he is expected to return to the field for the Vikings in Week 7.
In Mason's absence, Aaron Jones Sr. has been a workhorse . Without Minnesota's RB2, Jones averaged 51 offensive snaps played. With Mason in Week 1, the 31-year-old running back played only 30 snaps.
Mason is an effective player when healthy and should help Jones stay healthy and be fresh after the bye. Considering the Vikings' early bye week this season, they will need Mason and Jones to be a one-two punch out of the backfield. Otherwise, Minnesota's glaring RB depth concerns will be an even bigger issue .

title: Vikings Trade Deadline Big Board: Realistic Targets and Potential Sells
full_text:
At 5-0, the Minnesota Vikings could reasonably be serious buyers at the NFL trade deadline. Coming off the bye, the Vikings should have a great idea of how they want to address some roster needs , and a trade (or two) can't be ruled out for general manager Nolan Teasley.
The Vikings' new GM has already shown a penchant for making roster moves, and the Vikings could look to add a safety, running back or receiver within the next three weeks. On the flip side, players could also be on the move out of Minnesota as well.
Here's who the Vikings could look to add, and who they could ship out before the Nov. 10 deadline.
Kenneth Gainwell, RB (Buccaneers)
Despite the imminent return of Jordan Mason, the Vikings could still look to add to their backfield ahead of the deadline. Aaron Jones, meanwhile, proved two things as the bell cow for Minnesota over the past few weeks, and it's that he's still an efficient runner but lacks explosion . Without any indication that rookie speedster Demond Claiborne will earn a bigger role, the Vikings could turn to Kenneth Gainwell, who has fallen out of favor in Tampa Bay.
Gainwell has just 19 carries for a modest 61 yards through six games with the 1-5 Buccaneers, and despite being one of their prized free agent acquisitions, he seems to be a complete afterthought in the offense. Sound familiar?
Gainwell had over 1,000 total yards with Pittsburgh in 2025 as a solid runner and strong pass catcher, and may be that juice off the bench that the Vikings haven't been able to find just yet.
Antoine Winfield Jr., S (Buccaneers)
Another target from the listless Bucs, Antoine Winfield Jr. could follow in his father's footsteps with a move to Minnesota. Safety is clearly the weak spot on an otherwise elite defense, with Harrison Smith very much looking his age and Joshua Metellus consistently on the wrong end of big plays. Winfield could be more than just a feel-good story and would become the missing piece of the puzzle for Brian Flores.
The deal wouldn't come without complications, though, as Winfield is currently injured with a rib issue and hasn't played at his peak for over two years now. Still, the former All-Pro would provide an immediate boost to the Vikings' secondary once he's healthy, and a mid-round pick could entice the Bucs enough to move off their pricey player during a lost season.
In the event that the Vikings move on from Jauan Jennings , they could look to backfill that WR3 spot via trade. Tai Felton and Myles Price haven't shown much, and Odell Beckham Jr. is the wildest of all wild cards . While he doesn't fit the big-bodied type the Vikings might be looking for, Jerry Jeudy would be a nice option if the Browns could... stop winning?
Yes, while most expected them to be sellers by this point, your Cleveland Browns are instead in first place in the AFC North. Still, regardless of their newfound success, Jeudy has stayed quiet with just 12 catches through six games. If the Browns want to add some draft capital for their forgotten receiver, the Vikings could add 1,299 yards just two seasons ago.
His base salary is just $1.5 million for 2026 , according to Spotrac , and he has no guaranteed money left in 2027, so Jeudy could theoretically be a rental if the Vikings opt to move on as well.
Jennings has been about as disappointing as can be after signing a 1-year, $8 million deal this spring. He has just two catches, and his 30.3 run-block grade from Pro Football Focus ranks 196th at the position.
The Vikings still seem somewhat set on fixing him, but if his production doesn't improve over the next week or two, Teasley may be wise to just get what he can.
Ivan Pace remains a valuable special teams player for Minnesota, but has been mostly a forgotten piece on defense. He's played just 15% of snaps and already seems to be losing some ground to rookie Jake Golday, who looks to be progressing every week.
Pace wouldn't net very much in return, so the Vikings could decide his special teams play outweighs a Day 3 pick. Still, it's clear Pace's role on defense has dissolved to an occasional pass rusher for Flores's hyper-aggressive scheme.
Jay Ward started most of the second half of the 2025 season but now, like Pace, has been limited to mostly special teams play.
The Vikings are currently rostering six safeties, and Ward appears to be in the doghouse for whatever reason. Despite the group's mediocre play, Ward still hasn't found a way onto the field, but a safety-needy team may still value a former starter who's only 26.

title: Predicting How Patriots, Bears Perform on TNF: Battle Between 2 Young QBs
full_text:
Back in 2024, the New England Patriots and Chicago Bears — led by rookie quarterbacks — met in a defensive slugfest. Two years later, those same teams and those same quarterbacks have the opportunity to rack up plenty of points on Thursday Night Football.
But it's not going to be easy. Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel gave the Bears defense plenty of credit. The matchup of 4-2 teams in primetime will certainly gave some haymakers thrown from each side.
"They're creating some third and longer situations. They're winning on first and second down," Vrabel said Tuesday. "They disguise well. They blitz. Their off the ball players contribute heavily, I think, to the pressure."
Ahead of Week 7, Patriots On SI beat reporters Ethan Hurwitz and Zac Ventola break down how the game will unfold, which players will be x-factors and predict a final score. Who do you think is right?
Caleb Williams helped lead the Bears to the postseason in 2025, but has dealt with injuries this year. When he's healthy, he's one of the best quarterbacks in the league. The Patriots will have to find a way to limit his production and force the Bears to churn out first downs slowly.
The Patriots have gotten elite prouction from their young pass rushers, including Elijah Ponder — who's recorded half a sack in five-straight games. If they can start to make things hairy for Williams in the pocket and force him to move around on a hamstring that forced him to miss Week 5, there's a good shot New England comes out on top.
Byard, one of the Patriots' biggest free agent signings from this offseason, spent the last two seasons with the Bears. He'll need to have a major impact against his former team, especially when it comes to trying to neutralize the arm talents that Williams possesses. The Patriots secondary struggled at times on Sunday, and it would be a great time to force some turnovers (Byard, the NFL's leader interceptions from a season ago, is yet to grab his first).
Final Score Prediction: Patriots 31, Bears 24
The Patriots are rolling right now and they have a real shot to land a big blow to kick off Week 7. Yes, the Bears will score points — that's just part of the Ben Johnson experience. But the Patriots have found a groove offensively, and despite the offensive line injuries , they'll find a way to pull out their fourth-straight victory.
Quite simply, the Bears may be one of the three most difficult opponents on the Patriots’ schedule this season. Chicago has been battle-tested against playoff-caliber squads such as the Minnesota Vikings, Green Bay Packers and Atlanta Falcons. Plus, third-year quarterback Caleb Williams is one of the most dynamic players in the NFL.
With the Patriots still going through a slew of injuries, this game may decide how much I am drinking the Kool-Aid of this New England squad. Chicago’s offense tallies the fifth-most yards per game in the NFL, while its defense allows the seventh-fewest. All-in-all, it would be a shocking success if the Patriots can march into Soldier Field and take down the Bears on prime-time television.
X-Factor: EDGE Elijah Ponder
New England will need to put pressure on Chicago to have any chance at a win. Last week, Williams went a perfect 24/24 passing in clean pockets against the Falcons, per Next Gen Stats. Plus, the team averages the most rushing yards per game in the NFL at more than 160. Fortunately for the Patriots, Ponder sits top-three in the league in both sacks and tackles for losses. The 24-year-old may be New England’s best chance at slowing down the high-powered Chicago offense.
Caleb Williams was a perfect 24/24 for 248 yards from a clean pocket in the Bears' Week 6 win over the Falcons. His 24 attempts are the most without an incompletion from a clean pocket in a game since at least 2018. Powered by @awscloud pic.twitter.com/Vrx6fZNBRu
Final Score Prediction: Patriots 34, Bears 30
The name of the game for the Patriots’ defense on Thursday is to bend, but not break. The Bears’ offense is too talented to be fully contained the entire night. However, if New England can hold Chicago to a few field goals (or force a handful of turnovers on downs), that should be enough for quarterback Drake Maye to work with. Plus, I’d expect a bounce-back performance from wide receiver A.J. Brown . Ultimately, as long as the Patriots can contain the Bears to a sub-35-point performance, I anticipate a win for New England.

title: Patriots Week 7 Injury Report: Short Week, But Long List of Injuries
full_text:
FOXBORO — Are the New England Patriots noticing anything different when it comes to their injuries? It feels like every week, another contributor is going down with something — and then getting put onto injured reserve.
"Nope. Just how it goes," Mike Vrabel bluntly said Monday at his press conference.
The Patriots had already made a move because of their Week 6 injuries Monday, placing wide receiver Romeo Doubs on IR with a shoulder injury . He suffered the injury after catching a 42-yard touchdown in their 26-19 win over the New York Jets . But now they're going to have to fight past these injuries ahead of their Thursday Night Football matchup with the Chicago Bears.
Here's how the Patriots' second injury report looked after a practice in shells.
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (knee)
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (knee)
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (personal)
The Bears, coming off a 31-23 win over Atlanta Falcons, released their second injury report of the week.
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (thumb/toe)
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (concussion)
DID NOT PARTICIPATE (hamstring)
Already down two guards from earlier in the season, the Patriots took a beating up front in Week 6. Three players — Brown, Vera-Tucker and Moses — all left Sunday's win with lower-body injuries. Losing them forced a lot of shuffling throughout the game, and the Patriots would some how pull out a win on the back of their reserves .
"Vrabes, he preaches next man mentality," Matt Pryor, who stepped in at right guard, told Patriots On SI postgame. "Just staying prepared mentally, making sure you're honing into the game plan. That way when the opportunity does come up, you're prepared."
But this week, with just a limited amount of time to get healthy, the team had to bring in some reinforcements. They signed guard/centers Andrew Rupcich and Jacob Rizy to the practice squad , two players who were with the team during the preseason.
Both of those players had inspiring summers, and now join Jake Kubas, Xavier Newman-Johnson and Lorenz Metz on the practice squad. The Patriots also have Bryant working his way back off of IR.
Good news for the Patriots? Moses was limited, already a positive start. Bryant was also a full participant, potentially signaling he could make his return to the 53-man roster this week.
In recent weeks, the following Patriots have been banged up at cornerback : Christian Gonzalez, Carlton Davis, Karon Prunty and Channing Canada. That's been a long list and it's forced some other players to step into larger roles.
One of those players was Charles Woods, who has also had to nurse a shoulder injury since Week 4. Woods, who has stepped in as a starter since Davis has been sidelined, grabbed his first interception of his NFL career in the fourth quarter against the Jets . That play, where he looked more like a receiver than a defensive back, was the culmination of what's been a lot of hard work for the young defensive back.
"It was a phenomenal play," Kevin Byard said postgame. "For guys to come in, take advantage of opportunities, obviously with CD being down, phenomenal play by him. He’s been playing good football all year. He’s a starting corner in this league, so I’m just happy that, when he gets in there and plays, he’s been taking advantage of the opportunity."
The Patriots had three cornerbacks listed on their initial injury report, so it could end up being another big day for Woods in coverage.
The Patriots have had Vera-Tucker start every game at left guard this season. Brown has started the last two at right guard. Both of them won’t end up playing against Chicago on Thursday after their prior injuries.
With them out, according to MassLive’s Mark Daniels, the Patriots will turn to Walter Rouse at left guard — his first start at the position in his career. The door was also left open for Moses to potentially play at right tackle, and Caleb Lomu to maybe get some snaps at guard.
"I think that Caleb will have to be ready to go at multiple positions," Mike Vrabel said. "We were getting ready for him to have to be able to pull the ball in the game in a different scenario. So, where that ends up being on Thursday, he'll have to be ready for a couple spots."

title: Patriots Don't Have Positive Updates on Injured OGs Ahead of Bears Game
full_text:
FOXBORO — The New England Patriots lost both Alijah Vera-Tucker and Ben Brown in last week's win over the New York Jets. Now with a quick turnaround against the Chicago Bears looming, it's unlikely that the pair of guards will be dressing in Week 7.
Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel gave an update on the statuses of both players — who left last week with lower-body injures — and it wasn't positive. They were absent from both practices on Monday and Tuesday .
Vrabel was short and sweet when asked about if they'd be available against the Bears, saying "probably not."
Vera-Tucker, the team's consistent starter at left guard, left the game with a hamstring injury in the first half. He'd be replaced by Brown — who'd later go on to suffer a knee injury and be ruled out himself.
With a game rapidly approaching, the Patriots will be very shorthanded up front . Morgan Moses, the right tackle who suffered an ankle injury against the Jets, was limited on Monday and spotted at practice on Tuesday, a positive sign for his game status.
Does Moses have a shot to play?
"I think he does," Vrabel said.
The Patriots went out and signed two backup guards to their practice squad this week, reuniting with Jacob Rizy and Andrew Rupcich. They also have Jake Kubas and Xavier Newman-Johnson on the practice squad as well.
They also have Matt Pryor , who came in to play right guard last week.
In the summer, the Patriots gave first round rookie Caleb Lomu some snaps at guard. Could he end up getting time inside on Thursday?
"I think that Caleb will have to be ready to go at multiple positions," Vrabel said. "I mean, we were getting ready for him to have to be able to put the ball in the game and different scenarios. So, where that ends up being on Thursday, he'll have to be ready for a couple spots."
So without Vera-Tucker and Brown, who will the Patriots turn to? Well, we know who the starter at left guard will be. According to MassLive's Mark Daniels , Walter Rouse will be lining up there for his first start of the season.
The Patriots traded for Rouse at the roster cutdown deadline , and converted him from tackle to guard. He's gotten game reps at right guard in the past, but got his first taste of the left side against New York. Rouse was in the game for the Patriots' final drive that burned a lot of time off the clock.
"I'm just continuing to get better each week, week in and week out," Rouse told Patriots On SI after the game. "In the mornings, during practice, during team meetings, o-line meetings. How can I get better at guard?
"I think just coming out there today, all that preparation that speaks (to) how far I've come and just continue to get better, so I can play and I can be wherever the team needs me."
The Patriots ' second injury report of the week will be released later tonight, and will give us some more clarity about who might be available for Thursday.

title: Most Important Patriots Postgame Quotes From Week 6 — And What They Mean Going Forward
full_text:
FOXBORO — Mike Vrabel said it best after the Patriots' 26-19 win over the New York Jets. He said that he felt the team was "lucky" to come out of that game on the winning side, and he's not totally wrong.
After two-straight impressive outings against winning teams, they played down to the Jets' level .
"We're lucky to win, is probably where I'd start, but we're happy that we won. We'll enjoy it for about an hour, and then we're going to focus on the next task," Vrabel said. "Fortunate, whatever. We just didn't play very well. We tried to beat ourselves, but we made enough plays in critical situations to help us get through here today."
Here are some of the biggest quote following New England's win , including what they could mean for the Patriots as they move into a short week against the Bears.
The Patriots led 17-3 at one point, and had a true chance of running away with it. But self-inflicted wounds, including a pair of fumbles, kept the Jets alive for much of the game . It wasn't a pretty win at all. However, they were able to escape at the end — and are aware of what needs to be corrected heading into Week 7.
Mike Vrabel on the Patriots' depth stepping up: "I enjoy watching those guys go out and take advantage of their opportunity. They go from sitting there as a backup not knowing whether they're going to be in the game, to contributing to us winning. So that's exciting."
Drake Maye on the return of A.J. Brown: "It was great to see him back out there. It was cool to see a different guy in the huddle. Man, he looks cool in the huddle. So, I'm looking forward to just growing, just building the connection. I think there's some me, there's some, obviously plays he wish he had back, but man, I tell him, I was just telling him in the locker room, 'Man, you ain't got to worry about one.' He's a player in this league. He's going to be one of the best players on the field every time he steps on it."
Corey Kiner on carrying the ball eight-straight times in the fourth quarter: "It feels great. To be in that position in the game, to see the smiles on my teammates’ faces and my coaches’ faces, that they can trust me. It felt great, all the hard work we have been putting in as a team and personally, it just feels great."
Milton Williams on getting his first sack of the season: “Man, it was just on us. It was eating at us week in and week out just being close but not finishing the job. So we had those conversations all week. Vrabel talked a little noise, got in our ear a little bit."
Will Campbell on playing alongside several backup linemen: "Yeah, I mean, as bad as it is and as unfortunate as it is, it’s just the way this game goes. Coach Vrabel talks each week about preparing as a starter. Guys never know what could happen in a game, and you have to be ready whenever you get your opportunity. I feel like some guys stepped up big for us today."
Kevin Byard on the defense succeeding on third and fourth down: "I think for us as a defense, we feel like we are a dominant defense and wanted to be able to put on a dominant performance. It just didn’t feel like that. Now, obviously we’re going to watch the film and find things to correct, which I’m sure there’s a lot out there, but it’s a lot of good too. So, at the end of the day, celebrate this victory."
The Patriots travel to Chicago this week for their first Thursday Night Football game of the season. That will be a big test and it's a matchup that's lined with storylines. Two of the first three picks of the 2024 Draft going head-to-head for the second time in their careers, while both head coaches are often pitted against each other because they both got hired in the same cycle.
Would the Patriots actually be better with Ben Johnson instead of Vrabel? I wouldn't go that far, but this week will be a good litmus test to see how well the Patriots can handle another tough environment. The Bears offense can light up the scoreboard, so the Patriots will need to adjust to a more high-flying air raid style.
The running defense will need to pick it up, as they've allowed James Cook and Braelon Allen to stack long runs together in recent weeks. They'll also need to get healthy, which is a tough ask for a team extremely banged up on offense.
Can the Patriots win against the Bears in primetime? Yes. But they'll need to try and improve off last week's winning performance, and try to not get lucky this time.

title: With Depth An Issue, 1 Patriots Rookie Has Risen to the Occasion
full_text:
Rookie offensive tackle Caleb Lomu has proven to not only be an effective depth piece for a battered offensive line, but a cornerstone to the protection the New England Patriots are hoping to build around quarterback Drake Maye.
Lomu was the 28th overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft. The Patriots traded up four spots to acquire the 6-foot-6, 313-pound tackle out of Utah. Lomu was an All-Big 12 First Team selection in 2025, and played all 12 games of Utah's season without allowing a sack.
Entering the NFL regular season, Lomu was expected to be the third or fourth tackle on the depth chart, behind starters Will Campbell and Morgan Moses. Marcus Bryant was expected to be the sixth offensive linemen in heavy sets or, taking the place of either Campbell or Moses in the event of an injury.
On filling in for injured starters, Lomu said, "It does happen, unfortunately, in this league. Everyone's got to prepare like a starter for those types of things that happen."
Bryant, who's slated to be activated off the injured reserve soon, has been sidelined for most of the season, giving Lomu a higher percentage of snaps. Both Campbell (knee) and Moses (foot) have obtained injuries in the past two games that have given the 21-year-old rookie extended playing time. Here's how he's performed so far:
Before analyzing the statistics and grades given to Lomu by Pro Football Focus, it's important to note that Lomu played left tackle in college and has lined up on the right side of the line in a majority of his snaps for the Patriots. Playing out of position makes this assessment more impressive, and builds confidence as Lomu being the right tackle of New England's future.
PFF has graded Lomu's overall pass blocking reps at 80.2. His pass blocking efficiency is a 98.0 and his overall offensive grade is 75.1. Each of these grades is the highest through six weeks of all rookie tackles.
Per @PFF , Caleb Lomu's current rankings in his rookie class (at T): 🔷 1st - Pass Blocking Grade (80.2) 🔷 1st - Offensive Grade (75.1) 🔷 6th - Run Blocking Grade (66.0) 🔷 1st - Pass Blocking Efficiency (98.0)* He's showing that 1-28 value. *minimum 50 pass-blocking snaps pic.twitter.com/kN8goxdbYe
Considering Lomu was the seventh player taken at his position, and the last tackle to go in the first round, his pass blocking grades among other rookies go beyond what people have expected from him. He also ranks sixth in run blocking (66.0).
Lomu's best outing was against the Jets, where he played a season high 60 offensive snaps (88.2% of total offense). Lomu played 30 pass blocking snaps without letting up a single pressure. He scored an 80.4 pass blocking grade on Sunday.
With the Jets having one of the most ferocious pass rushes in the NFL, Lomu's skills in New England's 26-19 victory were up to the test. However, the Big 12 star was very familiar with New York's largest threat on defense, David Bailey.
The second overall pick in this year's draft played at Texas Tech, where he'd line up against Lomu on the defensive edge in a conference match just a year ago. In that game, Lomu allowed zero sacks from the standout defensive end.
While his performance has looked stellar through grading, Josh McDaniels and offensive line coach Doug Marone have been intentional about providing extra protection on Lomu's end of the line.
Often, a tight end will stay back to help block or chip Lomu's opponent before entering their route. When using added protection in the backfield, the running back has shadowed Lomu to assist the rookie.
watch caleb lomu on number 2 overall pick david bailey pic.twitter.com/Su8dsyKu7F
This blocking scheme isn't because the Patriots don't have confidence in their first-round pick, but can be attributed to the strength in second-year linemen Campbell and the stellar season he's having so far. It also doesn't hurt to build Lomu's confidence by giving him opportunities to win his pass blocking reps.
Head coach Mike Vrabel shared after Sunday's game, "I hate when guys get injured, but I also understand that on the other side of that, there's an opportunity."
He also said,  "You never know what's going to happen in this league, and we talk about it all the time, preparing for the journey. When guys get their chance, they go in there and perform."
So far, Lomu has taken advantage of his opportunities and performed at a high level. With injuries continuing the plague the offensive line, the rookie tackle will be an important part of the success the Patriots hope to acheive in 2026.

title: Patriots Week 6 Snap Count Analysis: Reserves Get Plenty of Playing Time
full_text:
It's been three-straight wins for the New England Patriots, and they are getting production up and down the roster. From the top — Drake Maye and Christian Gonzalez continue to play lights out football — to the bottom, where young special teams players are earning more reps, the Patriots have carved out a really good football team six weeks in. Their last showing, a 26-19 victory over the New York Jets, wasn't the prettiest , but they got a lot of good snaps from a lot of players.
"Won't know until we move forward, but I just know that you have to be able to continue to improve, and I don't feel like we did," Mike Vrabel said. "We won, which is the most important thing. We just, I don't think we improved from what we had shown the previous two weeks, and I have to figure out why. That's my job. My job's also to get us to win and also to get us to improve."

title: Assessing Patriots' WR Situation Post-Romeo Doubs Injury: Who Steps Up?
full_text:
The New England Patriots got the win over the New York Jets, but still suffered a big loss to their offense. Romeo Doubs, who caught his third touchdown of the season in the 26-19 win, was placed on IR with a shoulder injury and will miss the next four games.
Doubs is the third receiver to hit IR for the Patriots this season, joining A.J. Brown (who returned to game action this week) and Mack Hollins (who has two more games left to miss). But this news comes at the worst time, as Doubs just started to find his footing in the Patriots offense.
Through six games, Doubs — the former Green Bay Packer who inked a large contract in free agency — has been targeted 24 times, caught 14 passes and those three aforementioned touchdowns. Now, he'll have to sit out for games against the Chicago Bears, Miami Dolphins, Green Bay Packers and Detroit Lions.
So with Doubs and Hollins both out, who steps up?
The Patriots have options, but in terms of numbers, it's not that vast of a unit right now.
Currently on the active roster, the Patriots have Brown, DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams and Efton Chism III. Brown, who returned to the field after a high-ankle sprain suffered in Week 1, struggled — and yet, his talent remains the best in the room. The Patriots have also gotten good moments out of the other three.
Douglas has been a bright spot these last two weeks . He's caught three touchdowns in the last two games, constantly getting wide open deep down the field. Sure, he fumbled the ball against the Jets after doing too much after the play, but he's been very consistent with his hands when it comes to catching the ball.
The Patriots' win over New York wasn't pretty by any stretch of the imagination, but they did just enough. Douglas agrees.
"I feel like we’ve just got to learn. We can learn from our mistakes," he said postgame. "I feel like we had the ball a lot, for a minute, a long time. But, we’ll go back to the drawing board and learn from what we messed up on."
The Patriots are going to need to pull that drawing board out and figure out how they can try to win some more games with a depleted unit catching passes.
Williams hasn't been used that often, but his speed down the sideline is always worth throwing the ball his way. And Chism, the Week 4 hero with his game winner against the Bills, could step up for more snaps in the slot to replace Doubs after not catching a pass against the Jets.
On the practice squad, the Patriots have four players with varying experiences. Undrafted rookies Kyle Dixon and Cameron Dorner had moments during the preseason , but have yet to make their NFL debuts in the regular season. Chandler Brayboy, who the Patriots signed a few weeks back, hasn't suited up in his second season.
The Patriots also signed Ryan Miller on Monday, a young receiver who's bounced around the league since entering it in 2023. Most recently, he played for the Miami Dolphins — catching a 77-yard touchdown in Week 2 of this season.
There's eight receivers in the building for this week's game, and all of them are going to need to get ready to potentially suit up.
"Everybody prepares as a starter," Mike Vrabel said Monday. "I can't wait to watch those guys that prepare all week without knowing whether they're going to get an opportunity to play. And then when they do, take advantage of it, and that's a testament to those players."
The Patriots will be back on the practice field Tuesday afternoon as they prepare for their Thursday Night Football matchup with the Chicago Bears. They'll need to find a way to get Brown more involved in the passing game and have some of the younger players help fill the hole left by Doubs. It's going to be interesting to see how this offense adapts, especially on a short week.

title: Patriots Lose Another WR to Injured Reserve, Make Additional Transactions
full_text:
The New England Patriots announced Monday afternoon that wide receiver Romeo Doubs will be placed on the injured reserve. Doubs, who's been the Patriots leading receiver in yards, injured his shoulder in Sunday's win against the New York Jets.
Doubs was a major free agent acquisition of the 2026 offseason, signing for four years on a deal worth up to $80 million dollars. The former Green Bay Packers star served as the Patriots' top wideout while receiver A.J. Brown was sidelined for four weeks with an ankle injury.
With Brown's return on Sunday, Doubs was slated to have more opportunities to make plays, lining up opposite of the Super Bowl-winning receiver. Almost immediately, Doubs saw more potential when Drake Maye threw him a 42-yard touchdown pass on a long post route. As Doubs used his body to protect the football from the ground, he suffered an injury to his shoulder.
Doubs will join Patriots wide receiver Mack Hollins on the injured reserve . Hollins has been injured with a calf issue since Week 4's game against Buffalo. Doubs' IR stint will last at least four weeks.
With Brown's injury occuring Week 1, and both Hollins and Doubs being out for some time, the Patriots will go another at least another four weeks without a healthy receiver room. For less than three quarters of play, the Patriots have had all six receivers they entered the season with, fully healthy.
As of right now, the receivers that are listed on the active roster are Brown, DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams, and Efton Chism III. On the practice squad, Chandler Brayboy, Kyle Dixon, Cameron Dorner, and new practice squad signing Ryan Miller add limited depth to the position.
In addition to a weakened receiver room, the Patriots also suffered signifcant losses on the offensive line during their 26-19 win over New York. Tackle Morgan Moses and guards Alijah Vera-Tucker and Ben Brown each sustained injuries.
With starting guard Mike Onwenu likely to miss the rest of the season with an ankle injury, and Will Campbell playing through an MCL sprain, the Patriots options up front are very limited.
The team signed guards Andrew Rupcich and Jacob Rizy to their practice squad on Monday. Both Rucich and Rizy had prior stints on the Patriots practice squad and spent time in Patriots training camp.
The Patriots made a lot of roster moves today: Placed on IR - WR Romeo Doubs Signed to 53-man roster - S Elliott Davison Signed to practice squad - WR Ryan Miller, OG Andrew Rupcich, OG Jacob Rizy Released from practice squad - CB D’Shawn Jamison
At receiver, New England signed Miller, a third-year player now on his third team. Miller was waived from the Dolphins practice squad last week, but recorded a 77-yard touchdown in Week 2.
To make room for the three practice squad additions, cornerback D'Shawn Jamison was released.
The final roster move was a 53-man roster signing to replace Doubs. The Patriots signed safety Elliott Davison to the active roster. He was a temporary elevation the last two weeks.

title: Patriots Sign Pair of Familiar OL Following Injuries
full_text:
FOXBORO — The New England Patriots had three starting offensive linemen get hurt in yesterday's win over the New York Jets, putting that unit under the spotlight for Thursday's primetime game against the Chicago Bears.
So the Patriots are bringing in some familiar faces to add some much-needed depth.
At his media availability Monday morning, head coach Mike Vrabel shared that the Patriots are signing center/guards Andrew Rupcich and Jacob Rizy to the practice squad. Both of the players were with the team during the summer months with pretty substantial roles on the backup units.
"Guys that have been here previously to help us here as we move forward," Vrabel said of the pair. "I would say that we have to stay pretty fluid."
Rupcich was in line for a spot on the 53-man roster this season , working as a backup guard and center alongside Ben Brown — who got banged up in the win over New York. But he got hurt in a preseason game and was placed on IR. The Patriots would later release him with an injury settlement.
Rizy also was on the Patriots' initial practice squad during the regular season, but was not activated to the game day roster. He got a larger dose of snaps in the preseason after Rupcich got injured. They'll joins guards Xavier Newman-Johnson and Jake Kubas, and tackle Lorenz Metz on the practice squad.
The Patriots now have 18 players on their practice squad and will need to make a transaction to make room.
The Patriots got a lot of players banged up along the line. Brown left the game with a knee injury (his second of the season) and Alijah Vera-Tucker would suffer a hamstring injury. Tackle Morgan Moses, already nursing a foot injury, would leave with an ankle.
Caleb Lomu, Walter Rouse and Matt Pryor would all come in to help stop the bleeding.
"Proud of the way the guys that were in there finished the game," Vrabel said Monday. "Critical drive, and one that they showed up in good fashion and we were able to run the football, take the time down, take the clock down, and end the drive with some points."
After the game, Vrabel spoke about if any of these injuries would bleed into the team's upcoming primetime game in four days.
"We are all smart people here, some smarter than others. But it's a short week. So whether they can make it back or not, I don't know," Vrabel said. "They don't finish the game. We'll have to see. But I don't know any other thing other than that. And we'll just have to figure out who we have available and find 48 to put out there.
"So it's just hard to say, but it's a short week. And if you don't finish the game, that's a quick turnaround."
They already lost guards Mike Onwenu and Greg Van Roten to lower-body injuries, and tackle Marcus Bryant continues to work his way back from IR with an ankle injury suffered in the preseason.
The Patriots will have a walkthrough on Tuesday ahead of their game. Their first projected injury report will be released later Monday afternoon.

title: Patriots Turnovers Among NFL's Worst After 2 More vs. Jets
full_text:
During Sunday's 26-19 win against the New York Jets , the New England Patriots fumbled twice, bringing their season total to 13 turnovers, the second most in the NFL — trailing only the 0-6 Los Angeles Chargers with 15.
On Monday morning, head coach Mike Vrabel said, "We turn the ball over at an historic rate, it's ridiculous." He added that the Pats' turnover tendencies are "embarrassing."
With six total fumbles lost on the season, the Patriots' are tied for third with the most fumbles lost by any NFL team this season.
Yesterday's turnovers came on a pair of positive plays. The first, came on what would have been a seven-yard gain for TreVeyon Henderson . But as he was falling to the ground, rookie sensation David Bailey ripped the ball from his grasp, giving the Jets generous field position in the third quarter.
The second giveaway happened 49 yards away from the line of scrimmage. After Drake Maye found DeMario "Pop" Douglas downfield, Douglas made a couple of shifty moves to continue his run after the catch. He was caught from behind by linebacker Jamien Sherwood, who put his fist on the ball and forced a turnover, which gave the Jets an opportunity to bring the game back to a one-score contest.
Pop Douglas on his fumble: "I'm sick. I can't lie. I'm sick. That gonna haunt me...I just gotta stop doing too much." - @CLNSMedia pic.twitter.com/QDcxMLKiv8
In the locker room after the game, Douglas said, "I'm sick, I can't lie. That [fumble is] gonna haunt me."
He went on to say that he's only going to think about his turnover for the day before he "flips the page" and moves on to prepping for Chicago on Thursday night. He also stated, "I try to do too much."
The Patriots third fumble of the game came unconventially, as it occured during the Jets onside kick attempt. Wide receiver A.J. Brown, making his first on-field appearance since going down with an ankle injury in Week 1 , attempted to recover the onside kick, but it slipped through his hands. Luckily, Douglas was able to fall on the ball and secure the win for the Pats.
AJ Brown drops the onside kick ... Patriots still manage to recover to end the game pic.twitter.com/WBb8xewrVe
Entering Sunday's Week 6 divisonal match , the Jets defense had forced 10 fumbles on the year, which ranks second of all NFL defenses. Knowing this statistic, the Patriots staff emphasized ball security before Sunday's game.
Despite the intentional effort to reverse the narrative that their offensive turnovers are easy to capitalize on, New England still put the ball on the ground three times, and had it taken twice.
New England was able to force one turnover on the Jets offense, intercepting Geno Smith in the fourth quarter. Charles Woods' first career interception was also the first Smith has thrown all season.
CHARLES WOODS INT‼️ 📺 CBS pic.twitter.com/79f638eg5N
In losing the turnover battle on Sunday, the Patriots plus-minus turnover differential falls to a staggering -6 on the season, the third worst turnover margin in the NFL.
Vrabel and the offense will look to correct turnover issues as they enter Week 6 play against the Chicago Bears on Thursday night.

Reflecting on the win over New York, Moore praised the rushing attack, takeaways, and mid-game execution, but stressed the need to finish better after nearly losing a 34-10 fourth-quarter lead.

title: The Good, Bad and Ugly: Saints Finally Win, but Major Problems Remain
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints finally have a reason to celebrate. Their 34-27 victory over the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium on Sunday was far from seamless, but it brought a much-needed end to a troublesome stretch.
Riding a three-game losing streak and facing mounting questions about the franchise's direction, New Orleans desperately needed a win. The Saints delivered by overcoming an early 10-0 deficit, though they nearly squandered a commanding 24-point lead late in the second half.
Quarterback Tyler Shough completed 16 of 30 passes for 144 yards and three touchdowns, guiding an offense that showed encouraging progress on the ground. Meanwhile, the defense created three interceptions despite struggling to contain New York's passing game.
The win gives head coach Kellen Moore 's squad welcome breathing room, after the team entered the week under heavy scrutiny following critical remarks from franchise icon Drew Brees and owner Gayle Benson .
Still, the team's inability to comfortably close out the game after building a 34-10 advantage underscores ongoing concerns about their consistency and ability to finish strong.
Here is a look at the good, bad and ugly from the Saints' victory over the Giants.
Following weeks of criticism regarding a stagnant ground attack, the Saints may have uncovered a workable formula.
New Orleans ran for a season-high 175 yards, offering vital balance to an offense that had relied far too heavily on Tyler Shough to make plays.
Kendre Miller paced the backfield with 70 yards on 20 carries, while C.J. Donaldson added 39 yards on six attempts. Alvin Kamara chipped in 34 yards on seven carries, and Shough contributed 32 yards along with a rushing touchdown.
This collective output was an encouraging sign for a unit that had failed to establish any momentum during its three-game slide.
However, the Saints still have considerable work ahead.
Even so, efficiency remains an issue; Miller averaged just 3.5 yards per carry, reflecting the play-to-play inconsistency that still lingers.
Lineman Jeremiah Wright provided a notable spark after replacing the injured Cesar Ruiz at right guard. His presence was felt in the second half, as the Saints repeatedly—and successfully—ran behind the right side of the line.
To sustain this progress, the offensive line must open cleaner lanes up front rather than depending on backfield effort to gain positive yardage.
While far from dominant, Sunday's performance marked a meaningful step toward a more balanced attack.
Despite forcing three interceptions, the Saints' defensive backfield repeatedly yielded big plays during New York's late comeback bid.
Receiver Malik Nabers and tight end Isaiah Likely caused major problems throughout the contest.
Nabers hauled in 12 receptions for 165 yards, while Likely added six catches for 99 yards and a touchdown.
After replacing starter Jameis Winston , backup J.J. McCarthy threw for 243 yards in just over 11 minutes, orchestrating three straight touchdown drives to cut a 34-10 deficit to seven points.
New Orleans did deliver key playmaking moments: Martin Emerson Jr. picked off two passes, Julian Blackmon intercepted another, and the pass rush brought down Winston four times.
However, surrendering 461 total yards (377 passing) highlights persistent pass-coverage issues that defensive coordinator Brandon Staley must resolve.
For three quarters, the Saints looked poised for their most convincing win of the year—a strong statement following three straight home defeats.
Instead, they nearly suffered a catastrophic fourth-quarter collapse.
After trailing 10-0 early, New Orleans reeled off 34 unanswered points using balanced rushing, opportunistic turnovers, and efficient red-zone execution.
Shough's 18-yard touchdown strike to Chris Olave early in the fourth quarter pushed the lead to 34-10, prompting the Saints to begin rotating in reserves.
However, the momentum quickly shifted.
With McCarthy at quarterback, New York scored 17 unanswered points over the final 11 minutes, exploiting defensive breakdowns and stalling offensive possessions.
An offense that had scored on four straight drives suddenly went cold, finishing an alarming 4-for-15 on third down.
Meanwhile, the defense surrendered multiple scoring drives as New York steadily chipped away at the deficit.
The Giants eventually cut the lead to 34-27 and drove deep into New Orleans territory. The Saints survived only when McCarthy's fourth-down pass to Likely fell incomplete near the end zone.
For a Saints team already facing criticism over its lack of consistency, nearly blowing a 24-point advantage raises legitimate questions about its ability to finish games.
Moore and his staff deserve credit for halting the losing streak, but nearly letting a 24-point lead slip away shows that New Orleans still has significant work ahead to compete with top-tier opponents.

title: 4 Takeaways From Saints' 34-27 Week 6 Victory Over Giants
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints finally have something to celebrate, although Sunday's 34-27 victory over the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium was far from convincing.
After three consecutive losses, mounting criticism, and growing questions about the franchise's direction, New Orleans desperately needed a win. The Saints delivered one, overcoming a sluggish start before nearly squandering a commanding 34-10 lead in the second half.
Quarterback Tyler Shough , who completed 16 of 30 passes for 144 yards and three touchdowns, and the offense showed encouraging signs, particularly with an improved rushing attack, while the defense produced three interceptions despite struggling to contain former Saints quarterback Jameis Winston and JJ McCarthy .
The victory also provided some much-needed relief for head coach Kellen Moore , whose team entered the matchup facing increased scrutiny following public criticism from franchise legend Drew Brees and owner Gayle Benson .
However, the Saints' inability to put away the Giants after building a 24-point advantage demonstrated why significant questions remain about their consistency and ability to finish games.
Here are four instant reactions from New Orleans' much-needed victory.
The Saints always have at least one special teamer that becomes a star whether it’s Morten Andersen , Michael Lewis or Steve Gleason .
This time, it has been linebacker Isaiah Stalbird , who has been valuable on special teams all year, and he made the biggest play of the game.
Trailing 10-3 with less than a minute remaining in the first half, New Orleans looked set to enter halftime with another double-digit deficit. However, Stalbird delivered arguably the biggest play of the afternoon on special teams.
The rookie safety forced a fumble on Charlie Jones 's kickoff return, allowing tight end Oscar Delp to recover the football and give New Orleans possession deep in Giants territory.
Shough capitalized on the turnover, connecting with rookie Bryce Lance for a touchdown that tied the game at 10 with one second remaining before halftime.
The sequence completely changed the momentum.
After struggling offensively throughout much of the first half, the Saints suddenly found themselves in position to take control. New Orleans carried that momentum into the third quarter, scoring 24 additional unanswered points to build a commanding advantage.
Although Stalbird's contribution won't receive the same attention as Shough's four-touchdown performance or Martin Emerson Jr. 's two interceptions, his forced fumble was arguably the game's most important play.
After weeks of heavy criticism in regard to its horrendous rushing attack, the Saints may have figured out the formula.
New Orleans finished with a season-high 175 rushing yards, providing much-needed balance to an offense that has frequently relied on too much on Shough to generate production.
Kendre Miller led the charge with 70 yards on 20 carries, while C.J. Donaldson contributed 39 yards on six attempts. Alvin Kamara added 34 yards on seven carries, and Shough chipped in another 32 yards and a touchdown run.
The production was particularly encouraging considering New Orleans had struggled to establish a reliable ground game during its three-game losing streak.
However, the Saints still have considerable work ahead.
Miller averaged just 3.5 yards a carry, highlighting the inconsistency that continues to plague the rushing attack despite the improved overall numbers.
Another player worth monitoring is offensive lineman Jeremiah Wright , who came in for the injured Cesar Ruiz at right guard. His impact became noticeable as it was a trend that the Saints ran the ball to the right a solid amount in the second half and with success.
The Saints need their offensive front, including Wright when he is involved, to create more consistent running lanes rather than relying on individual efforts to generate positive yardage.
Sunday's performance was hardly a dominant rushing effort, but it represented a meaningful step forward for an offense desperately searching for balance.
Despite grabbing three interceptions, the Saints' secondary once struggled once again against a solid receiving corps in coverage during New York's fourth-quarter comeback.
Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers and tight end Isaiah Likely torched New Orleans’ secondary all game.
Nabers recorded 12 catches for 165 yards, while Likely had six catches for 99 yards and a touchdown.
After replacing Jameis Winston, J.J. McCarthy threw for 243 yards in just over 11 minutes, sparking three straight touchdown drives to trim a 34-10 deficit to seven points.
Still, the defense created crucial takeaways: Martin Emerson Jr. had two interceptions (one off McCarthy), Julian Blackmon picked off Winston, and the pass rush logged four sacks on Winston.
Yet, allowing 461 total yards (377 passing) highlights the already serious concerns on whether or not the secondary can slow so. Defensive coordinator Brandon Staley must fix these coverage breakdowns to prevent future collapses.
Few teams entered Week 6 under more pressure than the Saints.
Following three consecutive losses, including a disappointing 23-13 defeat against the Minnesota Vikings , New Orleans found itself under intense scrutiny from fans, former players and ownership.
Former Saints quarterback Drew Brees, who called the game for Fox and was inducted into the Saints Ring of Honor at halftime during the loss to the Vikings, criticized the team's offense and Moore's play-calling .
A few days later, Saints owner Gayle Benson publicly expressed her frustration with the team's 1-4 start during a speaking engagement at the Greater New Orleans Quarterback Club, making it clear that recent performances were unacceptable.
Benson specifically challenged the team's leadership, including Moore and general manager Mickey Loomis , to address the mistakes that had contributed to the disappointing start.
Those comments placed additional pressure on Moore, whose second season as head coach has been defined by inconsistent performances and questions about the team's direction.
Sunday's victory provided a much-needed response.
The Saints showed resilience after falling behind 10-0, capitalized on turnovers and demonstrated the offensive explosiveness that had been largely absent during their losing streak.
More importantly, they found a way to win.
Yet blowing nearly all of a 24-point fourth-quarter lead highlighted the issues behind Benson's criticism. With execution and closing troubles nearly turning a blowout into a loss, the 2-4 Saints face major questions before playing the Pittsburgh Steelers in Paris. Snapping the streak offers short-term relief, but New Orleans must show real growth to make this a true turning point.

title: Postgame Live Blog: Saints Survive Late Rally from Giants to Break Losing Skid
full_text:
The New Orleans Saints survive a furious comeback from the New York Giants to pull off a much-needed 34-27 win and break a three-game losing skid.
The Saints will now travel to Paris to take on the Pittsburgh Steelers on Oct. 25.
The New Orleans Saints survive a furious comeback from the New York Giants to pull off a much-needed 34-27 win and break a three-game losing skid.
