title: Aaron Rodgers Check-In: Steelers Getting Enough From QB?
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers , after a comeback win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 6, have now started 4-2 for a fourth-straight season.
They made the playoffs in each of those prior three instances, which bodes well for the Steelers and Aaron Rodgers to make it back there in the future Hall of Famer's final season of his career.
Rodgers, who looked like he was on his way out of Pittsburgh once Mike Tomlin stepped down in January, opted to return for one last run once the organization hired Mike McCarthy, his former head coach for over a decade from 2006 to 2018 with the Green Bay Packers.
Now that the season is a third of the way finished, let's put together a report card for Rodgers and dive into how he's performed for the Steelers thus far in 2026.
Rodgers has thrown five interceptions (tied for seventh-most in the NFL) through six contests and is on pace for roughly 14, assuming he plays in all 17 of Pittsburgh's regular season games.
That would be quite the jump from the seven he threw for the Steelers in 2025, and it would also represent his career-high in a single year.
Rodgers has always done a great job of protecting the ball, and it's easy to assume that his decision-making or ability to process defenses has dropped at 42 years old based on his interception total up to this point.
That simply isn't the case, however. Three of Rodgers' five picks have deflected off the hands of a Pittsburgh receiver, with the first example coming on a screen to Germie Bernard in Week 2, the second on an in-breaker to Roman Wilson in Week 3 and the third on a screen to Darnell Washington in Week 6.
Additionally, one of Rodgers' two interceptions against the Cleveland Browns in Week 4 was on a last-ditch throw downfield while trailing by three points with 10 seconds left in the game, so it's hard to blame him too much for that play.
Rodgers unquestionably has his limitations given his age. There are times where he steps into sacks, he does hold onto the ball too long sometimes, and his lack of mobility does hold back Pittsburgh's offense in the modern NFL.
At the same time, Rodgers has played about as well as the Steelers could've realistically hoped upon reuniting with McCarthy.
Though he's tied for the third-most sacks taken of any quarterback in the league with 19 (per Next Gen Stats ) and has had to play behind an offensive line that, at best, has been inconsistent in pass protection, Rodgers has still operated well from the pocket.
With 1,487 yards (eighth-most in the NFL) and 12 touchdowns (tied for fourth-most) through six weeks, Rodgers is on pace for 4,213 yards and 34 touchdowns this season.
If he reaches those numbers, it would be his most yards in a single year since 2020 and his most touchdowns since 2021. That touchdown total would also tie Ben Roethlisberger (2018) for the most in a season in franchise history.
Considering Rodgers won MVP in both 2020 and 2021 with the Packers, that's a good omen for both him and Pittsburgh moving forward.
It is worth pointing out, though, that Rodgers has not been overly efficient. His 61.4 completion percentage is the 11th-worst among qualified passers (per Next Gen Stats ) and a pass EPA of -48.9 is the third-lowest mark under the same criteria.
Rodgers, and the Steelers' offense as a whole, must clean some things up if they want to remain in playoff contention and make noise should they get there.
Again, Rodgers hasn't been perfect, but that never should've been the expectation. He's playing at a similar level to what he showcased in 2025 and has arguably even improved with a better infrastructure around him in McCarthy's system.
As long as he keeps up his current level of play and production, Pittsburgh should feel pretty good about its chances of making it back to the postseason for a fourth straight year, and that's really all it can ask for out of Rodgers.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Steelers Have Obvious Solution to Third Down Struggles
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- After earning their first road victory of the season, the Pittsburgh Steelers have the chance to set the schedule on fire. Two straight wins improved their record to 4-2, and an international trip to Paris, France, can help them earn their fifth win of the 2026 campaign.
In order to get the victory, the Steelers have to improve in several key areas. No area is more important than getting better results on third down. Head coach Mike McCarthy said so himself during his weekly press conference. After his offense has started the season converting on just 25 of 76 third-down opportunities, McCarthy discussed the team's struggles to extend drives.
"Boy, we left some out there," he admitted. "We have to convert on third downs. I think it puts us in a different level offensively. You know, you have about four, five sets of downs that we left out there yesterday and still had a lot of opportunities."
As McCarthy continues to establish this offense's identity, he has to rely on his best players on third down. That means a switch in play calling and a focus on running back Jaylen Warren on any third down with less than six yards to gain.
McCarthy has been consistent with one message over the past few weeks, and that's his belief in running back Jaylen Warren. In back-to-back weeks, he's referred to Warren as the offense's "featured player" and "one of the hottest" backs in the NFL right now.
But Warren wasn't a featured player when third down arrived. In the first half of Week 6, the Steelers attempted to get him the ball once on third down. That attempt was an incomplete pass to Warren on a third-and-short.
In the second half, the Steelers finally found Warren on a third down, and it was a successful play. Warren picked up 16 yards on the dump-off pass from Aaron Rodgers, putting the Steelers in the red zone and helping them put three more points on the board in their fourth quarter comeback.
Moving forward, running the ball in that scenario is a focus.
"Definitely want to get the ball ran more," McCarthy said. "That's clearly a focus. But, yeah, third down - it's happened numerous weeks. And so we've got to do a better job there."
One situation where the Steelers absolutely have to run the ball on third down is near the goal line. The Steelers had a golden opportunity after cornerback Jamel Dean intercepted Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Jalon Daniels and returned it inside the 5-yard line.
The Steelers passed twice in three plays, separated by a handoff to Warren that went for two yards. That was their only positive play of that series.
On third down, with one yard to gain for the score, Rodgers opted for a low-probability pass attempt to DK Metcalf. The pass was incomplete, stopping the clock and giving the Bucs a chance to tie the game in the final moments.
The Steelers should have given the ball to Warren on third down and trusted their best back and offensive player to get the job done.
And that, in a nutshell, is what McCarthy needs to do more. In those tough third down play calls, he has to rely on Warren and see what happens. How else are they going to improve their frustrating third down results?
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Steelers Continue to Look Like Winners With Najee Harris Decision
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers' decision to move on from Najee Harris and commit to Jaylen Warren continues to look better by the day.
Harris, who signed a one-year deal with the New York Giants in August, was released following the team's Week 5 loss to the New Orleans Saints.
Coming off a torn Achilles he suffered as a member of the Los Angeles Chargers in 2025, Harris recorded just 99 yards on 31 carries for the Giants before being let go.
Warren, on the other hand, has emerged as one of the NFL's top running backs now that he's landed an opportunity to be the Steelers' featured back . He has 460 yards and a touchdown on 84 carries over six games, along with 258 yards and a score on 21 receptions.
A first-round pick out of Alabama in the 2021 NFL Draft, Harris was supposed to be a workhorse and star-level running back for the Steelers.
To a certain extent, that came true. Harris finished his rookie season with 1,667 yards from scrimmage and 10 touchdowns.
The issue for Harris, though, has always been his lack of true explosiveness, and that was never more evident than when Warren entered the picture.
As an undrafted rookie in 2022, Warren finished with 379 yards and a touchdown on 77 carries (4.9 yards per attempt), while Harris had 1,034 yards on 272 carries (3.8 yards per attempt) with seven scores.
Then, during the 2023 campaign, Warren rushed for 784 yards and four touchdowns on 149 carries (5.3 yards per attempt). Harris, meanwhile, logged 1,035 yards and eight touchdowns across 255 carries (4.1 yards per attempt).
Pittsburgh did not pick up Harris' fifth-year option before the 2024 season, yet he remained ahead of Warren in the pecking order despite the latter being far more efficient and dynamic, both on the ground and through the air during their time sharing the backfield up to that point.
Harris posted 1,043 yards on 263 carries (4.0 yards per attempt) with six touchdowns in 2024, while Warren had 511 yards and one score on 120 carries (4.3 yards per attempt).
From there, Harris hit free agency and joined the Chargers while Warren signed a two-year, $11.904 million extension ahead of the 2025 campaign that looks like one of the biggest bargains in the league.
It's not surprising that Warren was far more efficient than Harris during their overlapping stints with the Steelers, given that the former had a smaller workload and was a prototypical change-of-pace back at 5-foot-8, while the latter fit the mold of an old-school, physical back at 6-foot-1 and a little over 230 pounds who thrived in short-yardage situations while being fed a boatload of carries.
Still, just based on the numbers and the film, it became clear very early on in Warren's career that he was the higher-upside option for Pittsburgh and offered far more dynamism than Harris ever could, both on the ground and through the air.
Harris filled his role in a viable manner, but the Steelers' opting to prioritize him so heavily over Warren, particularly in the running game, held back the offense as a whole for several years.
Pittsburgh did pivot from Harris at the right time, though, and Warren has now proven to be an elite running back.
He was excellent in 2025 with 1,291 yards and eight touchdowns from scrimmage despite Kenneth Gainwell eating into his workload quite significantly, and he's set to exceed that total by a good amount in 2026.
Over 17 games, Warren is on pace for 1,303 rushing yards and 731 receiving yards, which would come out to 2,034 yards from scrimmage.
Those numbers are a bit inflated since Rico Dowdle missed three games with a toe injury before returning in the Steelers' Week 6 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, though Warren still finished that contest with 16 touches and should command a vast majority of the workload moving forward.
If Warren does exceed 2,000 yards from scrimmage, he'd become just the third player in franchise history to accomplish that feat, joining Le'Veon Bell (2,215 in 2014) and Barry Foster (2,034 in 1992).
We're still a ways away from that becoming a reality, but it speaks to just how dominant Warren has been and further hammers home the point that Pittsburgh made the right choice to move on from Harris.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Steelers Rookie WR Quickly Joining Rookie of the Year Mix
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- It might be a bit too early to state this, but the Pittsburgh Steelers have a new star at wide receiver. Germie Bernard, the team's rookie second-round draft pick, has come up huge two weeks in a row for the offense.
As the Steelers face more and more injuries on the offensive side of the ball, Bernard has met the moment. He's been the team's best receiver over the past two games, producing 17 receptions for 167 yards and a touchdown to help navigate the franchise to back-to-back wins.
Through six games, Bernard is up to 227 receiving yards. That total ranks third among all NFL rookies, trailing just Cleveland Browns pass-catcher Denzel Boston and Tennessee Titans first-round pick Carnell Tate.
But Bernard has everything going for him, and it's putting him in position to be the first Steelers rookie to win the AP Offensive Rookie of the Year Award since Ben Roethlisberger accomplished that feat in 2004.
What separates Bernard from so many others is his work ethic. He meets every moment with the same drive and determination, and he's never fazed. All season long, he's been challenged by Aaron Rodgers in the locker room and meetings, whether that's pop quizzes in the facility or asking him not to make the same mistake twice, and he's responded to a satisfactory degree, according to the starting QB.
That mentality has been consistent since he arrived in Pittsburgh. Whatever the challenge, he is unbothered and confident in himself. It's not arrogance or boasting, or anything close to that; it's a belief in himself that can only be described as beyond his years.
"There comes a time when the confidence starts to match the potential, and I think we're reaching that time with Germie," Rodgers recently said about his rookie wideout. "Very proud of him."
"My confidence comes from my relationship with God, so I hold confidence within myself," Bernard said earlier this season. "I have a high expectation of myself, so I know that I can go out there and make plays and know I wouldn't be here for no reason. That's where my confidence comes from. It doesn't come from making plays or anything like that. It comes internally."
Bernard is an incredible first-year player, but the biggest reason why you should buy Bernard being a legitimate OROY candidate is his quarterback. Compared to what his competition has under center, it's somewhat easy to predict who will have the most success the rest of the way.
The Titans are a mess. At 1-5, they are in the basement of the AFC South. Their second-year quarterback, Cam Ward, is still struggling. Even with the volume of targets Tate receives, betting on him to keep producing is a tough ask.
Even more discouraging is the number of yards Tate accumulated in one game. His best performance came against the Baltimore Ravens in Week 4, totaling 145 receiving yards on nine receptions.
Outside of that game, his next best performance is 70 yards in Week 6. There is a boom-or-bust factor to playing with a still developing quarterback like Ward, but unless Tate has a few more performances like Week 4, he won't be at the top of the rookie leaderboard at season's end.
The same concern can be expressed for Boston. Deshaun Watson may be a ticking time bomb. While the Browns are 4-2 through six games, they've achieved that mostly despite Watson's play. He's completed less than 64% of his passes and has thrown for more than 250 yards just once this season. Credit to Watson for not turning the ball over, with two interceptions to seven touchdowns, but he's earned as much confidence from his organization as Ward has in Tennessee.
Meanwhile, Bernard has a future Hall of Fame QB throwing him the ball. The two are building a nice rapport, evidenced by their Week 5 and 6 connections. If that continues, Bernard could be topping the leaderboards and kissing 1,000 yards when the regular season comes to an end.
And that could make Bernard just the fourth player in team history to capture the illustrious award.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Marquez Valdes-Scantling Signing Might Mean Good News for Steelers
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are adding Marquez Valdes-Scantling to their practice squad , and it's easy to interpret that they're expecting to call him up to the active roster as soon as possible.
Truthfully, we all should have saw this coming. Head coach Mike McCarthy hinted at it just hours before the report broke, and it felt obvious that Valdes-Scantling was the top option for this team.
"The biggest thing is just continue to develop. You're probably tired of hearing this, I know Omar [Khan] is too. I believe in the 68 guys that we have in the building. When opportunities are presented, that's who I prefer to go with, but I'm not blind or naive to the others, the men that are out there, especially if you work with individuals in the past or they have a past relationship here and so forth," McCarthy said during his weekly press conference. "You're always looking, and that's Omar's job, and our personnel department does a good job of it. I thought both [Brandon Smith and Brandon Johnson] did some good things. They've just got to keep working. These guys have — they've busted their tail. They've earned this opportunity. We'll just continue to work."
Brandon Smith and Brandon Johnson didn't play well enough for this team to believe they were the answers moving forward, and are now prepared to test out an old friend of the team's and Aaron Rodgers'. And while most fans seemed disappointed in the news, it may hint at good news for the Steelers moving forward.
Valdes-Scantling is coming to Pittsburgh to help fill the void left by Roman Wilson (finger) and Michael Pittman Jr. (foot). Both are on Injured Reserve, and it's unknown how long they're expected to miss, with reports claiming Pittman Jr. might be out for a longer period of time this season.
The addition of a 32-year-old wideout doesn't move the needle in times of need, but maybe that's a good thing. Because it might be hinting that the Steelers are prepared to push through just a few weeks before getting at least one of their starting wide receivers back - and chances are, that'll be Wilson.
Wilson needs to miss another three games before being eligible to return to practice and eventually the active roster. That would make Week 11 against the Philadelphia Eagles the first game he could be back on the field for the Steelers, if he comes right off of IR and back onto the 53-man roster.
Maybe the Steelers are prepared to battle through three games with Germie Bernard and DK Metcalf being enough, and they simply view the addition of Valdes-Scantling as a better third option in a short span.
That would be great news for the Steelers, who finally found the light with Wilson this season. But it's not the only good sign for Pittsburgh.
Now, things can change and the trade deadline is still far enough away that general manager Omar Khan can go out and still make a splash move, whether that's a trade or a signing. But the addition of Valdes-Scantling certainly tells you that rookie Bernard is going to get the first opportunity to remain the focal point of the passing attack.
Both Bernard and Metcalf caught 11 passes in the team's win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 5, and look like the 1-2 punch Pittsburgh has been looking for.
Giving Valdes-Scantling the call over names like Tyreek Hill or maybe trades like Brian Thomas Jr. shows that this team has its two top options. They're simply looking for a rotational player who can help more than the ones they already have.
Again, great news for the Steelers, who have been searching high and low for a player of Bernard's caliber to walk into their wide receiver room in the last few years.
So, while disappointing to some, the Valdes-Scantling move might be good news for the Steelers. And while it's not splashy, this team may believe in what they have, and what they're going to get back, enough to push through some hard times.
That's a great indication that they've come a long way in their receiver options. Something every fan is thrilled to see.

title: Steelers' Jalen Ramsey Is Not the Same Player Anymore - And That's Great News
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- Pittsburgh Steelers defensive back Jalen Ramsey is not the same player he used to be. He's not even the same player he was when he first arrived in Pittsburgh before the 2025 season.
When the Steelers acquired Ramsey from the Miami Dolphins in the summer of '25, they anticipated getting a starting outside cornerback to pair with Joey Porter Jr. Instead, they landed a player who was still an excellent player, but wasn't quite fit for the role.
So far in 2026, however, Ramsey has arguably been the team's most impressive defensive player. Even more impressive is that he's achieving this in his newfound role as a hybrid safety and nickel cornerback. His game-sealing sack in overtime of Week 6 was the latest example of Ramsey making big plays for this defense.
It took some time, but it's clear now that Ramsey's transformation from All-Pro outside corner to an elite and versatile defensive back is complete.
Ramsey's play on the field speaks for itself this season. Through six games, he has 37 total tackles. He's recorded eight or more in a game three times so far this season, and 23 of his total tackles have been recorded individually. In addition, he has two sacks, two passes defended and a forced fumble.
Beyond his production on the field, Ramsey is undoubtedly one of the most respected voices within the organization. His winning pedigree and individual accomplishments set him apart from a majority of the defense, and it's clear that when he speaks, the team listens.
Ahead of their Week 5 contest against the Indianapolis Colts, Ramsey pointed out a slight "disconnect" between the players and coaching staff. He didn't mean it alarmingly, later clarifying his comments via social media. The problem, however, was that he was spot on. There was a disconnect between the players and staff.
That was rectified in Week 5, however. Defensive coordinator Patrick Graham, now down on the sidelines instead of in the booth on game days, was right alongside his players. As a result, the communication and performance improved. They allowed 332 yards to the Colts in Week 5, but limited them to just 22 points. In Week 6, they turned things up a notch, limiting the Tampa Bay Buccaneers to just 224 yards and 19 points.
Over those two games, Ramsey recorded 19 total tackles, both of his sacks in 2026 and one pass defended. And he's done it all while recovering from a fractured wrist.
That's a veteran leading by example, not just by his words. He called for accountability on all sides, and everyone responded.
After the 2025 season, I would have called you nuts for suggesting that Ramsey could regain his All-Pro form. Even his Pro Bowl selection last year felt like an obligatory invitation more than one based on merit.
About to turn 32 years old and with over 150 games in his NFL career, it's fair to wonder how much he had left in the tank.
Ramsey is playing like an All-Pro defensive back. Call him a nickel cornerback, if you prefer. Call him a safety, if that feels more appropriate.
It doesn't really matter. What matters is that Ramsey is no longer the player he was when the Jacksonville Jaguars drafted him with the fifth overall pick in the 2016 NFL Draft. The player he is now, however, is a versatile playmaker in the secondary. And it's exactly what this Steelers defense needed.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Steelers Re-Signing Aaron Rodgers' Former WR Marquez Valdes-Scantling
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are reuniting with an old friend. According to The Athletic's Mike DeFabo, the black and gold and bringing back wide receiver Marquez Valdes-Scantling as they try to help their depleted depth.
Valdes-Scantling spent part of the 2025 season with the Steelers, playing in five games with one start. He caught 10 passes for 80 yards and a touchdown while reconnecting with his former Green Bay Packers teammate, Aaron Rodgers.
Now, he's joining his former quarterback for one more season, and signing back to the Steelers as a midseason Hail Mary once again. However, unlike last year, Valdes-Scantling is looking to replace two injured starters instead of walking in as the team was desperate to find anyone who could produce.
Valdes-Scantling will sign to the team's practice squad, but his familiarity with the team and Rodgers should make him a quick call-up to the active roster.
The Steeles have placed wideouts Roman Wilson (finger) and Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) on Injured Reserve over the last two weeks. Pittman Jr. is expected to miss a significant amount of time with his injury, while Wilson is hopeful to return shortly after his four-game milestone is complete.
Ben Skowronek missed Week 5 with a calf injury. It's unknown if he'll miss more time.
Brandon Smith and Brandon Johnson were both called up from the practice squad in Week 5 to fill the gaps. Neither caught a pass, with Smith playing a very limited role offensively and Johnson being a last-resort for Pittsburgh.
So, they'll try to rebuild the group moving forward, and will start with the addition of Valdes-Scantling, who will now work alongside DK Metcalf, Germie Bernard and Kaden Wetjen in the wide receiver room.
The Steelers have two star players in Metcalf and Bernard. Both finished with 11 receptions in Week 5 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and are expected to remain the focal points of the team's passing attack moving forward.
Whenever called up to the active roster or used during game days, Valdes-Scantling steps into Pittsburgh's offense as a third option in the wide receiver room, and another addition to the passing game. Tight ends Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington are amongst the top weapons for Rodgers at the moment, and Valdes-Scantling will likely fill in behind or within that group.
Once Wilson returns from IR, Valdes-Scantling may take a back seat to the third-year speedster and become the fourth wideout option, and possibly fifth behind Skowronek when he returns.
For now, though, he's a player who can spread the field and who brings plenty of speed and comfort with Rodgers. The two combined for over 2,000 yards and 10 touchdowns during their time in Green Bay together, and will look to have that chemistry again in Rodgers' final season.
Expect Valdes-Scantling to be the last wide receiver move for now . This team may continue to search for options near the trade deadline, but they'll likely give Valdes-Scantling a shot to fill the hole and prove his worth for a second season.
If he does, they will probably wait until Wilson returns from IR and settle with what they have currently at the position.

title: Steelers' Paris Plan: Travel Arrangements, NFL's Statement
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are very much aware of the protests that are currently ongoing in France and have a plan in place as they get set to face the New Orleans Saints in Paris in Week 7.
During his weekly press conference, head coach Mike McCarthy noted that the Steelers conducted a Zoom call with the league office, which is typical protocol for international games, and that the organization is confident in its plan as it heads overseas.
“I'm obviously very aware, that’s part or the normal planning anytime you go abroad," McCarthy said. "The team is excited about playing over there….we had a Zoom call today with the league office, that’s normal protocol. We have a lot of confidence in our plan.”
A string of anti-government protests have taken place throughout France recently.
According to USA Today , more than 2,000 people were arrested in the country for their roles in riots that ultimately became violent over the weekend.
The protests first began when high school and university students were seeking more funding from the French government for education while also wanting better conditions in schools.
Other groups later joined in, including labor unions, farmers and other workers' groups (as noted by USA Today).
The rising cost of living in France has also been a central topic within the protests.
The NFL put out a statement this past weekend, which noted that preparations for the meeting between the Steelers and Saints at Stade de France remain ongoing while the league works with local authorities to ensure all operational and security matters are properly tended to.
"Preparations continue as scheduled for NFL events and the game at Stade de France next Sunday," the NFL said, per ESPN's Katherine Terrell . "We continue to work closely with local authorities and partners on all operational and security matters. We are also providing the two clubs with regular updates. There's been no disruption or impact at league sites."
Coming off a comeback 26-19 victory on the road over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in overtime, Pittsburgh is now sitting at 4-2 and in a three-way atop the AFC North .
The Cleveland Browns hold a three-way tiebreaker over the Steelers and Baltimore Ravens, however, as they are 2-0 in the division while Pittsburgh is 1-1 and Baltimore is 0-1 after falling to Cleveland this past weekend.
As the Steelers look to build on their two-game win streak, they won't head over to France until later in the week, on Thursday, October 22. New Orleans, meanwhile, has already landed in Paris.
Pittsburgh followed the same plan ahead of its contest in Dublin, Ireland last season against the Minnesota Vikings, and it paid off with a 24-21 victory at Croke Park.
McCarthy explained that the Steelers' decision to hold off on heading to France for a few days came down to attempting to keep the entire process as normal as possible for the team while giving themselves the best odds of coming away with a win.
“Just like anything, when the schedule comes out we’re on a 7-day week flow here," McCarthy said. "Played yesterday in Tampa, had to travel back, so that factors into it... Whether you’re playing in the Super Bowl or you're playing in a Monday night game, you look at all of those things and the reality of it is I've always tried to stick to the basics. The hydration, the sleep, just to give the men the best opportunity to prepare and perform while staying in the normal flow of operation as possible."
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Steelers' Most Important Defenders Emerge in Week 6 Victory
full_text:
PITTSBURGH — The Pittsburgh Steelers can be described in many ways - unpolished, frustrating, dizzying - among others.
But what you can’t use to describe the Steelers is the word ”loser.” Pittsburgh went into Raymond James Stadium and took down the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, giving the Steelers their first road victory under new head coach Mike McCarthy.
Three quarters of the win were downright ugly. They entered the final 15 minutes down 16-3 with little hope, but exited with a 26-19 win. While this game is largely one they want to move on from, the one thing they can’t ignore is how much this defense lives and dies by two unexpected players.
The Steelers are now 4-2 , and it’s all thanks to the play of veteran duo Jalen Ramsey and Jamel Dean. It’s clear now that the Steelers' defense goes the way of their championship-winning tandem.
What an absolute masterpiece of a performance from defensive back Jalen Ramsey. It’s been clear all season long that the former All-Pro and Super Bowl winner has a chip on his shoulder, and his performance in Week 6 was a thing of beauty.
He posted 10 total tackles, including four tackles for loss and two sacks. His second sack of the game was a victory-sealing play for the Steelers, yet another example of Ramsey taking care of business for the Pittsburgh defense.
Ramsey is turning back the clock in 2026. Playing through a fractured wrist, he’s been the team’s best defender. Through six games, he has 37 total tackles, two sacks, two passes defended and a forced fumble. He’s making an impact at every level of the defense, and it’s leading the Steelers to wins they desperately need.
After the Steelers traded Joey Porter Jr. to the Dallas Cowboys, the biggest question that emerged was how this secondary could take a step forward in pass coverage without their top cornerback.
The answer apparently was just waiting to get back on the field after missing Week 5. Dean was picture-perfect in his return to Tampa Bay. He recorded six passes defended and his first interception with the Steelers. He nearly took the interception back for a touchdown, only to be stopped at the 3-yard line by Buccaneers quarterback Jalon Daniels.
It wasn’t just that Dean was unbeatable in coverage, it was how clutch his performance was. That fourth quarter interception put the Steelers in front of the Bucs late in regulation. The offense failed to fully capitalize, but Dean took advantage of a rookie quarterback’s mistake at the perfect time.
That’s what the Steelers have been missing. They’ve long had their outside linebackers creating splash plays and carrying the team to victory, but it hasn’t been enough. The Steelers also needed their secondary to prove they can steal a game for the team.
That finally happened in Week 6, thanks to Jamel Dean and Jalen Ramsey. And if it wasn’t abundantly clear before, this defense starts and stops with its veteran tandem in the secondary.
Jacob is a featured writer covering the Pittsburgh Steelers for Steelers On SI and the NHL for Breakaway On SI. He also co-hosts the All Steelers Talk podcast. Previous work covering the NHL for Inside the Penguins and The Hockey News.

title: Where Steelers Stand in AFC North After Huge Comeback Win
full_text:
It wasn't easy, but the Pittsburgh Steelers mounted a 13-point comeback in the fourth quarter and defeated the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in overtime in Week 6 to move to 4-2 on the season.
After the game, Aaron Rodgers talked about how the victory may ultimately change the Steelers ' trajectory since it was a game they had to have in order to avoid being .500 at 3-3 heading into an international matchup with the New Orleans Saints in Paris during Week 7.
“The thing is, these are the most important moments for us as a team to grow. Because this is a trajectory-altering win today,” Rodgers said. “To go 3-3, we’ve got the Paris trip, that’s just not what you want to do.”
After capturing its first road win of the season, where does Pittsburgh sit in the AFC North standings?
The Baltimore Ravens and Cleveland Browns faced off at Huntington Bank Field, though two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson was out for a second straight week for the former with an ankle injury.
Tyler "Snoop" Huntley started in Jackson's place for the 4-1 Ravens, and while he led the team to a win over the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday Night Football in Week 5, that wasn't the case this time around.
Cleveland made up a seven-point difference in the fourth quarter and won as time expired on a 37-yard field goal from Andre Szmyt, moving it to 4-2 while Baltimore dropped to 4-2.
As a result, the Steelers , Ravens and Browns are all technically tied atop the division, while the Cincinnati Bengals, who were on bye, are a half-game behind at 3-2.
Because Cleveland is 2-0 in the AFC North, it holds the tiebreaker over Pittsburgh (1-1 in division) and Baltimore (0-1) at the moment.
"Cleveland won today, so now the three of us are 4-2...," Rodgers said. "To be 4-2 now, to win our first road game, to beat a team we should've beat. There's no two-ways around it, you gotta beat teams like that if you want to get where we want to get. Didn't look like a win for a long time, so I'm proud of our guys. Defense kept us in it, and offense finally made a couple plays."
It's shaping up to be quite the race down the stretch, and it's starting to feel a bit like 2023, when all four teams in the division finished over .500.
As Rodgers alluded to, the Steelers couldn't afford to let their game against Tampa Bay slip through their fingers. With the Bucs at 1-4 heading into it while having an undrafted rookie starting at quarterback in Jalon Daniels, those are the types of situations Pittsburgh has to take full advantage of if it wants to remain in playoff contention.
Now, the Steelers have to find a way to take down another NFC South squad in the Saints, who are 2-4, over in Paris this week before heading back to Acrisure Stadium and playing the Browns in Week 8.
The Cleveland contest in particular is crucial because of the AFC North ramifications, though New Orleans is one of the easier matchups left on Pittsburgh's schedule and is another opponent the black and gold must defeat before things really ramp up following their Week 9 bye.
From a Sunday Night Football showdown with the Bengals on the road in Week 10 to a Black Friday matinee at home against the Denver Broncos in Week 11 before hosting the Houston Texans on Sunday Night Football in Week 12 and hitting the road for Monday Night Football vs. the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 13, the Steelers will face an absolute gauntlet of opponents immediately coming out of their bye.
That doesn't take into account the two contests it has against the Ravens in Weeks 15 (home) and 18 (road) either.
As a result, Pittsburgh would really benefit from stacking wins over New Orleans and Cleveland as a means of protecting itself against a pretty brutal stretch in the second half of its schedule.
Jack is a New Jersey native who graduated from the University of Pittsburgh as a Media & Professional Communications major in 2024 who is now covering the Pittsburgh Steelers and New York Yankees for On SI.

title: Week 7 NFL Power Rankings Roundup: Seahawks Remain Top 10 Despite Loss to Broncos
full_text:
This hasn’t been the start the Seattle Seahawks envisioned . The defending champs suffered an overtime loss to the Denver Broncos in Week 6 and are now 3-3 on the year.
There’s still plenty of time to turn things around and make a run at the playoffs, but it’s safe to say their first six weeks have been a disappointment.
Even so, they’re still a team that’s highly regarded around the league and among media outlets. That’s evident in our Week 7 NFL power rankings roundup, which still has Seattle as a fixture in the top 10.
Connor Orr dropped the Seahawks just one spot. He believes they could see some change on offense with the return of Zach Charbonnet , which is anticipated to happen very soon.
"Zach Charbonnet is (likely) back. With a completely new offensive coordinator and similar run philosophy, we’ll see if it makes the kind of difference we expect it to," Orr wrote.
ESPN kept Seattle at No. 6, although Brady Henderson also believes the run game needs help. He also says the pass protection and ball security need to improve as well. The good news is that all of this is fixable.
"The Seahawks' run game has been underwhelming and their pass protection has been problematic, but no issue is holding first-year coordinator Brian Fleury's unit back like turnovers. It has committed 12 of them, third most of any offense so far," Henderson wrote.
Bleacher Report had a similar drop from six to nine for Seattle, and Kristopher Knox is pointing at the ground game and Sam Darnold’s interceptions as the primary reasons for concern.
"Backfield injuries have prevented the Seahawks from running the ball effectively. As a team, Seattle has averaged just 3.9 yards per carry. This has allowed opposing defenses to focus on pressuring quarterback Sam Darnold, who has been the team's other issue," Knox wrote. "With seven interceptions in less than five full games, Darnold has actively cost Seattle wins."
Ranking: 10 | Last week: 6
The Athletic is also focused on the ground game, saying their offense will struggle as long as Emanuel Wilson is the lead back. They also gave the Seahawks the lowest spot out of all these rankings, putting them at No. 10 overall.
"Why are the defending champions struggling? Because a former undrafted free agent in his fourth year of a journeyman career is their top-scoring running back (9.4 ppg). While Kenneth Walker III is carrying the Chiefs, Seattle first-round pick Jadarian Price has struggled with injuries and fumbles and is 58th in the league in rushing (119 yards) while he rehabs a chest injury on injured reserve," Josh Kendall and Chad Graff wrote.
Nate Davis dropped Seattle three spots and accurately says you can’t have Sam Darnold throw 51 times per game and expect to win.
"Can't have QB Sam Darnold throwing a career-high 51 times − and getting beaten to a pulp in the process − and expect to win. Sure would help to get injured RBs Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet back," Davis wrote.
The Seahawks are a team that wins with defense and a strong run game. Even though they haven’t been elite to start the 2026 season, their defense has been good enough and their ground game can become vastly improved once healthy. That’s why they’re still seen as one of the biggest threats in the NFL.

title: Seahawks Urged to Target Eagles Tight End Ahead of Trade Deadline
full_text:
This season hasn’t gotten off to an ideal start for the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks. Their Week 6 loss to the Denver Broncos on Thursday Night Football left them with a record of 3-3.
That has them in second place as the NFC West isn’t as competitive as it was a year ago, but they’re still far behind the 6-0 San Francisco 49ers. They’re also entering a tough stretch with the Kansas City Chiefs and Chicago Bears as their next two opponents.
These games will be huge for the Seahawks, who need to start putting wins together. For that to happen, their offense has to improve. Seahawks On SI’s Michael Hanich believes getting tight end A.J. Barner involved in the offense would help, but they could also look for an upgrade at that position ahead of the trade deadline.
One player who may be available is Dallas Goedert, who Matt Verderame of SI says would be a fit in Seattle . Verderame admits Goedert hasn’t been the same player he once was, but that could allow Seattle to bring in an experienced veteran without surrendering a premium pick.
“Rumors have suggested the Eagles might move off Goedert as he’s aged and dealt with injuries, missing at least three games in four of the past five years. Yet, Goedert has held on, and now might be the time for Philadelphia to cut ties. Goedert is 31 years old and hasn’t had 600 yards since the 2022 season,” Verderame wrote. “He won’t bring a premium, but Goedert is a useful player with a ton of postseason experience.”
Goedert is a big target at 6-foot-5 and 256 pounds and would offer nine years of experience. This season, he has 17 receptions for 180 yards and two touchdowns. That’s more receptions, yardage, and touchdown catches than anyone on Seattle’s roster outside of Jaxon Smith-Njigba, and he accomplished that on a struggling offense in just four games.
With Jalen Hurts potentially out for the season, the Eagles could be sellers at the deadline. That’s why Verderame also mentioned guard Landon Dickerson as a player the Seahawks should target. Dickerson would be an upgrade at right guard, and could help Sam Darnold feel more comfortable in the pocket.
Whether it’s an offensive lineman, a running back , or a pass-catcher, the Seahawks need to make a move at the deadline. If not, they’ll have a hard time catching up in their division.

title: 8 Embarrassing Stats About the Seahawks After Week 6
full_text:
It has been a difficult season for the 2026 Seattle Seahawks as the reigning Super Bowl champions . There are a lot of expectations on them to compete at a high level despite some big changes around their team. The Seahawks possess a 3-3 overall record and are in firm second place in the NFC West.
​The Seahawks have a few things to fix if they want to get back at the top of the division and create a more efficient team moving forward. Seattle has flashes of last year’s Super Bowl-winning team, but some rough and embarrassing statistics that show there is a lot of work for them. They need to fix these ugly statistics to have a chance in Week 7 at home versus the Kansas City Chiefs (6-0) .
​Quarterback Sam Darnold is dead last when it comes to wins from NFC West quarterbacks for this season. His one win was an ugly 30-23 Week 4 home victory over the Los Angeles Chargers. San Francisco 49ers’ Brock Purdy has six wins and Seattle’s Drew Lock, Arizona Cardinals’ Jacoby Brissett and Los Angeles Rams’ Matthew Stafford each have two wins. Darnold is a big reason why the Seahawks haven’t won more games.
​Since becoming the Seahawks’ starting quarterback last season, Darnold has accounted for 27 turnovers. This is easily among the highest in the NFL . While some of the lost fumbles and interceptions aren’t his fault due to poor blocking and receivers stopping their routes, Darnold makes bad mistakes. The Seahawks have lost three games as a result of the bad turnovers.
​Darnold hasn’t been the only disappointment for the Seahawks’ offense. Seattle has averaged 129.5 rushing yards per game in the wins over the New England Patriots and the Arizona Cardinals. When the running game was plagued with fumbles, an injury to rookie Jadarian Price after Week 3 , and poor play from Emanuel Wilson and George Holani, the Seahawks averaged 96 rushing yards in the last four games. The Seahawks are 1-3 during that span.
​The running game has been so much of a mess that the Seahawks are critically failing expectations and support for the team. Seattle is so inefficient in the run game that they are 30th in expected points off the run game with -27.51 . It is just ahead of the Green Bay Packers, whose starting running back has legal issues, and the Las Vegas Raiders, who’ve surprisingly abandoned the run game.
​If the Seahawks are driving down the field and need to convert on third down, don’t have expectations. The Seahawks have converted only 32.4% of their third down attempts (24-of-74). First-year offensive coordinator Brian Fleury hasn’t been able to consistently get the clutch running game going, nor have pass-catchers outside wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba stepped up and been reliable.
​The Seahawks’ Dark Side Defense does have some struggles despite a solid first six games this season. The Seahawks have only gotten three sacks from their edge rushers. Two of the sacks are from Derick Hall and one is from Uchenna Nwosu. DeMarcus Lawrence is putting some pressure, but Dante Fowler Jr. is a better run-stopper at this point in his career. It isn’t a problem with the defense, as nickel Nick Emmanwori has two sacks in his limited time as a part-time pass rusher .
​Seattle’s defense has been great in certain areas, but they aren’t clutch this season. The Seahawks have allowed 7-of-7 (100%) of fourth downs to be converted. The next highest is the Buffalo Bills’ defense at 88.9%. Seattle ranked 10th in fourth-down conversions with 51.1% (23-of-45) last season.
​Another key reason why the Dark Side Defense isn’t clutch right now is their poor red zone defense . Seattle has allowed opponents to convert 78.6% of their drives into touchdowns, just ahead of the Commanders and the Detroit Lions. The biggest difference is that Seattle ranked 10th in points allowed per game, while the Lions rank 23rd and the Commanders rank 30th.

title: Slumping Seahawks Doing Things in 2026 They Didn’t Do in 2025
full_text:
Let’s go back to the Seahawks’ Super Bowl LX championship season. The team kicked off the season with a 17-13 loss at Lumen Field to the rival 49ers. The team responds with three consecutive wins, but then stubbed its toes in Week 5 at home in a last-second loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
Once again, Macdonald’s club bounced back —this time with four straight victories. Then came that 19-17 loss to the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium in Week 11. However, the ‘Hawks would not lose another game on the way to hoisting a Lombardi Trophy.
Hence Macdonald’s champions managed a 14-3 record—tied for the best mark in the league. Their three losses were a combined nine points. They finished with an imposing 8-1 record on the road, and did not lose consecutive games all season.
Former ASU and 49ers CB Jack Jones first on the scene at the crucial Jaxon Smith-Njigba drop. JSN lost him before the rare miss. Between this and the Skatt-Tie, it’s been an interesting day for League Devils #asu pic.twitter.com/Q7xkK6SqmF
Welcome to 2026. After opening the season with victories over the New England Patriots and Arizona Cardinals, the defending Super Bowl champions have dropped three of their last four contests. Thursday night’s 17-14 overtime loss at Denver was the team’s second consecutive setback, as well as the club’s second road loss of the season. That’s two things that did not happen in 2025. And with a 3-3 record, the Seahawks have already lost as many games as they did all of last season.
Something else that the ‘Hawks didn’t do a year ago that has happened this season has to do with pass protection. Macdonald’s club played a total of 20 games this past season. The most sacks allowed by the team in any of those contests was four. Those actually came in home wins vs. the Minnesota Vikings and Los Angeles Rams in Weeks 13 and 16, respectively.
The Broncos' defense has sacked Seahawks QB Sam Darnold five times today. Denver's up 14-3 in Q4 of #TNF . pic.twitter.com/u35fQjPKhP
Oops. In the 32-29 Week 5 home loss to the San Francisco 49ers, as well as the overtime setback at Denver, quarterback Sam Darnold was sacked five times. All told, the Seahawks have already allowed 16 QB traps in a half-dozen games. Including the club’s three-game postseason run, the ‘Hawks gave up just 33 sacks in 20 outings this past season.
With the 49ers’ 23-17 Monday night win over the Washington Commanders on Monday night, Seattle is now three games behind Kyle Shanahan’s first-place team—which also happens to own a 3-0 mark within the division. It’s safe to say that Macdonald’s team has dug itself a hole just six weeks into 2026. And things don’t get any easier as the Seahawks welcome old friend Kenneth Walker III and the 5-0 Kansas City Chiefs to Lumen Field this Sunday evening.

title: 3 Defensive Players the Seahawks Could Trade for From the Indianapolis Colts
full_text:
Earlier today, I wrote an article discussing some offensive players the Seattle Seahawks could trade for from the Indianapolis Colts. While we’re here, we should explore the defense as well. I imagine the Colts will be eager to blow things up on both sides of the ball, as the new braintrust will have little attachment to the roster that Chris Ballard put together.
I questioned the wisdom of trading for an offensive player in the prior article, so let me offer up the opposite perspective on defense. That is to say, the Seattle Seahawks are currently so good on defense, you could make the argument that adding a player isn’t going to move the needle . But, ultimately, it’s just an argument, so let’s take a look at some viable options.
The Seattle Seahawks are telling us something with the usage of Rylie Mills so far this season. And it’s the same thing that the tape tells you when you look at him on the field. He can’t hold up against the run. So opportunities for him to provide good snaps are extremely limited. And it’s possible that their current three-man rotation isn’t enough in the long run.
Grover Stewart has had a decade-long career of good, productive play, taking up space in the middle as a one-tech and three-tech. He’s getting old, but should still be able to provide 15-20 good reps a week. He’s in the final year of his contract, with around $7 million left in base for the season, so it should be fairly cheap and easy to make it work.
Same idea as Stewart, but Buckner is a much better playmaker and has a slightly more complex contract situation. With about half of his 2026 salary in bonus, the Colts would probably be looking for a little bit more to make it worth their while. However, he’s in his contract year as well, so it’s ultimately still a no-brainer for the Colts to trade him for something.
The complication would be if Buckner wants to get extended as soon as a trade goes through. The Seahawks can not afford to give big money to another interior lineman after paying Leonard Williams , with Byron Murphy coming due soon. So he has to agree to play things out and hit the market in March. Does he want a shot at a super bowl? You’d have to ask him.
This would be the Colts trying to recoup the Sauce Gardner disaster. After giving up two first round picks and a semi-intriguing player for a cornerback that has done nothing to help them win, Indianapolis desperately needs some significant picks back. Latu, a former first round pick in his third season, might be able to get a first round back. Emphasis on might.
Latu has been a little underwhelming so far this season, just a single sack under his belt, but he had 8.5 in 2025 and has more than two years left on his deal if you count the fifth-year option. Mike will have to decide if his game fits his defense, which is no guarantee, but if you pull the trigger here you have a long-term edge rusher to pair with Derick Hall .

title: 3 Offensive Players the Seahawks Could Trade for From the Indianapolis Colts
full_text:
When the Indianapolis Colts fired Chris Ballard, their General Manager of almost ten seasons, and replaced him with a former Seattle Seahawk scout and executive in Ed Dodds, many people immediately thought the same thing. The fire sale is imminent, and John Schneider has a clear in for negotiations. So, who is worth trading for on their offense?
Before we get into that, let me re-emphasize that I’m not convinced making a trade is a good idea for the Seahawks right now. One player, maybe even a couple players, may not fix their problems. If Brian Fleury can’t hack it as a playcaller, or Sam Darnold continues to give the ball away, the rest of this doesn’t even matter that much. But, for the sake of argument.
There was a lot of steam around the Seahawks drafting Taylor back in 2020. Now, with him established as an elite running back, perhaps it makes sense to bring him in. JT has made two straight pro bowls and is still well on pace for a thousand yard season. His 4.0 yard per carry average is easily a career-low, however, a red flag as he approaches 28 years old.
Other obstacles include his contract (two years left after 2026 at $44 million, plus around $4 million left in base on his 2026 salary), which means the Colts will likely demand significant compensation. Also, will John Schneider make a big draft capital AND monetary investment into a running back after he already blinked at giving Ken Walker a big contract? I doubt it.
Beyond that, does Taylor fit their offense? The Jonathan Taylor I’m familiar with tends to stick to the A-gap and B-gap, so I’m not sure if it’ll work in Seattle’s outside zone scheme. He has the speed for it, but there’s more to the outside zone than just speed. Are we really giving up a day two pick and significant money for a running back? Color me skeptical.
I’m not big on the idea of the Seahawks adding a wide receiver right now. I understand where the idea is coming from, but if this team can’t figure out how to use the receivers they already have , I’m hesitant to toss another log into the fire. Rashid Shaheed and Tory Horton should be more than enough for this offense, even if it’s a bit more pass-happy than expected.
However, Downs is in the final year of his rookie deal and should be pretty cheap. He’s been pretty productive, but not so productive that he should feel entitled to a quick extension. I imagine the Colts are going to take an ‘everything that’s not nailed down’ approach, and trading for Downs might block him from the Rams and 49ers as well. Worth a thought.
I’ve seen this one a lot, and it’s not hard to see why. Quenton Nelson has been a premiere left guard in this league for almost ten years, and PFF still considers him to be among the very best. He’s in a contract year, so he’s pretty easy to move, and is 30, so it’s very unlikely the Colts view him as part of their plans. The cost shouldn’t be as high as you’d think.
That being said, having a good offensive line in the NFL is much more than just stacking the most talented five players you can get. It’s about synergy and continuity. Injecting a new left guard into the mix is not guaranteed to improve things, even if the overall talent level goes up. Also, putting him in at left guard means you’re mixing things up elsewhere.
Grey Zabel moves to center in this hypothetical , which may not go smoothly (he played tackle in college). This bumps Jalen Sundell to either right guard, where he has a little bit of experience but nothing that guarantees future success, or to the bench. In my mind, Sundell is playing well at center right now. Also, would Nelson demand an immediate extension? It’s complex.

title: The Best, Worst and Likeliest Scenarios for Chiefs vs. Seahawks
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are preparing for battle as they take on the undefeated Kansas City Chiefs for Week 7's edition of Sunday Night Football.
It's a massive game for the Seahawks , who are looking to avoid a three-game losing streak against the only undefeated team left in the AFC.
Here's a look at three possible outcomes for the game in prime time this weekend.
The Seahawks know this matchup will come down to whether Kenneth Walker III has a good game. If the Seahawks' defensive front, which has been arguably the best in the league this season, can contain him, they should have the tools needed to pull out the win.
This is the No. 1 offense against the No. 1 defense, so sparks are destined to fly. Sometimes offense wins games, but a good defense will always find a way to beat a good offense. That's what Seattle hopes will happen in Week 7.
The Seahawks' offense has struggled mightily , especially in the turnover department. The team has thrown seven interceptions this season and fumbled five times, for 12 giveaways, which is a tie for third in the NFL. Only the New England Patriots and Los Angeles Chargers have given the ball up more frequently.
If the Chiefs' defense can capitalize on this and give Patrick Mahomes and their offense shorter fields throughout the night, this could be a blowout victory for the Chiefs. It could truly send the Seahawks into a spiral.
This game has a lot of defense written all over it. The Chiefs have allowed 10 points or fewer in three of their first five games, which sets the stage for a potential defensive struggle. The Seahawks have kept things close in their losses, so I'm anticipating another close contest between the two teams.
If that were to be the case, I like the Seahawks at home, with the crowd behind them, hoping to snap their two-game losing streak.
Kickoff for the game between the Chiefs and Seahawks is scheduled for Sunday at 5:20 pm PT inside Lumen Field. Fans can watch the game on NBC or stream it on Peacock.

title: Seahawks Face Big X-Factor in Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker III
full_text:
When the Seattle Seahawks host the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 7's edition of Sunday Night Football , most of the attention will be zeroed in on one player in particular.
Kenneth Walker III won Super Bowl MVP honors with the Seahawks back in February and is the NFL's leading rusher for the Chiefs. Eight months later, for the first time since leaving Seattle in free agency , Walker returns to Lumen Field for a chance to take on his former team.
This is a game that has been circled ever since the schedule came out in May, and the stage is set for one of the biggest rivalry games of the year.
Walker has picked up where he left off in the postseason for the Seahawks. So far this season, in his first five games with the Chiefs, he has run for over 70 yards in every matchup. Walker has found the end zone in four out of his five games, including a pair in each of the last two games, both of which were wins against divisional opponents. Through five weeks, Walker has 665 rushing yards and six touchdowns.
Walker leads the league in rushing yards and is only behind Jamir Gibbs (Detroit Lions), Javonte Williams (Dallas Cowboys), Jonathan Taylor (Indianapolis Colts), Derrick Henry (Baltimore Ravens), and Josh Allen (Buffalo Bills) in rushing touchdowns.
If there is anyone who knows Walker's rushing tendencies, it's the Seahawks' defensive line that went up against him in practice for the first four years of his career. So far this season, the Seahawks have allowed just 96 yards per game to opposing running backs, which ranks in the top 10 of the NFL. It's the best rush defense the Chiefs have faced this season, and it should test Walker more than he has been over the past couple of weeks.
Walker has added a lot of dynamism to the Chiefs' offense, and we haven't seen them face adversity quite yet. Kansas City has relied on Walker because he's been playing about as well as anyone in the NFL. If the Seahawks can find a way to silence him, or at least contain him to a normal production rate, Seattle could exit the matchup with a major win to get them back on track.
Kickoff between the Chiefs and Seahawks is scheduled for Sunday at 5:20 pm PT inside Lumen Field. Fans can watch the game on NBC or stream it on Peacock.

title: Mike Macdonald Explains Why Seahawks Lost vs. Broncos
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are turning over a new page as they get ready for their Week 7 matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday Night Football.
In order for the team to move forward, they have to be honest with themselves about what went wrong in their Week 6 loss against the Denver Broncos on Thursday Night Football. Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald spoke with reporters and explained what he saw after looking at the game film over the weekend.
"Based off the game, where my frustration lied, I think we talked about this after the game, but just the identity of us and Seahawk football. That feeling wasn't there," Macdonald said via the team's website.
"You're frustrated but also without the facts and without the objectivity behind everything, so that's what makes the problem-solving process interesting. That's part of the reason we like being coaches is because that's part of our process. So I'm proud of the couple days work that we put in. I think we had some honest conversations, an honest process. I think we're definitely more aligned as a team than we were a few days ago and I'm excited about where we can go, honestly."
The Seahawks loss against the Broncos had the ingredients for a victory. The Seahawks outgained the Broncos, 353-168, and the team had 24 first downs compared to Denver's 13. Still, it came down to the fact that the Seahawks couldn't score enough points. A pair of Darnold interceptions late in the game ultimately cost the Seahawks a win, along with a fumble earlier in the contest.
That being said, in an overtime game, a number of things could have gone differently to trigger a different result, and everyone needs to be held accountable for their actions.
The Seahawks are looking forward to another week of practice, during which they will look to clean up the mistakes they've made over the last two weeks that have cost them a pair of potential wins.
If the Seahawks can get back on track and beat the undefeated Chiefs at home, it should set them back on the right track for the second half of the regular season.

title: Seahawks Face First Must-Win Scenario of 2026 vs. Chiefs
full_text:
Eight months after winning the second Super Bowl in franchise history, the Seattle Seahawks are at risk of their worst seven-game start of the Mike Macdonald era when they host the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 7.
The Chiefs come in at 5-0, while the Seahawks (3-3) have lost three of their last four games after a solid beginning to 2026. Seattle has not begun a season 3-4 since 2022, and they went on to win just nine games.
Macdonald and the Seahawks are in must-win territory, especially with all the other storylines circling the matchup.
Former Seahawks running back and Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III is leading the NFL in rushing yards (665), even though the Chiefs have already had a bye week.
Walker is averaging 6.3 yards per carry in KC, while the Seahawks are averaging 3.9 as a team between their multiple running backs. That’s probably been the biggest hole on Seattle’s roster this season, after Walker and Zach Charbonnet were one of the best tandems in the league from 2022-25.
The common criticism, of course, has now been that the Seahawks shouldn’t have let Walker leave in free agency. That notion is misguided, however, as Walker said he knew “sometime during the season” that he would sign elsewhere in free agency. Walker signed with the Chiefs quickly after free agency began.
Should the Seahawks have worked harder to retain Walker? Probably, but we aren’t privy to every conversation that happened between the two sides.
Either way, Walker is thriving with his new team, and the Seahawks are struggling to run the ball without him and Charbonnet on the field. That’s where both sides stand.
So, with the stakes of falling to 3-4 on the line and the storylines that would emerge from Walker running all over the Seahawks’ defense on Sunday, Macdonald and Seattle must beat the Chiefs.
Two things are working against each other: Walker is averaging 133 rushing yards per game, and the Seahawks haven’t allowed a 100-yard rusher in 35 games — the longest such streak in the NFL.
The Seahawks have given up just 96 rushing yards per game this season, as their defense has continued to be one of the best units in the league. Now their former teammate will give them their toughest test of the 2026 season.
In the scope of the standings, Seattle has to try to keep pace with the 5-0 San Francisco 49ers (pending the result of Monday Night Football). They also need to stay ahead of the Arizona Cardinals and Los Angeles Rams, who are both 2-4.
Expectations were high heading into this season, coming off a championship, and those expectations haven’t changed. The Seahawks have to prove they are still better than their rivals and that they can win without Walker.

title: The Biggest Overreaction From 49ers Week 6 Win vs. Commanders
full_text:
It wasn't pretty by any means, but the San Francisco 49ers got the job done against the Washington Commanders on Monday night, 23-17.
One reason the game got out of hand was that the 49ers were missing Mike Evans . He left the game with roughly two minutes left in the first half after hurting his Achilles on his third catch.
The 49ers wisely kept him out of the rest of the game. Evans dealt with Achilles soreness all week. That's why he didn't participate in any of the practices leading up to this game.
Evans will most likely miss Week 7 against the Atlanta Falcons, rendering the 49ers desperate at wide receiver. His injury has led 49ers fans to further advocate for a blockbuster wide receiver trade.
While I understand the sentiment, it's a complete overreaction to the situation after their Week 6 win. Yes, things have certainly changed a bit with Evans' Achilles injury.
The wide receiver position is in a desolate spot, causing a knee-jerk reaction from fans to advocate for the 49ers to make a trade.
However, as I explained in a previous article, the 49ers don't need a blockbuster wide receiver trade . All of the players who are currently hurt are not lost for the season.
If that were the case, then by all means, make a trade. It would be malpractice for the 49ers not to make something happen with a couple more receivers out for the year.
But they're getting all of these players back in a few weeks. What's the point of making a trade for a wide receiver now?
Let's say the 49ers executed a trade at this very moment. That receiver will need time to acclimate to the 49ers' offense, which isn't easy.
How long will that take? At least a few games, probably, right? By that time, the 49ers will have Samuel and Robinson back. Evans might be fully fit by then, too.
So, this idea of needing a receiver isn't sound. At that point, it's basically saying the 49ers never had adequate talent at the position outside of Evans.
Meaning, the 49ers didn't do a great job addressing the position in the offseason. You can point to injuries and even mention Ricky Pearsall.
But Pearsall has always been an injury risk, so his absence isn't a surprise or detrimental. Even Evans' injury is expected, given his age and the mileage on his body.
This is the risk the 49ers took and were willing to take. For the most part, it's been working out perfectly fine. They have more than enough to continue to soar on offense.

title: 10 Winners and Losers From 49ers Week 6 Win vs. Commanders
full_text:
Defeating the Washington Commanders was a lot tougher than it should've been for the San Francisco 49ers . But they got it done nonetheless.
Some 49ers will love their performance in this game, while others will want to forget it. That said, here are the 10 winners and losers from the 49ers' Week 6 win over the Commanders.
What a performance from Malik Mustapha . He was the hero of this game, making back-to-back stops in the second-to-last series with the game on the line.
Mustapha could've folded under the pressure of those moments, but he met it head-on. He's been a wrecking ball ever since he started receiving playing time.
If Dre Greenlaw is the enforcer, then Mustapha is his second in command. It's safe to say he's cemented himself as the starter for the rest of the season.
Brock Purdy delivers another excellent performance. This time, he does it in primetime with the entire nation watching him. The bright lights never scare Purdy.
If anything, he thrived on it when he was lighting up the Commanders like a Christmas tree in the first half. Purdy simmered down in the second half, but he was balling nonetheless.
A major reason why Purdy was balling is that the offensive line kept him clean. Purdy was sacked twice but was only pressured six times on 34 dropbacks. That's nuts.
One of the sacks was a missed assignment, not an outright lost matchup. They also blocked really well in the run game. This group is the best one on the 49ers, and it isn't even close. They're elite.
The 49ers had done a great job in limiting Christian McCaffrey's workload this season, but against the Commanders, his heavy usage was required.
McCaffrey took 16 carries and nine receptions, which was desperately needed. The 49ers were lacking receivers, especially once Mike Evans exited the game.
A performance is a reminder that McCaffrey still has it. He's not the super explosive player he once was, but when the 49ers need him, he can carry a bulk of the offense.
Evans was off to an amazing start in this game with three catches for 94 yards. Unfortunately, he injured his Achilles on his final catch, which had been an issue for him all week.
Thankfully, Evans didn't suffer an Achilles tear. That's why he's a "winner." It could've been much worse. He'll most likely miss Week 7, but if that's all, it feels like the 49ers scored a win.
The first-half game plan for the 49ers was sensational. Everything Kyle Shanahan called was working perfectly. Yet for some reason, he didn't change it up in the second half when Evans left the game.
Shanahan got incredibly pass-happy in the second half. On the 49ers' second and third drives of that half, Shanahan called six straight passes. That's insane.
The running game was working well, and they needed to drain the clock with a two-score lead. His play calling allowed the Commanders to make it a close game. He must be better.
This was by far the worst performance of the season for Renardo Green. He can afford it since the 49ers won, and he's been phenomenal in every game before this.
But man, did he struggle. From busting coverages to committing a penalty, he looked like his 2025 version. Hopefully, this was just a one-off, and he bounces back next week.
With Mustapha playing lights out, he's making it impossible for Marques Sigle to get his starting job back. There's no telling if he'll see the field again, barring an injury to another player.
It's brutal for Sigle, as he was playing really well before his high ankle sprain. Unfortunately, this is part of the game. You miss time, another player shines in your place, and you're never seen again.
It feels like every game there is at least one blunder from Jacob Cowing. Against the Commanders, he did it as a punt returner when he decided to field punts around the five-yard line.
The 49ers have told Cowing he needs to let the ball hit the ground so it can bounce into the end zone. He's clearly not listening, which means it's only a matter of time before he loses his spot.
Another player who could lose his spot soon is kicker Eddy Pineiro. He has the yips, which is only fitting for a 49ers kicker.
I don't know if Pineiro caught lightning in a bottle last year and this is who he really is, but the 49ers can't continue like this. He's going to cost them a game if this doesn't get corrected soon.

title: How the 49ers Feel About Their 6-0 Start to the Season
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers sit atop the NFC standings after securing their sixth consecutive win of the season against the Washington Commanders.
Despite dealing with injuries, the 49ers have remained undefeated and hold the best record in the conference. They are 3-0 in the NFC West, having secured wins over the reigning Super Bowl champions, the Seattle Seahawks, and the Los Angeles Rams, who went into this season as the Super Bowl favorites.
It's been a hugely successful start to the season for San Francisco. The 49ers have shown plenty of strengths despite dealing with a string of injuries , overcoming concerns so far that their injury-hit roster could derail their season.
Despite the challenges, the 49ers have continued to deliver results and exceed expectations through the opening weeks of the season. Their impressive start has drawn reactions from coaches and players, who have shared their thoughts on the 100% win record.
"I feel good that we just won a game. I mean, 6-0 is better than any other options in your record, but definitely, I feel good when the year's over and you're the last team to win the last game of the year. So, I'll wait until that moment," shared Kyle Shanahan.
"Yeah. A win is a win. You know, they're hard to come by and no game is given to you," added Trent Williams. "We had a lot of guys go down. They did as well. So it's not an excuse, but I think we were just a hair off a couple of plays where we could have kept the drive alive. And ultimately we could have probably ended the game on our terms."
“Of course, 6-0, fantastic,” stated Fred Warner. “We’re gonna still continue to chase progression. You don’t want to just be a 6-0, you want to be a team that’s on the rise.”
It's the r ight mentality to have . The 49ers have often appeared focused on the ultimate goal of reaching the Super Bowl, but last season brought a shift in mindset. Rather than looking too far ahead, the focus turned to taking each game as it came and ensuring every player fulfilled their responsibilities to the best of their ability.
Of course, the ultimate goal has to be winning the Super Bowl. The 49ers are one of the biggest franchises in the league for a reason, so expectations will always be high. However, the key is to focus on performing at their best, winning each game, and taking it one step at a time until they achieve their ultimate goal.

title: 49ers Have 3 Defenders Who Deserve Bigger Roles
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers do not have the highest-end name talent, but the group is starting to ascend together. The rise of three players who did not have significant roles earlier in the season could lead to the defense finishing stronger than expected, though. Can the 49ers continue to get these four contributors on the field?
Williams is recovering from an ACL injury and just debuted last week. So, it is not a huge shock he has not played much. However, despite the small sample it is clear that the defense is better with Williams on the field. The 49ers allow a 44.6% success rate without Williams on the field . When he has played this year, the opponent success rate is 29.8%. Opponents' yards per play is down from 5.1 to 3.3.
The numbers will normalize with more playing time. Still, he is clearly showing up and making a difference. San Francisco is going to need to play Williams more.
The rookie was in a minimal role to start the season. However, Dre Greenlaw being suspended has put him in a huge role over the past two weeks. Overall, the defense is better with Dugger. The success rate is down from 43.6% to 42% when Dugger plays. Meanwhile, the expected points allowed go from -0.014 to -0.107. The defense is more efficient when Dugger is on the field. The rookie should continue to get notable snaps.
Mustapha played sparingly early in the year. Then, he started the past two weeks with Marques Sigle injured. He has been a heat-seeking missile and a game-changer when he is on the field. The 49ers allow a positive EPA when Mustapha is not on the field. However, it is -0.201 when he is on the field. The 49ers' success rate drops from 47.9% without him to 36.3% with him on the field. Their yards per play are down from 5.1 to 4.6.
All three have not seen the field together much. However, the defense's success rate is just 33% allowed when they are playing. That is down from 47%. Lastly, their yards per play is down from 4.9 to 4.
Williams will play more. As Sigle and Greenlaw return to the lineup, it will be interesting to see how much Dugger and Mustapha can continue to mix in.
